Follow the distal ileum towards the caecum
concept: Taeniae coli converge on the base of the appendix - that is the surgical landmark

stem: A 32-year-old female underwent emergency caesarean section. At extubation she vomited and aspirated, requiring mechanical ventilation. Two hours later her arterial blood gas shows PaO2 of 48 mmHg. What is the best ventilator setting strategy?
opts: The minimum PEEP that allows at least 90% oxygen saturation
The PEEP that results in maximal compliance
The PEEP that results in an oxygen saturation of 90%
The maximum PEEP that results in a measurable change
concept: ARDS and acute hypoxaemic respiratory failure - use the lowest PEEP that achieves acceptable oxygenation

stem: A patient is scheduled for right-sided thoracoscopy and has a history of repeated pneumothoraces. X-ray shows one large emphysematous bulla on the right side. What is the best anaesthetic option?
opts: General anaesthesia with a single lumen tube
General anaesthesia with an endotracheal tube
General anaesthesia with a double lumen tube
concept: Thoracoscopy for bullectomy - one-lung ventilation requires a double lumen tube

stem: A 1-year-old male child is brought to clinic with swelling in the right groin and scrotum that has been present since birth, is gradually increasing, and becomes prominent on crying. What is the most appropriate operation?
concept: Congenital indirect inguinal hernia in an infant - herniotomy with high ligation of the sac

stem: A 37-year-old man presents with pain, swelling and deformity of the right wrist after a fall on an outstretched hand. On X-ray the distal fragment is displaced and angulated towards the dorsum. What is the diagnosis?
concept: Colles' fracture - extra-articular distal radius with dorsal displacement and angulation of the distal fragment

stem: A 55-year-old male presents in the outpatient department with difficulty in swallowing for one month, with lethargy and significant weight loss. What is the investigation of choice for diagnosis?
concept: Dysphagia with weight loss in an older adult - upper GI endoscopy with biopsy

stem: A 45-year-old male presents with difficulty in swallowing for one month, worse for liquids than solids, with no weight loss. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Dysphagia worse for liquids than solids - a motility disorder of the oesophagus rather than a mechanical obstruction

stem: A 65-year-old unconscious male is brought to the emergency room after a road traffic accident. His pulse is 130/min, blood pressure 70/40 mmHg and respiratory rate 20/min. He has signs of head injury. What type of shock is most likely?
concept: Tachycardia with hypotension after trauma = hypovolaemic shock from haemorrhage

stem: A 15-year-old girl is brought to hospital with bizarre movements of the upper limbs and mild jaundice. Her elder sister died at age 30 with similar complaints. She has hepatomegaly, bilirubin 4 mg/dl and raised alkaline phosphatase. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Wilson disease - young patient with chorea, liver disease, and a sibling with the same illness

stem: A 35-year-old female, with no known comorbidity, is planned for laparoscopic cholecystectomy. What is the most appropriate prophylactic antibiotic regimen?
opts: Several postoperative doses of a first generation cephalosporin
No antibiotic for a clean laparoscopic procedure
A single dose after the operation has begun
A single dose of a second generation cephalosporin before skin incision
concept: Clean laparoscopic surgery - a single prophylactic dose within 60 minutes before incision

stem: A 30-year-old male has bleeding per rectum, mostly on straining at stool. On proctoscopy, pea-sized engorged veins are seen inside the anal canal at the 3 and 11 o'clock positions. What is the most appropriate treatment?
concept: First and second degree internal haemorrhoids - conservative measures plus injection sclerotherapy

stem: A 30-year-old male has bleeding per rectum on straining. On examination, swollen engorged veins protrude outside the anus at 3, 7 and 11 o'clock and do not stay inside when gently pushed. What is the most appropriate treatment?
concept: Third degree haemorrhoids - prolapse requiring manual reduction; haemorrhoidectomy is definitive

stem: A 35-year-old male farmer presents with 24 hours of right leg pain and swelling after an injury with agricultural machinery. His temperature is 100 degrees F, pulse 120/min, blood pressure 75/45 mmHg, and there is crepitus in the wound. What is the causative organism?
concept: Post-traumatic crepitus, gas and myonecrosis within 24 hours = Clostridium perfringens gas gangrene

stem: A 35-year-old male comes to the surgical outpatient department four days after an open appendectomy with purulent discharge from the wound. The wound is gaping with foul-smelling discharge. What is the most likely pathogen?
concept: Wound infection with a putrid discharge after bowel surgery - the smell points to a gram-negative enteric organism

stem: A 30-year-old male presents to the emergency room 20 minutes after a motor vehicle accident with a pulse of 91/min and blood pressure 110/70 mmHg. There is a large untidy wound on the anterior aspect of the right thigh. The surgical resident plans to convert this into a tidy wound. Which factor necessitates this?
opts: Heavily ingrained dirt in the wound
Clean cut edges of the skin
concept: Debridement converts a contaminated, untidy wound into a clean wound

stem: A 27-year-old male underwent elective splenectomy. That night his pulse is 120/min, blood pressure 90/50 mmHg and urine output is less than 60 mL per hour. What is the most likely problem?
concept: Post-splenectomy night-time shock with oliguria - think bleeding until proved otherwise

stem: A 65-year-old male has had an emergency operation for a perforated duodenal ulcer. He has received a prolonged course of intravenous broad-spectrum antibiotics. On day 12 he develops watery diarrhoea with abdominal distension and fever. What is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Pseudomembranous colitis due to Clostridioides difficile
concept: Prolonged broad-spectrum antibiotics then watery diarrhoea with fever = Clostridioides difficile pseudomembranous colitis

stem: A 30-year-old male undergoes surgical resection of a colonic carcinoma. The tumour is found to involve the wall of the bowel up to but not through the muscularis propria. What is the correct staging?
concept: TNM staging of colorectal cancer - T1 invades submucosa, T2 invades muscularis propria, T3 invades through it into pericolorectal tissue

stem: A 55-year-old man is found to have a solitary, firm, non-tender thyroid nodule. Ultrasound shows a solid hypoechoic nodule with irregular margins and internal microcalcifications. What is the next best step in management?
concept: Suspicious thyroid nodule on ultrasound - fine needle aspiration is the first-line investigation

stem: A 45-year-old woman has had symptoms of gastro-oesophageal reflux for two years despite a proton pump inhibitor at standard dose. She has dysphagia and an endoscopy shows Barrett's oesophagus with low-grade dysplasia. What is the most appropriate management?
opts: Continue the proton pump inhibitor and repeat endoscopy in one year
Endoscopic ablation or mucosal resection with surveillance
concept: Barrett's oesophagus with dysplasia - endoscopic eradication therapy plus acid suppression and surveillance

stem: A 70-year-old man with a history of atrial fibrillation presents with acute severe abdominal pain out of proportion to the findings on examination, with a soft abdomen and no tenderness. He is hypotensive. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Pain out of proportion with a soft abdomen in an elderly patient with atrial fibrillation = acute mesenteric ischaemia

stem: A 36-year-old female presents with six months of weight gain, hirsutism, acne and hypertension. She also complains of polyuria and polydipsia. Which electrolyte abnormality is most likely to be present?
concept: Cushing's syndrome - hypokalaemia from mineralocorticoid activity of excess cortisol

stem: A 43-year-old barber complains of ill health, loss of weight, cough and expectoration of purulent sputum for six months. He has finger clubbing and bronchial breathing in the right upper zone. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Upper zone disease with clubbing and constitutional weight loss - pulmonary tuberculosis

stem: A 55-year-old smoker has cough and pain in the left upper limb with drooping of the upper eyelid. Chest X-ray shows haziness in the left apical region and erosion of the first rib. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Pancoast (superior sulcus) tumour - apical mass with first rib destruction, brachial plexus involvement and Horner syndrome

stem: A 50-year-old man presents with abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting and pyrexia 24 hours after attending a party. He was dehydrated, with blood pressure 100/70 mmHg and pulse 110/min. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Acute infective gastroenteritis from contaminated food - short incubation, fever and systemic upset point to Salmonella

stem: A 26-year-old woman was diagnosed with pulmonary tuberculosis and started on anti-tuberculous therapy. Which of the following is a complication associated with this therapy?
concept: Ethambutol toxicity - optic neuritis with loss of visual acuity and red-green colour blindness

stem: A 25-year-old lady on anti-tuberculosis treatment for three weeks develops jaundice. Her physician stops the drugs and plans to restart them carefully after the jaundice subsides. Which drug is most likely responsible?
concept: Pyrazinamide is the most hepatotoxic first-line anti-TB drug

stem: A 20-year-old male with one week of high-grade fever, a maculopapular rash on the trunk and bleeding from the gums has haemoglobin 10 g/dL, total leucocyte count 3,500 and platelets 8,000. IgM antibodies to dengue virus are positive. What is the most appropriate treatment?
concept: Dengue haemorrhagic fever - supportive care with fluid replacement; avoid platelet transfusion unless bleeding

stem: A 30-year-old sexually active male develops urethral discharge for the second time within a year. Gram stain of the discharge shows many white blood cells and kidney-bean shaped gram-negative diplococci within neutrophils. What is the treatment of choice?
concept: Gonococcal urethritis - intracellular gram-negative diplococci; treat gonorrhoea and cover coexisting Chlamydia

stem: A 36-year-old lady has been suffering from ulcerative colitis for eight years. She has three to four stools per day mixed with blood for the last two months, with no response to prednisolone and azathioprine. What is the most appropriate investigation?
concept: Steroid-refractory ulcerative colitis - colonoscopy with biopsies to assess extent and exclude dysplasia

stem: A 64-year-old man presents with episodes of diarrhoea and significant weight loss over five months, with bleeding per rectum twice. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Older adult with altered bowel habit, bleeding and weight loss - carcinoma of the colon

stem: A young army recruit is admitted on a July evening with loss of consciousness preceded by fits after outdoor exercise. His body temperature is 105 degrees F and the neck is supple. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Heat stroke - hyperpyrexia above 40 degrees C with central nervous system dysfunction after exertion in hot weather

stem: A 50-year-old man has had hypertension for six years and presents with palpitations and exertional chest pain. His pulse is 110/min and irregular, blood pressure 170/110 mmHg, with bilateral respiratory wheeze. Which antihypertensive is most appropriate?
concept: Rate and BP control together - atrial fibrillation with fast ventricular response on a background of hypertension

stem: A 49-year-old man with chronic renal failure develops joint pain and has had fractures on the slightest injury. What is the most likely cause of his renal osteodystrophy?
concept: Renal osteodystrophy - secondary hyperparathyroidism from low calcitriol and phosphate retention in chronic renal failure

stem: A 36-year-old lady presents with acute oliguric renal failure. Her ECG shows hyperkalaemia with predominant widening of the QRS complex. Which treatment is recommended immediately?
concept: Severe hyperkalaemia with ECG changes - intravenous calcium gluconate first to stabilise the myocardium

stem: A 12-year-old boy presents with a snake bite 12 hours ago, with drooping of the eyelids and froth at the mouth. He has bilateral ptosis and difficulty breathing. What immediate therapeutic measure is necessary to save his life?
concept: Post-synaptic neurotoxic snake bite - the paralysis is already established at 12 hours, so airway support, not antivenom, is life-saving

stem: A 13-year-old child suffers a skin infection caused by group A streptococci. A few weeks later he develops malaise, nausea, slight fever and smoky red urine. The serum ASO titre is 1:1024. What is the most likely outcome in this scenario?
concept: Acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis - usually self-limiting in children; hypertension is transient

stem: A 20-year-old female presents with lymphadenopathy. Histological examination of the lymph node showed granulomata. Definite diagnosis of tuberculosis in this case requires:
concept: Caseating granuloma - caseation necrosis is the histological hallmark that confirms tuberculosis; giant cells alone are not specific

stem: A 15-year-old girl reports to the medical outpatient department with a history of prolonged bleeding with trivial injuries since long. Family history is positive. Investigations reveal bleeding time 20 minutes, clotting time 8 minutes and platelet count 180,000 per microlitre. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Prolonged bleeding time with a normal platelet count and normal clotting time indicates a platelet function defect

stem: A 80-year-old woman was bed-ridden for six months. She died secondary to pulmonary thromboembolism. The most likely site of origin of the thrombus would be deep veins of the:
concept: Pulmonary thromboembolism - the deep veins of the calf are the usual site of origin of the thrombus

stem: A 45-year-old woman, a known diabetic, cut her finger while cooking. The wound healed later than usual. What is the most likely factor producing delayed healing in her?
concept: Delayed wound healing in a diabetic - infection is the commonest and most correctable cause

stem: A 65-year-old male presented with low-grade fever and productive cough for two weeks. His temperature is 100 degrees F and total white cell count is 11 x 10^9 with 85% neutrophils. Sputum culture grows an organism. What is the commonest bacterial cause of community-acquired pneumonia?
concept: Streptococcus pneumoniae is the commonest cause of community-acquired pneumonia; Klebsiella favours alcoholics and aspiration

stem: A 60-year-old man underwent right hemicolectomy two years ago. Recently he developed shortness of breath and right-sided chest pain. Clinically and radiologically he has a right pleural effusion. What is the most appropriate investigation to confirm the cause?
concept: New unilateral pleural effusion after resection of colonic carcinoma - pleural fluid cytology establishes the cause

stem: A 20-year-old female was diagnosed with ileocaecal tuberculosis. What is the best investigation to confirm the diagnosis?
concept: Ileocaecal tuberculosis - colonoscopy with biopsy of the ileocaecal valve showing caseating granulomas

stem: A young man with recurrent chest infections since childhood has chronic cough with copious foul-smelling sputum containing blood. Bronchiectasis is suspected. Which investigation confirms the diagnosis and defines its extent?
opts: High-resolution computed tomography of the chest
concept: Bronchiectasis - high-resolution CT is the diagnostic and extent-defining investigation

stem: A 35-year-old woman presents with palpitations, tremor, weight loss and intolerance to heat. Thyroid function shows a raised T4 and a suppressed TSH. Radioiodine uptake scan shows uniform diffuse uptake. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Graves' disease - diffuse uniform increased radioiodine uptake with raised T4 and suppressed TSH

stem: A 32-year-old woman has had diarrhoea for three weeks following a course of antibiotics for a urinary infection. She has abdominal cramping, fever and leucocytosis. Which organism is the most likely cause?
concept: Antibiotic-associated pseudomembranous colitis - Clostridioides difficile

stem: A 40-year-old woman presents with palpitations, weight loss and tremor. On examination there is a diffusely enlarged thyroid with a bruit and bilateral eye protrusion. Thyroid function shows raised T4 and suppressed TSH. What is the underlying mechanism?
concept: Graves' disease - thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulins activate the TSH receptor

stem: A 58-year-old man with a history of heavy smoking presents with haemoptysis, weight loss and a cavitary lesion in the right upper zone. Sputum cytology shows malignant cells. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
opts: CT of the chest with contrast and staging
Repeat sputum cytology in three months
concept: Lung cancer - CT of the chest for staging and tissue diagnosis; antituberculous treatment must not be started empirically

stem: A 70-year-old man presents with acute onset of right-sided weakness and slurred speech. Blood pressure is 210/110 mmHg. CT shows a right middle cerebral artery territory infarct. Which antihypertensive is most appropriate in the first hour?
opts: Lower blood pressure by about 15% only
Rapid reduction of blood pressure to a normal value
concept: Acute ischaemic stroke - permissive hypertension; lower BP by no more than about 15% in the first 24 hours

stem: A 35-year-old lady presents with vertigo on changing posture. What is the most probable cause?
concept: Vertigo provoked by changing posture - distinguish a peripheral vestibular disorder from postural hypotension

stem: A recently married young lady suddenly develops severe spasmodic pain in the right iliac fossa and is brought to the emergency department in a state of shock. The most likely cause is:
concept: Ectopic pregnancy - ruptured tubal pregnancy causing shock, with a positive pregnancy history

stem: If a person suffered a stab injury and air entered the intrapleural space, producing a pneumothorax, what is the most likely response for the lung?
opts: Expand outward and the chest wall springs inward
Collapse inward and the chest wall collapses inward
Collapse inward and the chest wall springs outward
Expand outward and the chest wall springs outward
concept: Pneumothorax - loss of negative intrapleural pressure causes the lung to collapse inward while the chest wall springs outward

stem: A 6-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department with laryngeal obstruction. The best site for a transverse incision for tracheostomy is between:
concept: Paediatric tracheostomy - trachea is short and narrow, so the incision is higher, between the 2nd and 3rd rings

stem: A patient was brought to hospital after a roadside accident. On examination he is pale with low blood pressure and has a fracture of the left 10th rib. Which organ is most likely to be injured?
concept: Splenic injury - a fractured left 10th rib is a classic marker of splenic laceration

stem: Following a severe automobile accident a 29-year-old woman is found to have an unstable hip joint. When asked to stand on the right leg with the left leg lifted, her pelvis sinks downward on the left side. Which muscle is most likely to be injured?
concept: Trendelenburg test - the abductors of the weight-bearing side hold the pelvis level, so a contralateral pelvic drop localises the injury to the standing limb

stem: While repairing a direct inguinal hernia, a surgeon should find the hernial sac:
opts: Lateral to the inferior epigastric artery
Medial to the inferior epigastric artery
concept: Direct inguinal hernia - the sac is MEDIAL to the inferior epigastric artery; indirect lies lateral

stem: A person was brought to the emergency department with a stab wound in the right flexor retinaculum. On exploration the median nerve was found to be severed. He is most likely to suffer loss of:
concept: Median nerve severed at the flexor retinaculum - thenar motor loss with preserved thenar skin sensation

stem: An 18-year-old married lady presents with pain in the right iliac fossa and vomiting in the emergency department. On examination there was tenderness in the right iliac fossa, fever and raised white cell count. Her last menstrual period was three months ago. The most likely site of the pathology is:
concept: Young woman with amenorrhoea and right iliac fossa pain - ectopic pregnancy must be excluded before appendicitis

stem: A 28-year-old piano player has a brain tumour affecting the left hemisphere. Which function is most likely to be affected?
opts: Fine finger movements of the hand
Ability to cope with large crowds when meeting new people
Ability to find her way around her home
concept: Left hemisphere lesion - loss of contralateral fine motor control and of language

stem: A patient with a peptic ulcer in the proximal first part of the duodenum develops severe haematemesis. The clinician suggests an embolisation procedure. The ideal vessel to be embolised is the:
concept: Duodenal ulcer bleeding from the gastroduodenal artery - the first part of the duodenum is supplied mainly by the gastroduodenal artery

stem: A young man reports an injury to the perineum during an automobile accident. His penile urethra is ruptured. Where is extravasated urine most likely to collect?
concept: Ruptured bulbar (spongy) penile urethra - urine extravasates into the superficial perineal pouch and scrotum

stem: A patient has a known peptic ulcer in the proximal duodenum and develops severe haematemesis. Which artery is the source of the bleeding most likely to be?
concept: Peptic ulcer in the first part of the duodenum bleeds from the gastroduodenal artery

stem: A 60-year-old man has a hoarse voice and difficulty swallowing for three months. Examination of the neck reveals a hard, fixed thyroid mass with enlarged cervical lymph nodes. Which investigation is most appropriate to establish the diagnosis?
opts: Ultrasound of the neck with guided fine needle aspiration
concept: Suspected thyroid carcinoma - ultrasound with ultrasound-guided fine needle aspiration is the diagnostic test

stem: A patient has a laceration of the radial side of the wrist after a fall on an outstretched hand. On testing, finger extension and wrist extension are preserved but the thumb is abducted weakly. Which nerve is most likely injured?
concept: Wrist injury with weak thumb abduction and preserved finger/wrist extension - posterior interosseous nerve

stem: A 34-year-old woman has a hard, irregular, mobile lump in the upper outer quadrant of the right breast of three months' duration. There is dimpling of the skin over the lump. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Breast carcinoma - hard irregular mobile lump with skin dimpling from Cooper's ligament involvement

stem: A 40-year-old man has severe pain in the right hypochondrium radiating to the right scapula, precipitated by a fatty meal. On examination he is febrile with a positive Murphy's sign. Which of the following is most likely to be found on ultrasound?
opts: Multiple gallstones in the gallbladder with wall thickening
A dilated common bile duct with stones
A hyperechoic lesion in the pancreatic head
concept: Acute cholecystitis - ultrasound shows gallstones, gallbladder wall thickening and pericholecystic fluid

stem: A 45-year-old man has sudden severe pain in the chest radiating to the left arm with sweating and nausea. Blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg. Which coronary artery is most likely occluded?
concept: Anterior wall MI with shock - the left anterior descending artery is the most commonly occluded and supplies the largest area

stem: A 70-year-old man has difficulty in initiating urination, a weak stream, dribbling and nocturia. On digital rectal examination the prostate is symmetrically enlarged, smooth and firm. Which drug class is the most appropriate first-line treatment?
concept: Benign prostatic hyperplasia - alpha-1 blockers relax prostatic and bladder neck smooth muscle as first-line

stem: A woman under stress notices that her salivary secretion has become thick and viscid, unlike the usual watery type. The adrenergic receptors most likely responsible are:
concept: Sympathetic stimulation of salivary glands - alpha receptors produce viscous protein-rich saliva, beta receptors produce watery secretion

stem: A 25-year-old athletic woman carries out heavy exercise. During the exercise, increased loss of body water occurs through:
concept: Exercising muscle generates heat dissipated mainly by evaporation of sweat

stem: In a patient having clasp-knife rigidity when the arm is passively flexed at the elbow, there is initial resistance to flexion followed by rapid flexion. The rapid flexion is due to relaxation of extensors resulting from stimulation of:
concept: Clasp-knife rigidity - Golgi tendon organ Ib afferent feedback causes sudden extensor relaxation

stem: An 8-year-old child has profuse bleeding after extraction of a deciduous tooth. After full investigation he is diagnosed as having classic haemophilia. Blood analysis would most likely show deficiency of:
concept: Classic haemophilia A - factor VIII deficiency; haemophilia B (Christmas disease) is factor IX

stem: A 40-year-old female presents with deep jaundice and bleeding gums. Her ultrasound shows bile duct obstruction due to a stone. If untreated, the most likely deficiency she can develop is of:
concept: Obstructive jaundice with fat malabsorption - fat-soluble vitamin K deficiency causes coagulopathy

stem: A patient receiving infusion of large amounts of dextrose in water would have inhibition of secretion of:
concept: Volume expansion from a large dextrose infusion suppresses antidiuretic hormone secretion

stem: A patient has hypoxia with low arterial PO2 and a haemoglobin concentration of 15 g/dL. The type of hypoxia he suffers from is:
concept: Hypoxic hypoxia - low arterial PO2 with normal haemoglobin, so the oxygen content of arterial blood is reduced

stem: In a man performing exercise, venous return from the legs is facilitated mainly by:
concept: The calf muscle pump - skeletal muscle contraction compresses veins, and venous valves make it a one-way pump

stem: Anaphylactic shock, when compared with hypovolaemic shock, most likely has:
opts: Heart rate much lower than normal
Total peripheral resistance greater than normal
concept: Anaphylaxis is distributive shock - reduced SVR with compensatory tachycardia and reduced venous return; hypovolaemia also reduces venous return

stem: A healthy 22-year-old medical student performs an exercise stress test. Which factor is most likely to DECREASE in her skeletal muscle during exercise?
concept: During exercise, arteriolar resistance in skeletal muscle falls because local metabolites override sympathetic tone

stem: A 12-year-old child is admitted with recent onset of widespread purpura. Laboratory investigations reveal an abnormality accounting for the bleeding problem. The most likely finding will be:
concept: Non-thrombocytopenic purpura - platelet number versus platelet function is the discriminator, and a low count is the far commoner cause in a child

stem: A 50-year-old male in the emergency department has central chest pain radiating to both arms. His central venous pressure is elevated, the neck veins are distended, the skin is cold and the blood pressure is 95/60 mmHg. Which type of shock is this?
concept: Cardiogenic shock - low output with raised CVP and compensatory high systemic vascular resistance

stem: A 40-year-old female has a heart rate of 100/min, a blood pressure of 95/60 mmHg, and warm extremities. Which of the following patterns best fits her haemodynamic state?
opts: Low cardiac output, low systemic vascular resistance
High cardiac output, low systemic vascular resistance
High cardiac output, high systemic vascular resistance
Low cardiac output, high systemic vascular resistance
concept: Warm shock - low systemic vascular resistance with a relatively high or normal cardiac output, as in early sepsis

stem: An 80-year-old woman has an impaired ability to concentrate urine despite adequate intake of water and a normal blood pressure. Secretion of which hormone is most likely to be impaired?
concept: Concentrating urine depends on ADH acting on the collecting ducts via aquaporin-2 insertion

stem: A 35-year-old man with a high serum potassium level is given a drug that slows the heart rate without reducing the serum potassium. Which of the following is the most likely effect of this drug on the resting membrane potential of cardiac muscle?
opts: Decreases potassium efflux and prolongs the action potential
Has no effect on the resting membrane potential
concept: Hyperkalaemia raises the resting membrane potential by reducing K+ efflux, making the fast sodium channels unavailable and widening the QRS

stem: A 21-year-old woman cut her forearm after a fall. The next day the wound had decreased slightly in size. Which tissue is most probably responsible for this wound contraction?
concept: Wound contraction by myofibroblasts - contractile fibroblasts, not skeletal muscle, close a wound by pulling its edges together

stem: A child is diagnosed as a true hermaphrodite. What is the most likely genotype?
concept: True hermaphroditism (ovotesticular DSD) - an XX individual carrying a Y-chromosome segment that directs testicular development alongside ovarian tissue

stem: A 65-year-old male presented with low-grade fever and productive cough for two weeks. His temperature is 100 degrees F and the total white cell count is 11 x 10^9 with 85% neutrophils. Sputum culture grows a gram-positive lancet-shaped diplococcus. What is the causative organism?
concept: Gram-positive lancet-shaped diplococci with a capsule - Streptococcus pneumoniae

stem: An 18-year-old boy was brought to the emergency room complaining of severe abdominal pain for the last two hours, having attended his college annual dinner. His temperature is 100 degrees F with a mild tachycardia. The causative bacterium is most likely:
concept: Acute food poisoning after a banquet - Staphylococcus aureus causes the shortest incubation

stem: A 12-year-old child presents with a skin infection caused by group A streptococci. A few weeks later he develops malaise, nausea, slight fever and smoky red urine. Serum ASO titre is 1:1024. The most likely outcome is:
concept: Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis after skin infection - self-limiting, with transient hypertension

stem: A 30-year-old woman presents with fever, burning micturition and increased urinary frequency for two days. Urinalysis shows many white cells and a trace of protein. What is the commonest causative organism?
concept: Acute uncomplicated cystitis in women - E. coli in 80-90%

stem: A 55-year-old female in the emergency department has severe generalised abdominal pain for six hours with a history of gallstones for which she had been advised surgery. She is tachycardic with a soft, distended abdomen. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Acute biliary pancreatitis - gallstone obstruction of the pancreatic outflow in a woman with known gallstones

stem: A 46-year-old person is admitted with acute abdominal pain and migratory thrombophlebitis. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Migratory thrombophlebitis with acute abdominal pain - acute pancreatitis

stem: A 35-year-old man has chronic diarrhoea with steatorrhoea after a resection of a segment of small bowel. Which of the following is the most likely consequence?
concept: Ileal resection - bile salt malabsorption, fat-soluble vitamin loss and B12 deficiency

stem: A 45-year-old alcoholic male presents with severe abdominal pain radiating to the back for 12 hours. On examination the abdomen is soft and distended with epigastric tenderness. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Acute pancreatitis - alcoholic, epigastric pain radiating to the back, soft abdomen

stem: A 50-year-old woman has a firm, painful lump in the breast at the site of a previous trauma three months ago. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Fat necrosis after breast trauma - a carcinoma mimic

stem: A 40-year-old woman presents with abdominal pain for 12 hours, nausea and vomiting, and is febrile with right upper quadrant tenderness. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Acute cholecystitis - right upper quadrant pain with fever and Murphy's sign

stem: A 27-year-old woman has a 3 cm mobile lump in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast. On ultrasound it is a well-defined, oval, hypoechoic mass with thin radiating septations. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Fibroadenoma - well-defined oval hypoechoic mass with radiating septations in a young woman

stem: A 34-year-old female is found to have raised serum conjugated bilirubin with an alkaline phosphatase that is disproportionately raised. Ultrasound shows dilatation of the intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Conjugated hyperbilirubinaemia with raised ALP and dilated ducts - cholestasis, needing imaging to find the cause

stem: A 4-month-old boy has a swelling in the right groin that has been present since birth, becomes prominent on crying and can be reduced. Ultrasound shows bowel within the inguinal canal. What is the most likely underlying embryological defect?
opts: Failure of fusion of the urethral folds
Failure of obliteration of the processus vaginalis
Failure of regression of the thyroglossal duct
Failure of descent of the testes
concept: Congenital indirect inguinal hernia - failure of the processus vaginalis to obliterate

stem: A 45-year-old woman has had menorrhagia and a pelvic mass for two years. Histology of the specimen shows glands and stroma resembling endometrium within the myometrium. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Adenomyosis - endometrial glands and stroma within the myometrium, diffusely enlarged boggy uterus

stem: A 60-year-old woman has a painless, progressively enlarging, irregular cervical mass. Biopsy shows sheets of malignant squamous cells forming keratin pearls. What is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix
concept: Squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix - keratin pearls, HPV 16 and 18, screening with Pap smear

stem: A 25-year-old woman has had menorrhagia, dysmenorrhoea and a uniformly enlarged boggy tender uterus. Histology after hysterectomy shows endometrial glands and stroma within the myometrium. Which hormone is used in the medical treatment of her condition?
concept: Adenomyosis treated by progesterone-suppressing agents - levonorgestrel intrauterine system, progestogens, GnRH analogues

stem: A 65-year-old man has a hard, irregular, non-tender prostate nodule on digital rectal examination with a raised prostate specific antigen of 40 ng/mL. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
opts: Repeat the PSA in three months
concept: Suspected prostate carcinoma - ultrasound-guided core biopsy for histological confirmation

stem: A 20-year-old girl presents with irregular menstrual cycles for one year followed by three months of amenorrhoea. She is obese with oily skin and mild hirsutism over the upper lip and chin. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: PCOS - oligomenorrhoea with obesity, hirsutism, acne and polycystic ovaries

stem: A 35-year-old third gravida is seen in antenatal clinic with a history of two previous stillbirths at home with large babies. Her one-hour 50 g glucose challenge test shows a one-hour blood sugar of 140 mg/dL. What is the most appropriate investigation next?
opts: A full oral glucose tolerance test
concept: Glucose challenge test of 50 g - a 1-hour value of 140 mg/dL needs the diagnostic 100 g oral glucose tolerance test

stem: A 28-year-old G3P2 is in labour at 38 weeks and has been in labour for six hours. Vaginal examination reveals full cervical dilatation with the head in mentoposterior position at station -1. The cardiotocograph is reactive. What is the most appropriate management at this stage?
opts: Allow labour to continue with reassessment
concept: Prolonged second stage with a mentoposterior head - operative delivery by caesarean

stem: A 25-year-old housewife complains of extremely painful but regular periods with normal flow. She also has deep dyspareunia and has not conceived in five years of marriage. On pelvic examination there is right-sided adnexal tenderness. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Severe cyclical dysmenorrhoea with deep dyspareunia and infertility is endometriosis

stem: A 30-year-old woman G2P1 presented at 28 weeks of amenorrhoea with labour pain and is in active labour. She has a history of foul-smelling, milky vaginal discharge. What is the most likely cause of preterm labour?
concept: Preterm labour with a foul-smelling thin grey discharge indicates bacterial vaginosis

stem: A 32-year-old lady was admitted with abruptio placentae at 8 a.m. and delivered after 24 hours. She is bleeding profusely although the uterus is well contracted and there is no vaginal tear. Blood report shows haemoglobin 7 g/dL and platelets 80,000. What is the most appropriate transfusion?
concept: Massive obstetric haemorrhage with anaemia and thrombocytopenia - whole blood restores red cells and clotting factors together

stem: A 24-year-old primigravida with a BMI of 16 has been hospitalised for two weeks with recurrent bleeding per vaginum. She is 33 weeks pregnant and has diagnosed placenta previa type IV. On examination she is suspected to have developed deep vein thrombosis. Which is the most important risk factor?
concept: DVT risk in pregnancy - prolonged immobilisation from bleeding and hospitalisation dominates here

stem: A 14-year-old girl presents with heavy, prolonged, irregular menstrual bleeding. She is thin built and pale. Abdominal examination is normal. What is the most suitable investigation?
concept: Adolescent menorrhagia - pelvic ultrasound assesses the endometrium and excludes structural causes

stem: A 26-year-old primigravida at 34 weeks of gestation presents with bleeding per vaginum. She is haemodynamically stable. The uterine height corresponds with gestational age and the lie is longitudinal. Speculum examination shows no cervical lesion and the membranes are intact. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Painless third-trimester bleeding with a normal lie and intact membranes - placenta previa

stem: A 24-year-old woman at term has an epidural in place for labour analgesia. Two days after the epidural catheter is removed she develops a severe headache that is worse on sitting and relieved by lying down. What is the most appropriate next step?
opts: Bed rest, hydration and intravenous caffeine
concept: Post-dural-puncture headache - the positional character distinguishes it from every other headache after labour analgesia

stem: A 15-year-old boy with fever, malaise, cough and rash is diagnosed as having measles. What is the most frequent immediate complication of measles?
concept: Measles - otitis media and bronchopneumonia are the commonest complications; SSPE is the late one

stem: A 1-year-old boy woke at 4 a.m. with a loud respiratory noise. On examination in the emergency room he is cyanosed, drooling saliva from the mouth and has an inspiratory stridor. What is the best management option?
opts: His throat should be examined to look for a foreign body
Suctioning and oxygen therapy will improve him
He should be admitted to a paediatric intensive care unit
His airway should be assessed while maintaining oxygenation and avoiding agitation
concept: Acute upper airway obstruction - keep the child calm, oxygen, and secure the airway without forcing examination

stem: A 2-year-old child has a seven-day history of cough with low-grade fever, watery eyes and nose, followed by paroxysmal coughing that exhausts the child. What is the best treatment?
concept: Whooping cough in a child - a macrolide is first-line because it penetrates the respiratory tract and has activity against Bordetella pertussis

stem: A 5-year-old child is bitten on the hand by a neighbour's dog while the dog was eating. The dog has been vaccinated regularly. Which steps are needed for rabies prophylaxis?
opts: Kill the dog and examine the brain
concept: Rabies post-exposure prophylaxis for a category III bite - vaccine plus wound infiltration with human rabies immunoglobulin

stem: A 3-year-old boy is brought to the outpatient department with developmental delay. On examination he has a wide-open fontanelle, a small umbilical hernia and short stature. No bony abnormalities are seen. What is the most appropriate investigation?
opts: Serum TSH and free T4 levels
concept: Congenital hypothyroidism - developmental delay with wide-open fontanelle, umbilical hernia and short stature

stem: A 2-year-old child comes with a history of cough for seven days. On examination the respiratory rate is 70 breaths per minute, there is dull percussion note on the right side of the chest and bronchial breath sounds are heard. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Dull percussion with bronchial breath sounds - lung consolidation, not pleural effusion

stem: A 3-year-old mother of a 2-month-old infant presents concerned that her baby is not feeding well and has fewer wet nappies. Which of the following is the most reliable indicator that the infant is receiving adequate milk?
concept: Adequate breast milk intake is confirmed by weight gain - the most reliable indicator

stem: A 3-year-old child is brought to the outpatient department with a 10-day history of loose stools. On examination the child is afebrile with sunken eyes and skin pinch returning normally. What is your diagnosis according to IMNCI classification?
opts: Chronic watery diarrhoea with some dehydration
Acute watery diarrhoea with some dehydration
Acute watery diarrhoea with no dehydration
concept: IMNCI classification - duration determines acute versus persistent, and hydration status is graded separately

stem: A newborn has a heart murmur heard in the first week of life. Echocardiography shows a defect in the membranous interventricular septum. Which of the following shunt directions is most likely?
concept: Ventricular septal defect - left-to-right shunt because left ventricular pressure exceeds right

stem: A 55-year-old man has recurrent episodes of confusion and sweating during fasting or after exercise. A supervised 72-hour fast is stopped at 14 hours when he becomes symptomatic with a plasma glucose of 38 mg/dL. Serum insulin is 22 microU/mL (high) and C-peptide is 3.1 ng/mL (high); a sulfonylurea screen is negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Factitious hypoglycaemia from surreptitious insulin injection
concept: Insulinoma — endogenous hyperinsulinaemia proven by high C-peptide during supervised fasting

stem: A 42-year-old woman has a 1-week history of painful neck swelling, fever and palpitations after an upper respiratory infection. Free T4 is raised, TSH is suppressed, and 24-hour radioiodine uptake is 2%. Which mechanism best explains the thyrotoxicosis?
opts: TSH-receptor antibody stimulation of the thyroid (Graves disease)
Viral thyroiditis with follicular destruction releasing preformed hormone (destructive thyrotoxicosis)
An autonomous adenoma secreting excess T4
Acute suppurative infection of the gland with abscess formation
concept: Subacute thyroiditis — destructive thyrotoxicosis with low radioiodine uptake

stem: A 52-year-old woman is evaluated for a 1.8 cm right thyroid nodule. Which ultrasound feature is LEAST suggestive of thyroid malignancy?
opts: A smooth complete halo with homogeneous isoechoic texture
concept: Thyroid nodule — sonographic features of malignancy (negative stem)

stem: A 25-year-old woman has recurrent calcium stones, hypokalaemia and a persistent normal anion gap metabolic acidosis with a normal GFR. Which finding would argue AGAINST distal (type 1) renal tubular acidosis as the diagnosis?
opts: A urine pH that falls to 5.0 during systemic acidaemia
concept: Distal (type 1) RTA — inability to acidify urine (negative stem)

stem: A 64-year-old hypertensive smoker with recurrent 'flash' pulmonary oedema starts an ACE inhibitor and her creatinine rises from 1.2 to 2.3 mg/dL within 5 days. Bilateral renal artery stenosis is suspected. Which mechanism best explains the creatinine rise?
opts: Afferent arteriolar constriction by blockade of angiotensin II
Mesangial cell contraction reducing the filtration surface
Efferent arteriolar dilation abolishing glomerular filtration pressure in the stenotic kidneys
Aldosterone suppression causing renal salt wasting
concept: Renal artery stenosis — ACE inhibitor efferent arteriolar vasodilation (mechanism)

stem: A 60-year-old man with cirrhosis and ascites develops fever and abdominal pain. Paracentesis yields cloudy fluid with a polymorphonuclear (PMN) count of 450 cells/mm3; the bacterial culture is reported negative at 48 hours. What is the most appropriate treatment?
opts: Observation with repeat paracentesis in 48 hours
concept: Culture-negative neutrocytic ascites — treated exactly as SBP

stem: A 68-year-old woman develops profuse watery diarrhoea 7 days after a course of clindamycin. Sigmoidoscopy shows yellow-white adherent plaques. Which intervention is LEAST appropriate?
concept: C. difficile colitis — loperamide contraindicated (negative stem)

stem: A 64-year-old man presents with back pain, pathological vertebral fractures, anaemia and creatinine 2.1 mg/dL. Serum calcium is 11.5 mg/dL. Serum protein electrophoresis shows NO M-spike, but serum free light chains are markedly elevated and urine contains Bence Jones protein. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Light-chain (Bence Jones) multiple myeloma — CRAB features without an M-spike on SPEP

stem: A 59-year-old man presents 90 minutes after onset of acute left hemiparesis (NIHSS 12). His BP is 205/118 mmHg. IV labetalol lowers it to 184/108 mmHg. What is the most appropriate next step?
opts: Continue lowering BP to below 120/80 before thrombolysis
Delay thrombolysis for 24 hours of blood pressure control
concept: IV thrombolysis — BP threshold of 185/110 mmHg

stem: A 58-year-old diabetic man develops acute painful right-sided ptosis, diplopia and a 'down and out' eye. The right pupil is initially spared and briskly reactive. Two days later the pupil becomes dilated and non-reactive. What is the most appropriate next step?
opts: Reassure that diabetic third nerve palsy is benign and self-limiting
Urgent CT angiography to exclude a posterior communicating artery aneurysm
Start corticosteroids for presumed giant cell arteritis
Outpatient MRI in 6 weeks with observation
concept: CN III palsy — conversion from pupil-sparing to blown pupil = aneurysm until proven otherwise

stem: A 30-year-old man with crush injury and rhabdomyolysis has peaked T waves and a widened QRS complex. IV calcium gluconate is given. Which statement best describes how calcium gluconate acts in hyperkalaemia?
opts: Shifts potassium into cells via Na-K-ATPase stimulation
Binds serum potassium and excretes it renally as a complex
Stimulates aldosterone to increase renal potassium secretion
Stabilises the myocardial cell membrane against potassium-induced arrhythmia without changing the serum potassium
concept: Hyperkalaemia — mechanism of IV calcium (membrane stabilisation)

stem: A 42-year-old man sustains a contact burn to the forearm. The skin is waxy-white and dry, painless to pinprick, with visible thrombosed vessels and no capillary refill. What is the most likely burn depth?
concept: Burn depth — full-thickness burn recognition

stem: A 55-year-old man presents with a new left-sided varicocele that does NOT decompress when he lies down, together with microscopic haematuria. CT shows a left renal mass extending into the renal vein. What is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Renal cell carcinoma with renal vein thrombosis
Testicular germ cell tumour with retroperitoneal nodes
concept: Renal cell carcinoma — atypical presentation with an acute left varicocele

stem: A 38-year-old woman with Crohn disease who had extensive ileal resection develops recurrent calcium oxalate renal stones. Which mechanism best explains stone formation?
opts: Primary hyperoxaluria with hepatic oxalate overproduction
Chronic metabolic acidosis reducing urinary citrate
Hyperuricosuria with urate crystals nidating oxalate stones
Fat malabsorption binding calcium so unbound oxalate is absorbed in the colon (enteric hyperoxaluria)
concept: Enteric hyperoxaluria — mechanism of calcium oxalate stones after ileal resection

stem: A 28-year-old man with a C5 spinal cord injury suddenly develops severe headache, flushing, profuse sweating and a blood pressure of 210/110 mmHg. What is the FIRST step in management?
opts: Lay the patient flat with legs elevated
Sit the patient up, loosen tight clothing, and check and drain the urinary catheter
concept: Autonomic dysreflexia — initial management prioritisation

stem: A 79-year-old thin woman presents with 48 hours of colicky pain, vomiting and distension. There is no groin lump and she has no Howship-Romberg sign (no medial thigh pain). CT shows a right obturator hernia with proximal small-bowel dilation and no other cause of obstruction. What is the most appropriate management?
opts: Nasogastric decompression and observation for 24 hours
Urgent surgery to reduce and repair the obturator hernia
Discharge home with laxatives and review in 1 week
concept: Obturator hernia — obstruction confirmed on CT even without the Howship-Romberg sign

stem: A 74-year-old man, 4 days after total hip replacement, develops progressive abdominal distension without a mechanical obstruction on CT (acute colonic pseudo-obstruction). His caecal diameter is now 13 cm, and neostigmine plus two colonoscopic decompressions have failed to improve him. What is the most appropriate next step?
opts: Further colonoscopic decompression with a decompression tube
Surgical decompression (caecostomy or resection, with or without a stoma)
concept: Acute colonic pseudo-obstruction — indications for surgery (caecal diameter and failed decompression)

stem: A 52-year-old woman develops progressive stridor and respiratory distress 10 hours after total thyroidectomy. Her voice is only mildly weak but the stridor is severe. Laryngoscopy shows both vocal cords fixed in the paramedian position. What is the most appropriate management?
opts: Urgent intubation or tracheostomy for bilateral recurrent laryngeal nerve injury
Observation with voice rest and reassurance
Bedside opening of the wound for presumed haematoma
concept: Bilateral RLN injury — airway obstruction despite a nearly normal voice

stem: A 54-year-old woman who had a tracheostomy 3 weeks ago develops sudden, brisk, bright-red bleeding from the tracheostomy site. She is becoming hypotensive. What is the FIRST step in emergency management?
opts: Overinflate the tracheostomy cuff (and apply digital pressure through the stoma if needed) then prepare for urgent surgery
Pack the oropharynx with gauze swabs
Give IV tranexamic acid and observe
concept: Tracheo-innominate artery fistula — initial tamponade manoeuvre

stem: A 30-year-old G2P1 at 34 weeks has sudden severe constant abdominal pain. The uterus is tense and woody. There is NO vaginal bleeding. Ultrasound confirms intrauterine fetal demise. She is haemodynamically stable with a normal coagulation screen. What is the most appropriate management?
opts: Expectant management with delivery at 36 weeks
Vaginal delivery with serial monitoring of coagulation status
concept: Concealed placental abruption — vaginal delivery despite fetal demise

stem: During intrapartum monitoring, the CTG shows a smooth, regular sine-wave pattern at 130 bpm with absent beat-to-beat variability. Which cause is LEAST likely to produce this pattern?
opts: Severe fetal anaemia from Rh isoimmunisation
Umbilical cord compression with variable decelerations
concept: Sinusoidal CTG — causes (negative stem)

stem: A 2-year-old boy has had 7 days of fever with cracked lips, a strawberry tongue, a 1.5 cm cervical lymph node and swelling of his hands and feet. Which finding would be LEAST consistent with Kawasaki disease?
opts: A polymorphous rash on the trunk
Periungual desquamation in the second week
Purulent exudative conjunctivitis with a positive bacterial conjunctival culture
concept: Kawasaki disease — diagnostic criteria (negative stem)

stem: A 6-year-old girl is found to have breast buds. Over 12 months of follow-up there has been no progression, no pubic hair, no growth spurt, and her bone age matches her chronological age. What is the most appropriate management?
opts: Reassurance and continued observation for benign premature thelarche
GnRH analogue therapy after MRI to exclude a CNS cause
concept: Premature thelarche vs central precocious puberty — bone age and progression as discriminators

stem: An 82-year-old woman has rapid central vision loss with distortion. OCT shows subretinal fluid and a choroidal neovascular membrane under the macula. Why are intravitreal anti-VEGF agents the correct treatment?
opts: They treat the bacterial infection responsible for the exudation
They replace the antioxidant vitamins deficient in dry AMD
They directly seal the leaking vessels with laser photocoagulation
They neutralise VEGF-A, the growth factor driving choroidal neovascularisation and leakage
concept: Wet AMD — mechanism of anti-VEGF therapy

stem: A 66-year-old man with poorly controlled diabetes has had 3 weeks of worsening right ear pain. Otoscopy shows granulation tissue at the bony-cartilaginous junction, and he has developed a right facial palsy. Which management is LEAST appropriate?
opts: ENT referral with careful aural toilet and biopsy
concept: Malignant (necrotising) otitis externa — topical drops are insufficient (negative stem)

stem: A 12-year-old girl develops migratory polyarthritis, chorea and a new mitral regurgitation murmur 3 weeks after a streptococcal sore throat. Which mechanism best explains the cardiac injury in acute rheumatic fever?
opts: Direct bacterial invasion of the myocardium and valves
Type III immune-complex deposition restricted to the valve cusps
Molecular mimicry between streptococcal M-protein and host tissue antigens causing cross-reactive (Type II) antibody-mediated damage
Toxin-mediated superantigen injury of the conduction system
concept: Rheumatic fever — molecular mimicry and cross-reactive autoimmunity

stem: A 58-year-old man with poorly controlled diabetes has a necrotic, swollen, foul-smelling foot. The tissues are crepitant, Gram stain shows Gram-positive bacilli, and MRI shows gas tracking within muscle. What is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Wet gangrene from venous occlusion alone
Necrotising fasciitis due to group A streptococcus
concept: Gas gangrene — clostridial myonecrosis with crepitus and Gram-positive bacilli

stem: A 45-year-old diabetic man develops acute painful right ptosis and diplopia with the eye deviated 'down and out'. The right pupil is completely spared and briskly reactive. Which feature makes a posterior communicating artery aneurysm LESS likely?
opts: Complete pupil-sparing with a briskly reactive pupil
The 'down and out' position of the eye
concept: CN III palsy — pupil-sparing as the discriminator away from aneurysm

stem: A 30-year-old man has a 'cape'-like loss of pain and temperature over both shoulders and upper arms, with preserved light touch, plus wasting of the small hand muscles. Which mechanism best explains the dissociated sensory loss?
opts: A central cervical syrinx interrupting the pain and temperature fibres as they cross in the anterior white commissure
Hemisection of the cord (Brown-Sequard syndrome) interrupting one spinothalamic tract
Degeneration of the dorsal columns (posterior funiculi)
Occlusion of the anterior spinal artery at the cervical level
concept: Syringomyelia — mechanism of dissociated sensory loss (central crossing fibres)

stem: A 55-year-old man develops sudden dyspnoea and pleuritic chest pain 10 days after knee surgery. V/Q scanning shows multiple segmental regions that are ventilated but not perfused. His arterial PaCO2 is 33 mmHg (low). Which mechanism best explains the LOW PaCO2?
opts: Compensatory hyperventilation through the remaining patent vessels, keeping PaCO2 low despite increased alveolar dead space
Diffusion limitation across a thickened alveolar-capillary membrane
Right-to-left shunt causing carbon dioxide trapping
concept: Pulmonary embolism — dead space with compensatory hyperventilation (low PaCO2)

stem: A 54-year-old woman with myasthenia gravis on pyridostigmine develops urosepsis. Which antibiotic is LEAST appropriate for her?
concept: Drugs that worsen myasthenia gravis — aminoglycoside neuromuscular blockade (negative stem)

stem: A 64-year-old man who has taken amiodarone for 14 months develops cough and dyspnoea. Which finding would point AWAY from amiodarone pulmonary toxicity and TOWARD bacterial pneumonia?
opts: Progressive exertional dyspnoea over several weeks with a dry cough
Bilateral interstitial infiltrates on chest radiography
Acute fever with purulent sputum and a lobar consolidation on chest radiography
concept: Amiodarone pulmonary toxicity vs pneumonia — clinical differentiation (negative stem)

stem: A 6-month-old infant has hepatomegaly, fasting hypoglycaemia, lactic acidosis, hyperuricaemia and hyperlipidaemia due to glucose-6-phosphatase deficiency (von Gierke disease). Which metabolic finding is LEAST expected?
concept: Von Gierke disease — metabolic profile (negative stem)

stem: A health authority is considering a new population screening programme. Which condition is NOT suitable for screening?
opts: A common cancer with a long detectable preclinical phase and effective treatment at an early stage
A rapidly fatal cancer for which no effective treatment exists at any stage
A condition for which a valid, acceptable screening test exists
A condition where treating early changes the outcome compared with treating late
concept: Principles of screening — unsuitable target (negative stem)

stem: A body is found dead with intense cherry-red postmortem lividity and a bitter-almond odour from the stomach contents. Which statement correctly explains the cherry-red colour in cyanide poisoning?
opts: Cyanide inhibits cytochrome oxidase, so tissues cannot consume oxygen and venous blood remains oxygenated, appearing cherry-red
Cyanide converts haemoglobin to carboxyhaemoglobin, which is cherry-red
Cyanide converts haemoglobin to methaemoglobin, which is chocolate-brown
Cyanide causes venous congestion with deoxygenated blood, reddening the skin
concept: Cyanide poisoning — mechanism of cherry-red lividity (cytochrome oxidase blockade)

stem: A 64-year-old man with persistent atrial fibrillation has taken amiodarone 200 mg daily for 18 months. Over 6 weeks he develops a dry cough, weight loss, and progressive exertional dyspnoea. He is afebrile, with fine crackles and no wheeze. Chest X-ray shows bilateral interstitial and patchy alveolar infiltrates with a normal heart size, and SpO2 is 90% on room air. Which diagnosis and action is most appropriate?
opts: Heart failure - increase the diuretic dose
Amiodarone pulmonary toxicity - stop the drug and arrange further evaluation
concept: Amiodarone pulmonary toxicity - dose- and duration-dependent interstitial pneumonitis; stop the drug

stem: A 74-year-old woman with severe aortic stenosis has three episodes of painless bright-red bleeding per rectum over a year, each requiring transfusion, with iron-deficiency anaemia. Colonoscopy has been normal twice, and a CT angiogram during a bleed shows no active bleeding. Which diagnosis best explains the recurrent transfusion-dependent bleeding?
concept: Angiodysplasia - right-colon vascular ectasia (Heyde syndrome with aortic stenosis); subtle lesions missed on colonoscopy

stem: A 65-year-old woman develops profuse watery diarrhoea 8 days after a course of clindamycin; sigmoidoscopy shows yellow-white adherent plaques. While arranging stool testing for C. difficile toxin, which of the following is CONTRAINDICATED because it can precipitate toxic megacolon?
concept: Pseudomembranous colitis - C. difficile: loperamide is contraindicated (toxic megacolon); oral vancomycin is treatment

stem: A 58-year-old woman who has taken omeprazole for 8 months presents with a 2-week history of low-grade fever, flank pain, and a rash; creatinine has risen from 0.9 to 3.1 mg/dL. Urine shows sterile pyuria with WBC and granular casts; blood shows eosinophilia. Which single diagnosis best explains the pattern?
concept: Acute interstitial nephritis - drug hypersensitivity (PPI), fever/rash, eosinophilia, WBC casts

stem: A 62-year-old diabetic man on an ACE inhibitor has a normal anion-gap metabolic acidosis (HCO3 16 mmol/L) with K+ 5.9 mmol/L. Urine pH is 5.0 - the distal tubule can acidify urine normally. Which mechanism best explains the hyperkalaemic acidosis?
opts: Hypoaldosteronism with impaired distal K+ (and H+) secretion - type 4 RTA
concept: Type 4 RTA - hyperkalaemic, normal AG acidosis with PRESERVED urine acidification (aldosterone defect)

stem: A 50-year-old man with 14 years of poorly controlled type 2 diabetes has 3 weeks of progressive visual blurring, then sudden loss of vision in the right eye with floaters. Fundoscopy shows neovascularisation at the disc, vitreous haemorrhage, and fibrous proliferation. What is the most urgent intervention?
opts: Panretinal photocoagulation (laser) with urgent ophthalmology review
concept: Proliferative diabetic retinopathy - neovascularisation and vitreous haemorrhage -> urgent panretinal photocoagulation

stem: A 65-year-old diabetic woman with long-term poor control presents with rigors, right flank pain, and vomiting. BP 90/60 mmHg, WCC 28,000, glucose 420 mg/dL. CT shows gas within the renal parenchyma AND the perinephric space, with destruction of the renal architecture. Urine grows E. coli. Which description and management is correct?
opts: Renal calculus with no infection - analgesia
Emphysematous pyelonephritis - emergency drainage with IV antibiotics
concept: Emphysematous pyelonephritis - gas-forming necrotising renal infection in diabetes; emergency drainage

stem: A 63-year-old woman presents with 4 weeks of pallor, gum swelling, bruising, and a new right-sided facial nerve palsy. Blood shows WBC 48,000 with 70% blasts containing Auer rods; myeloperoxidase (MPO) is strongly positive and non-specific esterase is positive. Which leukaemia is most likely?
concept: Acute myeloid leukaemia - Auer rods, MPO positivity, gum and cranial-nerve infiltration (monocytic M4/M5)

stem: A 34-year-old G2P1 at 36 weeks has placental abruption with fetal demise. Two hours later she oozes from venepuncture sites and has gum bleeding. PT 29 s, aPTT 65 s, fibrinogen 90 mg/dL, platelets 45,000, D-dimer markedly elevated. Which description and treatment is correct?
opts: Disseminated intravascular coagulation - treat the cause and support with blood products
Vitamin K deficiency - give vitamin K
concept: DIC - consumption coagulopathy after obstetric tissue-factor release; treat the cause + supportive products

stem: A 70-year-old man with cirrhosis and a normal clotting profile continues to seize 10 minutes after a benzodiazepine for status epilepticus. Which second-line agent is the LEAST suitable choice in this patient?
concept: Status epilepticus in hepatic impairment - valproate is least suitable (hepatic metabolism + hepatotoxicity); levetiracetam preferred

stem: A 32-year-old man with coeliac disease confirmed on duodenal biopsy (villous atrophy, positive transglutaminase antibodies) develops intensely pruritic grouped vesicles on his elbows, knees, and buttocks; skin biopsy shows granular IgA in the dermal papillae. Which medication most rapidly controls the skin lesions?
concept: Dermatitis herpetiformis - dapsone rapidly controls the rash; gluten-free diet is the long-term treatment

stem: A 70-year-old man has fluctuating cognition, vivid formed visual hallucinations of small people, and mild parkinsonism. During a hospital admission he is given haloperidol for agitation and within hours becomes rigid, drowsy, and unable to sit, with fevers and a rising CK. Which diagnosis and management principle is central?
opts: Dementia with Lewy bodies - avoid neuroleptics (severe, potentially fatal sensitivity); use cholinesterase inhibitors
concept: Dementia with Lewy bodies - neuroleptic sensitivity (neuroleptic malignant-like reaction); avoid antipsychotics

stem: A 52-year-old man is rescued from a burning building with soot in the mouth and confusion. Intubated and ventilated on 100% oxygen, he remains acidotic: pH 7.10, lactate 12 mmol/L, carboxyhaemoglobin 8%, and central venous oxygen saturation is high (75%). Which treatment targets the underlying cellular toxin?
concept: Smoke inhalation - cyanide poisoning (lactic acidosis + high central venous oxygen saturation out of proportion to COHb); hydroxocobalamin

stem: A 41-year-old man with exsanguinating haemorrhage from a liver laceration is peri-arrest: temperature 34.8 C, pH 7.15, PT longer than 100 s. A massive transfusion protocol is activated. Which resuscitation strategy best prevents worsening coagulopathy and acidosis?
opts: Red cells alone until cross-match is complete
Crystalloid at 3 times the estimated blood loss
Balanced 1:1:1 red cells, plasma, and platelets
Plasma alone until red cells arrive
concept: Massive transfusion - balanced 1:1:1 damage-control resuscitation in the lethal triad

stem: A 70-year-old man develops painful bluish discolouration of multiple toes of both feet one day after coronary angiography. The feet are warm with palpable dorsalis pedis pulses; there is early gangrene of the right great toe tip, and his creatinine has begun to rise with new eosinophilia. Which listed diagnosis is LEAST consistent with this picture?
concept: Cholesterol atheroembolism (blue toe syndrome) - post-procedural, palpable pulses, AKI, eosinophilia; Raynaud is the least consistent mimic

stem: Immediately after extubation following a total thyroidectomy, a patient develops progressive stridor, respiratory distress, and oxygen desaturation. Awake flexible laryngoscopy shows BOTH vocal cords fixed in a paramedian position. What is the emergency, and the single most appropriate immediate management?
opts: Wound haematoma - open the wound at the bedside
Unilateral RLN injury - observe with hoarseness monitoring
Bilateral recurrent laryngeal nerve injury - urgent intubation/tracheostomy
concept: Bilateral RLN injury - both cords fixed in paramedian position -> acute airway obstruction -> urgent airway

stem: A 58-year-old man with known primary hyperparathyroidism presents with confusion, nausea, polyuria, and dehydration; calcium 15.2 mg/dL, PTH 420 pg/mL. After aggressive IV fluids and a bisphosphonate, calcium remains 13.8 mg/dL with improving alertness. Which is the definitive treatment?
opts: Observation and repeat calcium in the morning
concept: Parathyroid (hypercalcaemic) crisis - definitive treatment is urgent parathyroidectomy after medical stabilisation

stem: A 79-year-old cachectic woman with chronic constipation presents with 48 hours of colicky pain, vomiting, distension, and absolute constipation. There is no groin lump, no surgical scar, and no inguinal tenderness; she reports sharp pain down the medial side of the right thigh during coughing and on passive hip extension. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Obturator hernia - Howship-Romberg sign in the thin elderly woman; small-bowel obstruction without a lump

stem: A 27-year-old man has a painless solid right testicular mass. Tumour markers: AFP 540 ng/mL (elevated), hCG normal, LDH mildly raised. Orchidectomy is planned. Which histological classification applies, and what does it mean for further management?
opts: Non-seminomatous germ cell tumour - cisplatin-based chemotherapy pathway
concept: Testicular GCT - elevated AFP indicates a non-seminomatous component (pure seminoma never raises AFP)

stem: A 30-year-old man with a T5 complete spinal cord injury develops sudden severe headache, sweating, flushing, and BP 210/115 mmHg with bradycardia. Which single measure is the FIRST priority in management?
opts: Sit the patient up and relieve bladder distension (check and drain the catheter)
Start IV antibiotics for presumed urosepsis
concept: Autonomic dysreflexia - remove the noxious trigger (bladder distension first), then control BP if persistent

stem: A 34-year-old primigravida has an uncomplicated monochorionic diamniotic (MCDA) twin pregnancy confirmed on first-trimester ultrasound. She is now 34 weeks with normal growth and Dopplers of both twins. When is planned delivery recommended for uncomplicated MCDA twins, and why?
opts: 32-33 weeks - the shared placenta always fails after this
36-37 weeks - balancing late-stillbirth risk against prematurity
concept: Multiple pregnancy - chorionicity sets delivery timing (uncomplicated MCDA twins: 36-37 weeks)

stem: A 57-year-old woman on tamoxifen for breast cancer develops postmenopausal bleeding for the first time. Transvaginal ultrasound shows an endometrium of 9 mm with multiple cystic spaces (a pattern commonly seen with tamoxifen). Which single next step is most appropriate?
opts: CT of the abdomen and pelvis
concept: Postmenopausal bleeding on tamoxifen - tissue diagnosis (endometrial biopsy) is mandatory; ultrasound cannot exclude malignancy

stem: A 10-month-old girl is below the 3rd centile for weight with normal length and head circumference. During a 5-day admission in which nursing staff feed her, she gains 300 g; there is no vomiting or diarrhoea, and her mother is observed to feed her rarely. Which diagnosis best explains the findings?
concept: Failure to thrive - rapid hospital catch-up weight gain with adequate feeding discriminates non-organic (psychosocial) from organic causes

stem: A newborn girl has bilateral cataracts, a systolic murmur (PDA confirmed on echo), sensorineural hearing loss on screening, and a 'blueberry muffin' rash. Her mother had a brief maculopapular rash with fever in the first trimester and was never vaccinated. Which congenital infection is most likely?
concept: Congenital rubella syndrome - cataracts + congenital heart disease (PDA) + deafness after first-trimester maternal infection

stem: A 4-year-old boy with organophosphate ingestion was atropinised and improved with drying of secretions. Forty-eight hours later he is alert with dry secretions but develops neck-flexor weakness, proximal limb weakness, and shallow irregular breathing. Which diagnosis and immediate treatment is correct?
opts: Relapse of cholinergic crisis - give more atropine
Intermediate syndrome - supportive ventilation with early pralidoxime
concept: Organophosphate poisoning - intermediate syndrome (24-96 h neuromuscular weakness with dry secretions) -> ventilation + early pralidoxime

stem: A child develops bilateral retinoblastoma before 1 year of age; a parent had retinoblastoma. According to Knudson's two-hit hypothesis, the child inherited one defective allele and a second somatic event knocked out the remaining allele. Which gene class and gene product is lost in the retinal cells?
concept: Rb tumour suppressor - two-hit loss in hereditary retinoblastoma; gatekeeper of the cell cycle

stem: A 35-year-old man with severe acute pancreatitis develops progressive dyspnoea over 48 hours, is hypoxaemic on high-flow oxygen, and has bilateral alveolar opacities on chest X-ray with no cardiomegaly. His BNP is normal and echocardiography shows good function with no valvular disease. If lung tissue were examined, which finding would be most characteristic?
opts: Hyaline membranes lining the alveolar walls (diffuse alveolar damage)
concept: ARDS - diffuse alveolar damage with hyaline membranes after a systemic insult (pancreatitis)

stem: A 62-year-old right-handed man suddenly develops right-sided face and arm weakness with a non-fluent (Broca) aphasia; his right leg is spared and there is no visual field defect. Which vascular territory is involved, and which artery most likely?
opts: Superior division of the left middle cerebral artery (MCA)
concept: Cerebral arterial territories - MCA superior division (face/arm weakness + Broca aphasia, leg spared)

stem: During total abdominal hysterectomy, the uterine artery is clamped at the base of the broad ligament just lateral to the cervix. Which statement best describes the ureter's relationship there, and what risk does it carry?
opts: The ureter crosses anterior (superior) to the artery, protected by the ovarian ligament
The ureter passes UNDER (posterior to) the uterine artery - 'water under the bridge' - and can be clamped with it
The ureter lies 5 cm lateral to the artery and is outside the operative field
The ureter crosses the artery within the mesovarium, anterior to the ovary
concept: Pelvic ureter - passes under the uterine artery at the broad-ligament base; the classic hysterectomy injury hazard

stem: A 40-year-old man with an odontogenic infection has dysphagia and fever. CT shows a retropharyngeal collection that tracks BEHIND the alar fascia into the plane between the alar and prevertebral fasciae. Which complication risk is greatest, and what limits the spread?
opts: Direct carotid-sheath erosion with ipsilateral Horner syndrome
Posterior mediastinal spread, potentially to the level of the diaphragm
Anterior mediastinal spread through the pretracheal space
A self-limited abscess with no inferior extension
concept: Deep neck spaces - the danger space (alar-prevertebral plane) extends from the skull base to the diaphragm -> posterior mediastinitis

stem: A healthy 30-year-old woman at 32 weeks gestation lies supine on the examination couch and complains of dizziness; her blood pressure drops transiently. Compared with her non-pregnant baseline, which statement correctly describes cardiac output in normal pregnancy?
opts: Cardiac output is unchanged - blood is simply redistributed to the uterus
Cardiac output doubles to about 9 L/min
Cardiac output falls about 20% because of uterine venocaval compression
Cardiac output rises roughly 30-50% (an early stroke-volume rise plus a later modest heart-rate increase)
concept: Pregnancy physiology - cardiac output rises about 30-50%; supine hypotensive syndrome is a positional dip, not the baseline

stem: The countercurrent multiplier creates the medullary osmotic gradient that permits concentrated urine. A drug that abolishes active transport in one nephron segment abolishes urine-concentrating ability entirely. Which segment performs the active 'single effect' that drives the multiplier?
opts: Thick ascending limb - active NaCl reabsorption without water
Distal convoluted tubule - aldosterone-driven sodium reabsorption
concept: Countercurrent multiplier - the thick ascending limb's active NaCl pump is the single effect (why loop diuretics abolish concentration)

stem: A 68-year-old man with chronic kidney disease (eGFR 22 mL/min) has renal colic. Three days into treatment with an opioid he develops twitching and a generalised seizure; his renal function is unchanged. Which agent is most likely responsible, and which is the safest alternative?
opts: Meperidine (pethidine) - normeperidine accumulates and is proconvulsant
concept: Opioid prescribing in renal failure - normeperidine (meperidine metabolite) accumulates and causes seizures; fentanyl is the safest alternative

stem: A 58-year-old man with compensated cirrhosis (Child-Pugh A, previous variceal bleed) needs regular analgesia for painful knee osteoarthritis. Which analgesic regimen is most appropriate, and what is the key reason?
opts: Ibuprofen as needed while avoiding paracetamol entirely - NSAIDs are hepatic-safe
Paracetamol at a reduced dose while AVOIDING NSAIDs - NSAIDs raise bleeding and renal risk
High-dose paracetamol together with an NSAID for full cover
concept: Analgesic choice in cirrhosis - reduced-dose paracetamol is the safest option; NSAIDs are avoided (variceal bleeding and renal risk)

stem: A 62-year-old man is found to have an isolated alkaline phosphatase of 520 U/L with a normal GGT, bilirubin, ALT, calcium, and phosphate. Which pair of findings - and which single confirmatory test - best explains the pattern?
opts: Biliary pathology - confirm with liver biopsy
Bone isoenzyme source (e.g. Paget disease) - confirm with bone-specific ALP isoenzyme
Renal phosphate leak - confirm with 24-hour urinary calcium
concept: ALP isoenzymes - a normal GGT means a bone source; bone-specific ALP isoenzyme confirms (Paget disease)

stem: During a dengue outbreak, household surveys find Aedes aegypti larvae breeding in domestic water-storage containers, and serotype surveillance shows ongoing transmission. Which intervention provides the most effective SUSTAINED vector control?
opts: Insecticide fogging to kill adult mosquitoes
Isolation of all febrile patients at home
Source reduction by eliminating or covering breeding containers
concept: Dengue vector control - source reduction (container elimination) is the sustainable core measure; fogging is transient

stem: A district hospital reports 15 cases of acute watery diarrhoea in one week against a usual baseline of 2-3 cases per week. As the investigating team arrives, the FIRST step of the standard outbreak investigation sequence is:
opts: Confirm the existence of an outbreak by comparing current and expected incidence
Immediately implement control measures before anything else
Start an analytic (case-control) study of the suspected food source
Analyse all stool samples in the laboratory before investigating
concept: Outbreak investigation - confirm the outbreak exists (observed vs expected incidence) before descriptive and analytic steps

stem: A 68-year-old man is brought by his son because his handwriting has become progressively smaller over the past 8 months. His wife has noticed a repetitive to-and-fro movement of his right thumb and index finger at rest that disappears when he reaches for a cup of tea. On examination there is cogwheel rigidity in both upper limbs, expressionless face, and intact higher mental functions. There is no history of stroke or antipsychotic drug use. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Clinical diagnosis of Parkinson's disease

stem: A 24-year-old woman presents with recurrent episodes of unilateral throbbing headache lasting 6–12 hours, associated with nausea and marked photophobia. Each episode is preceded for about 20 minutes by flashing zigzag lines in one visual field, which resolve completely before the headache begins. Neurological examination between episodes is normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Migraine with visual aura

stem: A 42-year-old woman presents with 4 months of pain and stiffness in her hands, worst on waking and lasting over one hour.
