On examination the metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints of both hands are symmetrically swollen and tender. Rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP antibodies are positive. You decide to start a disease-modifying antirheumatic drug today. Which of the following is the first-line DMARD?
concept: First-line DMARD in rheumatoid arthritis

stem: A 58-year-old man who has smoked 30 cigarettes daily for 30 years presents with a productive cough of copious purulent sputum on most days for 3 months in each of the last two consecutive years. He is overweight, centrally cyanosed, and has mild pedal edema. Examination reveals coarse crackles and a loud P2. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Chronic bronchitis — clinical definition and blue bloater phenotype

stem: A 45-year-old obese man wakes at night with excruciating pain in his right first metatarsophalangeal joint after a wedding dinner with abundant red meat and beer. The joint is red, hot, swollen and so tender he cannot bear the weight of the bed sheet. He has no history of trauma. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Acute gout (podagra)

stem: A 28-year-old man developed self-limiting diarrhea two weeks ago. He now presents with 5 days of rapidly progressive weakness that began in his feet and has ascended to his thighs, making him unable to climb stairs. Examination shows symmetrical flaccid weakness with complete loss of deep tendon reflexes in all four limbs and mild distal numbness. He is able to breathe normally at present. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: GBS — ascending flaccid paralysis post-infection

stem: A 22-year-old woman presents with fatigue, joint pains, photosensitive rash over both cheeks sparing the nasolabial folds, and painless oral ulcers. Urinalysis shows 2+ proteinuria. Which of the following is the best screening test to confirm the suspected systemic disease?
concept: ANA as screening test for SLE

stem: A 62-year-old man with a 40-pack-year smoking history presents with 3 months of difficulty rising from a chair and climbing stairs. Interestingly, his strength improves after he has been walking for a few minutes. Examination shows proximal lower limb weakness, diminished deep tendon reflexes that reappear after sustained effort, and dry mouth. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome — paraneoplastic

stem: A 28-year-old man presents with 3 months of increasing right knee pain without night cries. X-ray of the distal femur shows an expansile lytic lesion centered in the epiphysis extending up to the subchondral bone plate, with a 'soap-bubble' appearance and no sclerotic margin or periosteal reaction. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Giant cell tumor — epiphyseal lytic lesion in young adult

stem: A 48-year-old woman complains of gritty, burning eyes that feel like sand, and a dry mouth that wakes her at night forcing her to drink water. She has noticed bilateral painless swelling below and in front of her ears, and mild joint pains of both hands. Schirmer test shows reduced tear production and anti-Ro (SS-A) antibodies are positive. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Sjögren syndrome — sicca complex

stem: A 20-year-old cricketer is struck on the left temple by a ball. He loses consciousness briefly, walks off the field and talks normally for 40 minutes, then becomes drowsy and vomits. He is brought to the emergency department with a dilated, unreactive left pupil. CT scan shows a lens-shaped (biconvex) hyperdense collection over the left frontotemporal region. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Extradural (epidural) hematoma — lucid interval

stem: A 34-year-old man with nephrolithiasis is found on investigation to have bicarbonate 16 mmol/L, potassium 3.1 mmol/L, chloride 116 mmol/L, and a normal anion gap. Urinalysis shows generalized aminoaciduria and glucosuria despite normal blood glucose, and urine pH remains above 5.5. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Proximal (Type 2) RTA — Fanconi syndrome

stem: A 40-year-old man presents with his first episode of acute left renal colic radiating from loin to groin. Non-contrast CT shows a small radio-opaque calculus in the distal ureter. Stone analysis is later reported. Which of the following is the MOST COMMON composition of renal calculi?
concept: Most common renal stone = calcium oxalate

stem: A 3-year-old girl is brought because her mother has noticed increasing abdominal size. Examination reveals a smooth, firm, non-tender mass in the right flank that does NOT cross the midline. There is mild hypertension and microscopic hematuria. Abdominal ultrasound shows a solid mass arising from the right kidney. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Wilms tumor (nephroblastoma)

stem: A 30-year-old man involved in a road traffic accident presents with severe respiratory distress, distended neck veins, and falling blood pressure. The left side of his chest is hyper-resonant with completely absent breath sounds, and the trachea is deviated to the right. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Tension pneumothorax — clinical diagnosis, needle decompression

stem: A 26-year-old marathon runner nears the end of a race. His exercising leg muscles are generating heat, carbon dioxide, and lactic acid, and erythrocyte 2,3-BPG levels are rising. Which of the following changes occurs in the oxygen-hemoglobin dissociation curve to favor oxygen delivery to these muscles?
concept: Right shift of O2-Hb curve during exercise

stem: A healthy adult volunteer undergoes overnight polysomnography. The technician identifies a stage occupying the largest proportion of total sleep time, in which the EEG background of theta activity is interrupted by brief high-frequency bursts and occasional high-amplitude, biphasic slow deflections. Which sleep stage contains these characteristic findings?
opts: Stage N2 — sleep spindles and K-complexes
concept: Stage N2 sleep — spindles and K-complexes

stem: A 70-year-old man presents over 6 months with a slow shuffling, broad-based 'magnetic' gait in which his feet seem glued to the floor, new urinary incontinence, and progressive forgetfulness. CT scan shows ventricular dilatation out of proportion to the cerebral sulcal atrophy; lumbar puncture opening pressure is normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: NPH — wet, wobbly, wacky triad

stem: A 60-year-old man with a 40-pack-year smoking history presents with confusion and lethargy. Serum sodium is 116 mmol/L with euvolemia, low serum osmolality, inappropriately concentrated urine and normal renal, adrenal and thyroid function. Chest X-ray shows a central hilar mass. Which of the following is the most likely histological type of his lung tumor?
concept: Small cell lung cancer — SIADH paraneoplastic syndrome

stem: A 55-year-old woman presents with 2 years of slowly progressive rights-sided weakness and morning headaches. CT shows a well-defined, extra-axial, dural-based mass with broad dural attachment and calcification compressing but not invading the underlying brain. Histology of the resected lesion shows whorls of cells with concentric lamellated calcifications. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Meningioma — extra-axial, dural-based, psammoma bodies

stem: A 26-year-old man with well-controlled focal epilepsy has been maintained on a single antiepileptic drug for 3 years. He now presents with gum hypertrophy, hirsutism, and coarsening of facial features that are embarrassing him socially. Blood counts and liver enzymes are normal. Which of the following drugs is most likely responsible for these effects?
concept: Phenytoin — gingival hyperplasia and hirsutism

stem: A 35-year-old man with allergic rhinitis works as a long-distance truck driver. He stopped taking his previous antihistamine because of intolerable daytime drowsiness that endangered his driving. Which of the following second-generation antihistamines should be prescribed to avoid sedation?
concept: Second-generation (non-sedating) antihistamines

stem: A 50-year-old man with chronic kidney disease stage 3 is being treated with chemotherapy for lymphoma and develops tumor lysis syndrome. He is started on rasburicase and allopurinol prophylaxis. During treatment he develops an acute, intensely painful attack of great toe arthritis. Which of the following drugs used in this metabolic emergency is itself a recognized cause of hyperuricemia and gout?
concept: Drug-induced hyperuricemia — loop diuretics

stem: A 55-year-old man undergoes truncal vagotomy with gastrojejunostomy for chronic gastric outlet obstruction. Two weeks after surgery, samples of his resting gastric content are aspirated and analyzed. Which of the following best describes the composition of resting (basal) gastric secretion?
concept: Basal gastric secretion composition

stem: A 20-year-old man presents with a single episode of painless gross hematuria that began 2 days after an upper respiratory tract infection with sore throat and low-grade fever. The hematuria resolves within 5 days. Serum complement C3 level is normal. Urinalysis 3 weeks later shows only persistent microscopic hematuria. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: IgA nephropathy — synpharyngitic hematuria

stem: A 24-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with acute severe asthma: respiratory rate 30/min, inability to complete sentences in one breath, pulse 118/min, peak expiratory flow 45% of predicted. Nebulized ipratropium is being arranged. Which of the following should be given IMMEDIATELY as the first-line bronchodilator?
concept: Acute asthma — short-acting beta-2 agonist first

stem: A 70-year-old man develops profuse diarrhea and vomiting during a cholera outbreak. On arrival his blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg lying down, JVP is not visible, skin turgor is reduced, urine output is 15 ml/hour with urine sodium 12 mmol/L, fractional excretion of sodium 0.7%, and urea:creatinine ratio is markedly raised. What is the most likely type of his acute kidney injury?
concept: Prerenal AKI — hypovolemia with sodium avidity

stem: A 65-year-old woman with acute pulmonary edema presents orthopneic with pink frothy sputum, bilateral crepitations, and blood pressure 160/95 mmHg. She is sat up, given oxygen, and sublingual glyceryl trinitrate. Which of the following intravenous drugs should be given to produce rapid diuresis and venodilation?
concept: Loop diuretic in acute pulmonary edema

stem: A 66-year-old woman presents with 2 years of gradually worsening right knee pain that increases with use and is relieved by rest, with morning stiffness lasting only 15 minutes. Examination shows crepitus, bony enlargement of the knee margin, and restricted flexion without warmth or effusion. X-ray shows asymmetric joint space narrowing with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes. ESR is normal, RF negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Osteoarthritis — wear-and-tear pattern

stem: A 7-year-old girl is referred because her schoolteacher reports frequent 10-second episodes during which she stops mid-sentence, stares blankly with fluttering eyelids, and does not respond to being called, then immediately resumes talking without confusion. These occur up to 30 times daily. EEG shows generalized 3-Hz spike-and-wave discharges. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Childhood absence epilepsy

stem: A 4-year-old boy presents with 5 days of periorbital swelling progressing to generalized edema and abdominal distension. Urine protein is 4+ on dipstick, 24-hour urine protein is 3.2 g, serum albumin is 16 g/L, and total cholesterol is 9.8 mmol/L. There is no hematuria, blood pressure is normal, and complement levels are normal. What is the most likely histological diagnosis?
concept: Minimal change disease — most common nephrotic syndrome in children

stem: A 60-year-old man started on a new antituberculous regimen 10 days ago presents with fever, maculopapular rash over the trunk, arthralgia, and a rise in serum creatinine from 0.9 to 2.4 mg/dL. Urinalysis shows mild proteinuria, pyuria with eosinophiluria, and white cell casts. Urine culture is sterile. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: AIN — drug hypersensitivity triad

stem: A 58-year-old man with known congestive cardiac failure presents with 2 weeks of increasing breathlessness. Chest examination shows stony dull percussion note, diminished breath sounds and reduced vocal resonance at both lung bases, with findings characteristically shifting when he sits forward. Serum BNP is markedly raised. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Pleural effusion — signs and transudate cause

stem: A 34-year-old woman presents with fluctuating ptosis and diplopia that worsens towards evening and after prolonged reading, with difficulty chewing meat at dinner despite normal breakfast swallowing. Ice-pack test shows resolution of ptosis, and anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies are positive. Which of the following is the first-line symptomatic treatment?
concept: Myasthenia gravis — acetylcholinesterase inhibitor

stem: A 38-year-old woman with symmetrical small-joint arthritis for 8 months has negative rheumatoid factor but persistent joint swelling and early erosions on hand X-ray. Which of the following antibodies, more specific than rheumatoid factor, should be ordered to support the diagnosis?
concept: Anti-CCP — most specific antibody for RA

stem: A 58-year-old diabetic man presents 2 days after an anterior STEMI. He is now in heart failure with an ejection fraction of 38% on echo, blood pressure 118/72 mmHg, potassium 4.1 mmol/L, and creatinine 1.1 mg/dL. Which of the following drugs improves survival and prevents adverse remodeling and should be started now?
concept: ACE inhibitor post-MI with LV dysfunction

stem: A 45-year-old woman presents with 2 years of Raynaud phenomenon, tightening of the skin limited to the face and hands with painful finger-tip pitting scars, and increasing difficulty swallowing solid food. Investigations show positive antinuclear antibody with a nucleolar pattern, dilated nailfold capillaries, and mild pulmonary fibrosis on high-resolution CT. What is the most likely diagnosis and its specific autoantibody?
concept: Limited systemic sclerosis (CREST) — anticentromere

stem: A 58-year-old man with early Parkinson's disease has tremor-predominant disease with minimal disability. His physician wants to delay starting levodopa and offers a drug that acts by promoting dopamine release and blocking its reuptake, providing mild symptomatic benefit. Which of the following drugs fits this description?
concept: Amantadine — dopamine release/reuptake blocker

stem: A 62-year-old hypertensive man presents with sudden right-sided hemiplegia and inability to speak. When asked a question, he understands perfectly, tries hard to answer, but produces broken, effortful, non-fluent speech with missing small words, and he becomes visibly frustrated because he knows what he wants to say. CT shows a left inferior frontal gyrus infarct. Which cortical area is affected?
concept: Broca (expressive) aphasia

stem: A 22-year-old woman presents with recurrent episodes of sudden breathlessness, wheeze and nocturnal cough, each triggered by cold air and her cat, and each resolving completely within hours. Between episodes she is entirely asymptomatic with normal examination. Spirometry shows FEV1/FVC 0.68 with 16% bronchodilator reversibility. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Asthma — reversible episodic airflow obstruction

stem: A 55-year-old man has worked for 20 years in stone cutting and tunnel construction. He presents with progressive exertional breathlessness and a chronic dry cough. Chest X-ray shows multiple small rounded opacities with 'egg-shell' calcification of hilar lymph nodes. He is now found to have markedly reduced FEV1 and is being screened for a known associated infection risk. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Silicosis — stone/rock dust exposure

stem: A neonatologist is explaining the oxygen delivery characteristics of fetal blood to a group of students. Fetal blood must be able to extract oxygen from the maternal circulation at relatively low oxygen tensions. Which of the following explains this property of fetal hemoglobin?
opts: Fetal hemoglobin binds 2,3-BPG more avidly than adult hemoglobin
Fetal hemoglobin has higher affinity for oxygen because 2,3-BPG binds it poorly
Fetal hemoglobin contains alpha chains that increase oxygen unloading
Fetal hemoglobin has a P50 identical to adult hemoglobin
concept: HbF left-shift of oxygen dissociation curve

stem: A 68-year-old man presents with 3 days of high fever, rigors, productive rusty sputum, and right-sided pleuritic chest pain. Examination shows consolidation of the right lower lobe with bronchial breathing. Sputum Gram stain shows gram-positive diplococci. What is the most likely causative organism?
concept: Pneumococcal lobar pneumonia

stem: A 24-year-old man presents with 2 days of painful vesicles grouped on an erythematous base over the right buttock, with burning neuralgia, following similar previous episodes. PCR from the vesicle fluid confirms herpes simplex virus type 2. Which of the following drugs should be prescribed for this episode?
concept: Acyclovir for HSV infections

stem: A 58-year-old man with a newly diagnosed central lung mass presents with confusion, nausea and generalized weakness. Serum sodium is 118 mmol/L, plasma osmolality 252 mOsm/kg, urine osmolality 520 mOsm/kg, urine sodium 55 mmol/L. He is clinically euvolemic with normal renal, adrenal and thyroid function. What is the most likely cause of his hyponatremia?
concept: SIADH — euvolemic hyponatremia

stem: A 30-year-old man with intractable dry non-productive cough from acute bronchitis, keeping him awake at night with no sputum production, asks for something to control it. His chest examination and oxygen saturation are normal. Which class of drug is most appropriate?
concept: Antitussive for dry cough

stem: A 45-year-old man presents with severe headache and vomiting after a subarachnoid hemorrhage; ICP monitoring shows sustained intracranial pressure of 28 mmHg. Along with head-up positioning and hyperosmolar therapy, an osmotic diuretic is ordered. Which of the following drugs acts by raising plasma osmolality to draw water out of brain tissue?
concept: Mannitol — osmotic diuretic for raised ICP

stem: A 52-year-old woman presents with progressive fatigue and pruritus. Examination shows xanthelasma and hepatomegaly. Investigations: ALP markedly raised, AMA (anti-mitochondrial antibody) positive, IgM elevated, cholesterol raised. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Primary biliary cholangitis — AMA positive

stem: A 28-year-old woman presents with a recurrent painful shallow ulcer on the inner aspect of her lower lip, 8 mm in diameter with a yellow-gray central base and erythematous halo, healing spontaneously over 10 days without scarring. She has no genital ulcers, no eye symptoms and no bowel symptoms. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Recurrent aphthous stomatitis

stem: A 40-year-old man presents with 3 weeks of progressive bilateral pitting pedal edema and frothy urine. Investigations: 24-hour urine protein 5.8 g, serum albumin 21 g/L, cholesterol 8.2 mmol/L, and microscopic hematuria absent. Renal biopsy shows effacement of epithelial foot processes. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Nephrotic syndrome definition

stem: A 25-year-old man fell from a ladder striking his head. He now presents with clear watery fluid dripping from his left nostril that tests positive for glucose, and a bruise spreading behind his left ear over the mastoid with intact tympanic membrane. There is left-sided anosmia. CT confirms a fracture line through the anterior skull base. What is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Basal cell carcinoma of the nose
concept: Basal skull fracture — CSF leak and Battle sign

stem: A newborn is examined after an uncomplicated delivery. There is a small cystic swelling in the lower lumbar midline covered by a layer of intact skin, which transilluminates, is associated with a tuft of hair and a dimple on the overlying skin, and neurology of the lower limbs is normal. MRI shows herniation of meninges through a posterior vertebral defect containing CSF only. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Spina bifida variants

stem: A 60-year-old woman presents with diffuse bone pain and difficulty rising from a chair, waddling gait, and proximal muscle weakness. Investigations: calcium 2.0 mmol/L, phosphate 0.7 mmol/L, ALP 340 U/L, PTH elevated, and 25-OH vitamin D level 8 ng/ml. X-ray shows partial radiolucent bands (Looser zones) in the pubic rami. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Osteomalacia — defective mineralization

stem: A 19-year-old woman brought to the emergency department after an acute panic attack is breathing at 38 breaths per minute. Arterial blood gas shows pH 7.56, PaCO2 26 mmHg, PaO2 104 mmHg, bicarbonate 22 mmol/L. Her hands are tetanic with positive Chvostek sign. What is the acid-base disturbance?
concept: Acute respiratory alkalosis from hyperventilation

stem: A 26-year-old woman with established systemic lupus erythematosus on hydroxychloroquine presents for review. She has active polyarthritis and new proteinuria. Which of the following antibodies correlates best with active disease and lupus nephritis flares?
concept: Anti-dsDNA tracks SLE activity and nephritis

stem: A 22-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department 1 hour after ingestion of an unknown quantity of her mother's sleeping tablets. She is drowsy with respiratory rate 8/min and oxygen saturation 88%. You decide the specific reversal agent is required. Which of the following is the antagonist of benzodiazepine overdose?
concept: Flumazenil — benzodiazepine antagonist

stem: A 24-year-old man presents with 3 years of gradual-onset inflammatory low back pain — worse at rest and in the early morning, better with exercise — with morning stiffness lasting over an hour. Examination shows restricted lumbar flexion (reduced Schober test) and chest expansion of 2 cm. HLA-B27 is positive and X-ray shows bilateral sacroiliitis with syndesmophytes. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Ankylosing spondylitis — axial spondyloarthropathy

stem: A 52-year-old man with chronic hepatitis B presents with 2 months of progressive ankle edema. 24-hour urine protein is 7.2 g, albumin 22 g/L, cholesterol 9 mmol/L; urine microscopy shows no hematuria and blood pressure is normal. Renal biopsy shows subepithelial immune deposits with a granular pattern and spike formation on silver stain. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Membranous nephropathy — adult nephrotic syndrome

stem: A 62-year-old man with NYHA class III heart failure, ejection fraction 30%, already on ramipril and carvedilol, remains symptomatic with persistent pulmonary congestion. Serum potassium is 4.3 mmol/L and creatinine is 1.0 mg/dL. Which of the following drugs should be added to reduce mortality and improve symptoms?
concept: Aldosterone antagonist in HFrEF

stem: A 47-year-old woman presents with the sudden onset of the worst headache of her life during straining at stool, followed by vomiting, neck stiffness and transient loss of consciousness. CT shows hyperdensity in the basal cisterns and the right middle cerebral artery bifurcation shows a saccular outpouching on angiography. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: SAH — thunderclap headache

stem: A 62-year-old man with a 50-pack-year smoking history presents with 3 months of worsening pain in his left shoulder radiating down the inner aspect of his arm, accompanied by weakness and wasting of the small muscles of his left hand. Examination shows ptosis, miosis and anhidrosis of the left eye, and absent left arm reflexes. Chest X-ray shows an apical mass. What is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Small cell lung cancer with SIADH
concept: Pancoast (superior sulcus) tumor — Horner + brachial plexus

stem: A 64-year-old man with newly diagnosed idiopathic Parkinson's disease has bradykinesia and rigidity interfering with dressing and eating. His physician starts a combination drug in which one component is converted centrally to dopamine and the other blocks its peripheral decarboxylation to minimize nausea and cardiovascular side effects. Which of the following is this combination?
concept: Levodopa + peripheral dopa-decarboxylase inhibitor

stem: A 72-year-old woman is brought by her family for 3 years of insidiously progressive memory decline. She first forgot recent conversations, then repeatedly asked the same questions, and has now started misplacing household objects and getting lost on familiar streets. She has no gait abnormality and no urinary incontinence. Examination shows slowly progressive cognitive impairment without focal signs. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Alzheimer's — progressive amnestic dementia

stem: A 36-year-old man with long-standing nephrolithiasis and nephrocalcinosis on ultrasound is investigated for persistent metabolic acidosis. Arterial pH is 7.30, bicarbonate 14 mmol/L, potassium 3.2 mmol/L, chloride 112 mmol/L (normal anion gap), and urine pH remains 6.8 despite acid loading. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Distal (Type 1) RTA — cannot acidify urine

stem: A 50-year-old man receiving palliative care for metastatic lung cancer has a distressing dry cough that is not controlled by simple measures. He is not hypoxic, and sputum retention is not an issue. Which of the following opioids is commonly used for its central antitussive action to suppress this cough?
concept: Codeine — antitussive opioid

stem: A 48-year-old man develops acute kidney injury 2 days after emergency laparotomy for perforated diverticulitis complicated by prolonged hypotension. On review, urine output is 20 ml/hour, urine sodium 48 mmol/L, fractional excretion of sodium 3.2%, and urinalysis shows muddy brown granular casts. Blood pressure is now stable on noradrenaline. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: ATN after ischemic insult

stem: A 74-year-old woman with chronic knee osteoarthritis presents with an acute hot swollen right knee after minor activity. Synovial fluid analysis shows rhomboid-shaped, positively birefringent crystals under polarized light, and knee X-ray shows chondrocalcinosis. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Pseudogout — calcium pyrophosphate deposition

stem: A 66-year-old man presents with recurrent deep venous thrombosis. The second episode occurred despite therapeutic anticoagulation. There is no family history of clotting, but he has unexplained weight loss and a strong smoking history. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
opts: Increase warfarin target INR to 3.5 lifelong
Placement of a permanent IVC filter
concept: Unprovoked/recurrent VTE — occult malignancy screen

stem: A 42-year-old woman presents 10 days after a long-haul flight with sudden pleuritic right chest pain, breathlessness, and mild hemoptysis. She is tachypneic at 28/min with tachycardia of 112/min, oxygen saturation 90%, and a swollen tender right calf. ECG shows sinus tachycardia with a new incomplete right bundle branch block. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: PE — post-flight pleuritic pain with DVT source

stem: A 58-year-old man who worked for 25 years as a coal miner presents with exertional breathlessness and a chronic cough productive of black-tinged sputum. Chest X-ray shows multiple small upper-zone rounded opacities with a large conglomerate mass in the upper lobe. He has no features of rheumatoid disease. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Coal worker's pneumoconiosis

stem: A 58-year-old man presents with 8 months of progressive weakness. Examination reveals a combination of wasting and fasciculations of both hands WITH brisk deep tendon reflexes and an extensor plantar response on the right. Over the months he has also developed slurred speech and difficulty swallowing, with no sensory loss, no sphincter involvement, and normal cognitive function. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: ALS — UMN + LMN signs without sensory loss

stem: A 26-year-old man develops acute pain and swelling of his right knee and both heels two weeks after recovering from a severe episode of bloody diarrhea. He also has painless burning on urination and a painless shallow ulcer on the glans penis, with redness and blurred vision in his right eye. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Reactive arthritis — can't see, pee, or climb a tree

stem: A 55-year-old man with benign prostatic hyperplasia presents with 3 days of increasing urinary hesitancy culminating in complete inability to pass urine, lower abdominal distension and pain. He has become increasingly drowsy with a creatinine that has risen from 1.0 to 4.5 mg/dL. Bladder catheterization releases 1800 ml of urine. What type of acute kidney injury is this?
concept: Postrenal AKI — obstructive uropathy

stem: A 32-year-old man presents with chronic symmetric scaly erythematous plaques over his elbows and knees with nail pitting and onycholysis, and now 6 months of pain and morning stiffness in his distal finger joints with dactylitis (sausage digits). There is no penile discharge or recent infection. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Psoriatic arthritis — skin, nails and DIP joints

stem: A 58-year-old woman with acute left ventricular failure and pulmonary edema is receiving emergency treatment. Which of the following drugs acts on the Na-K-2Cl cotransporter in the thick ascending limb of Henle and is the diuretic of choice in this emergency?
concept: Loop diuretic site and choice

stem: A 66-year-old smoker who works in a rubber factory presents with painless total macroscopic hematuria. Urine cytology shows malignant cells, and cystoscopy reveals a papillary lesion on the lateral bladder wall. Biopsy confirms a tumor arising from the bladder urothelium with invasion into the lamina propria. What is the most likely histological type?
concept: Bladder tumor histology and risk factors

stem: A 44-year-old man is referred by his family for 2 years of increasingly bizarre behavior — irritability, impulsive gambling, and disinhibited sexual remarks — followed by the emergence of involuntary, non-rhythmic, dancelike movements of the face and limbs. His father died of a similar progressive illness in his 50s. MRI shows caudate nucleus atrophy. What is the most likely diagnosis?
concept: Huntington disease — CAG repeat, caudate atrophy

stem: A 62-year-old man develops frequent runs of ventricular tachycardia during the acute phase of a myocardial infarction, with hemodynamic stability maintained. Which of the following class Ib antiarrhythmic drugs is the agent of choice for this ventricular arrhythmia?
concept: Lidocaine for acute post-MI ventricular arrhythmias

stem: A 7-year-old girl with newly diagnosed absence seizures — frequent brief staring spells with generalized 3-Hz spike-and-wave on EEG — is started on monotherapy. Which of the following is the drug of choice?
concept: Ethosuximide — drug of choice for absence seizures

stem: A sleep laboratory records a healthy 25-year-old volunteer. In one stage, the EEG shows low-amplitude mixed-frequency activity resembling wakefulness, accompanied by rapid eye movements, complete loss of skeletal muscle tone except the diaphragm, and irregular heart rate and respiration. Dreaming is reported on awakening from this stage. Which stage of sleep is being described?
concept: REM sleep — paradoxical sleep

stem: A 58-year-old male with hypertension and diabetes presents with crushing retrosternal chest pain for 2 hours. ECG shows 3 mm ST elevation in leads V1–V4. He is hemodynamically stable. What is the single best next step in management?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Reperfusion strategy in acute STEMI — PCI vs fibrinolysis
discriminator: Anterior STEMI (V1–V4) with early presentation and no PCI contraindication; primary PCI is superior when available within 120 minutes.

stem: A 65-year-old woman presents with chest pain at rest for 30 minutes. ECG shows 1 mm ST depression in leads V5–V6 and T-wave inversion. High-sensitivity troponin is elevated at 3× the upper reference limit. What is the most likely diagnosis?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: NSTEMI vs unstable angina differentiation based on troponin
discriminator: Elevated troponin in the setting of ischemic symptoms and ECG changes (ST depression, TWI) defines NSTEMI, not unstable angina.

stem: A 55-year-old man presents with inferior STEMI on ECG (ST elevation in II, III, aVF). His blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg and JVP is elevated. You administer nitroglycerin for chest pain and his BP drops to 70/40 mmHg. What complication explains this response?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: RV infarct complicating inferior MI — nitrate sensitivity
discriminator: Inferior MI + hypotension + elevated JVP + nitrate-induced severe hypotension is classic for RV infarction. Nitrates reduce preload, which the preload-dependent RV cannot tolerate.

stem: A 60-year-old male presents with acute onset chest pain radiating to the back, described as a tearing sensation. BP is 190/110 mmHg in the right arm and 140/80 mmHg in the left arm. ECG shows no ST elevation. Chest X-ray shows widened mediastinum. What is the most likely diagnosis?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Aortic dissection vs MI differentiation
discriminator: Tearing chest pain radiating to back, hypertension, pulse differential, widened mediastinum — all classic for aortic dissection, not ACS.

stem: A 70-year-old woman with diabetes presents with chest tightness for 6 hours. ECG shows 2 mm ST elevation in II, III, aVF. She is hemodynamically stable. The nearest PCI-capable center is 180 minutes away. What is the single best management?
opts: Observe and repeat ECG in 6 hours
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Fibrinolysis vs PCI decision when PCI delay > 120 minutes
discriminator: When PCI cannot be performed within 120 minutes of FMC, fibrinolysis is indicated unless contraindicated. Transfer time 180 min exceeds the 120-min window.

stem: A 62-year-old man presents with chest pain and dyspnea 4 days after an inferior STEMI. On examination, there is a new loud pansystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border with a palpable thrill. He is in pulmonary edema. What is the most likely complication?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Post-MI mechanical complications — VSD vs papillary muscle rupture
discriminator: New pansystolic murmur at LLSB + thrill + postero-inferior MI location 3–5 days post-MI = VSD. Papillary muscle rupture murmur is at apex, not LLSB, and typically has no thrill.

stem: A 50-year-old male presents with retrosternal chest pain on exertion for 3 months. Pain is relieved within 2 minutes of rest. He has no pain at rest. ECG during pain shows 1 mm ST depression. Troponin is normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Stable angina vs unstable angina differentiation
discriminator: Exertional chest pain relieved by rest within minutes, chronic pattern (>3 months), normal troponin = stable angina.

stem: A 75-year-old woman with NSTEMI is being risk-stratified. Her GRACE score is 145. She has ongoing chest pain and dynamic ECG changes. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: NSTEMI risk stratification — GRACE score and invasive strategy timing
discriminator: GRACE score > 140 + ongoing symptoms/dynamic ECG changes = high-risk NSTEMI requiring early invasive strategy (angiography within 24 hours).

stem: A 48-year-old male presents with STEMI. He had a stroke 3 weeks ago. What is the most appropriate reperfusion strategy?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Fibrinolysis contraindications — recent stroke is an absolute contraindication
discriminator: Recent stroke (within 3 months) is an absolute contraindication to fibrinolysis. PCI is the only viable reperfusion option.

stem: A 55-year-old male received fibrinolytic therapy for anterior STEMI 90 minutes ago. He now has persistent ST elevation of > 50% in the lead with maximum initial elevation, and his chest pain has not resolved. What is the next best step?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Failed fibrinolysis — criteria and rescue PCI indication
discriminator: Persistent ST elevation < 50% resolution at 60–90 min post-fibrinolysis + ongoing pain = failed fibrinolysis → rescue PCI.

stem: A 68-year-old male with anterior STEMI develops complete heart block with a ventricular rate of 35/min. Blood pressure is 80/50 mmHg. What is the single best next step?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Post-MI arrhythmias — AV block management in STEMI
discriminator: Hemodynamically unstable complete heart block (hypotension, low ventricular rate) requires immediate temporary pacing. Transcutaneous pacing is the fastest bedside option.

stem: A 72-year-old man presents with NSTEMI. His GRACE score is 95. He has no recurrence of chest pain, no heart failure, and no arrhythmias. What is the most appropriate management strategy?
opts: Conservative ischemia-guided approach with stress test
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: NSTEMI — low-risk GRACE score management
discriminator: GRACE < 109 (low risk) without high-risk features → conservative ischemia-guided approach is appropriate, not early invasive.

stem: A 45-year-old male presents with chest pain starting 4 hours ago. ECG shows STEMI. He has a history of hemophilia A. What is the most appropriate reperfusion strategy?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Fibrinolysis contraindication — bleeding diathesis
discriminator: Hemophilia (bleeding diathesis) is an absolute contraindication to fibrinolysis; PCI avoids systemic bleeding risk.

stem: A 54-year-old female presents with 9 hours of chest pain. ECG shows 3 mm ST elevation in leads V1–V4. She has no contraindications. What is the most appropriate management?
opts: Conservative management since window has passed
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: STEMI reperfusion beyond the fibrinolysis window (> 6 hours)
discriminator: ST elevation > 6 hours (9 hours) → fibrinolysis window (6 h) has passed. PCI is still effective for up to 24 hours for STEMI.

stem: A 65-year-old female with STEMI is being prepared for reperfusion. She mentions she took sildenafil 6 hours ago. Which reperfusion strategy should be avoided?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: ACS bundle / reperfusion — nitroglycerin interaction with sildenafil
discriminator: Sildenafil within 24 hours is a contraindication to nitroglycerin (which is part of ACS medical therapy and often co-administered with fibrinolysis). Fibrinolysis without nitrates is possible, but the question tests the interaction.

stem: A 60-year-old man presents with acute chest pain. ECG shows ST elevation in II, III, aVF with reciprocal ST depression in aVL. Troponin I is 25 ng/mL (normal < 0.04). He receives aspirin, clopidogrel, and heparin. What additional anticoagulant is part of the standard ACS bundle for STEMI undergoing fibrinolysis?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: ACS bundle — anticoagulation in STEMI with fibrinolysis
discriminator: Enoxaparin (LMWH) or unfractionated heparin is the standard anticoagulant in ACS bundle with fibrinolysis.

stem: A 58-year-old STEMI patient develops sudden electromechanical dissociation (EMD) with loss of consciousness 3 days after infarction. CPR is ongoing. What is the most likely cause?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Post-MI mechanical complication — free-wall rupture presentation
discriminator: EMD/pulseless electrical activity (PEA) 3 days post-MI is classic for free-wall rupture causing pericardial tamponade.

stem: A 62-year-old male presents with chest pain. High-sensitivity troponin at presentation is normal. Repeat troponin at 3 hours is elevated to 5× ULN. What is the diagnostic significance?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Troponin timing and interpretation — 0/3-hour algorithm
discriminator: A rise from normal to elevated troponin within 3 hours in the setting of ischemic symptoms meets criteria for NSTEMI using the 0/3-hour hs-cTn algorithm.

stem: A 50-year-old male with known CAD status post CABG 8 years ago presents with chest pain. ECG shows 2 mm ST elevation in leads II, III, aVF. What is the most likely mechanism?
opts: Left internal mammary artery graft occlusion
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: STEMI in post-CABG patient — graft occlusion patterns
discriminator: Inferior STEMI in post-CABG patient most commonly reflects SVG occlusion (to RCA or distal CX) because SVGs have higher failure rates than LIMA grafts.

stem: A 55-year-old male with recent anterior STEMI is being discharged. Which of the following is NOT part of standard secondary prevention after ACS?
opts: Dual antiplatelet therapy for at least 12 months
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Secondary prevention after ACS — standard pharmacotherapy
discriminator: CCBs are not first-line for secondary prevention after ACS (unless for hypertension refractory to other agents or for rate control in AF with contraindication to beta-blockers).

stem: A 65-year-old woman with diabetes and hypertension presents with intermittent chest tightness at rest for the past 2 days. ECG shows T-wave inversion in V3–V6. Troponin is normal at 0 and 3 hours. What is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Type 2 MI due to demand ischemia
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Unstable angina — rest pain + normal troponin + dynamic ECG
discriminator: Rest angina + dynamic ECG changes (TWI) but normal serial troponins = unstable angina. The key is two normal troponins rule out NSTEMI.

stem: A 48-year-old male presents with 4 hours of anterior STEMI. He is a known case of severe aortic stenosis awaiting valve replacement. What is the most appropriate reperfusion strategy?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Fibrinolysis relative contraindication — severe aortic stenosis
discriminator: Severe AS is a relative contraindication to fibrinolysis due to risk of systemic embolization from potential valvular vegetations/thrombi. PCI is preferred.

stem: A 70-year-old man presents with NSTEMI. His creatinine is 2.5 mg/dL (eGFR 25 mL/min). He is being considered for angiography. Which of the following is the most appropriate contrast and hydration strategy?
opts: No contrast — proceed with conservative management only
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: ACS management — contrast nephropathy prevention in CKD
discriminator: In CKD: low-osmolar or iso-osmolar contrast + IV normal saline hydration (1 mL/kg/h for 12 h pre- and post-procedure) is the standard preventive strategy for contrast-induced nephropathy.

stem: A 52-year-old male with inferior STEMI develops hypotension that worsens with nitroglycerin. JVP is elevated to 14 cm H2O. Lungs are clear. What is the next best step in management?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: RV infarct management — fluid resuscitation
discriminator: Inferior MI + hypotension + elevated JVP + clear lungs = RV infarction. Treatment is IV fluids (preload), NOT nitrates or diuretics.

stem: A 66-year-old female presents with acute chest pain. ECG shows 2 mm ST elevation in II, III, aVF. She is nauseated and vomiting. She has a history of peptic ulcer disease with a GI bleed 6 weeks ago. BP is 100/70 mmHg. What is the most appropriate reperfusion strategy?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Fibrinolysis contraindication — recent GI bleed + STEMI reperfusion
discriminator: Active peptic ulcer disease with recent GI bleed (< 6 weeks) is a relative contraindication to fibrinolysis. Primary PCI avoids systemic bleeding risk and is preferred.

stem: A 58-year-old man with hypertension presents with exertional dyspnea and orthopnea. Echocardiography shows LVEF of 35% with a dilated left ventricle. How is this condition classified?
opts: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)
Heart failure with mid-range ejection fraction (HFmrEF)
Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF)
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Classification of heart failure by LVEF
discriminator: LVEF < 40% defines HFrEF regardless of symptoms.

stem: A 62-year-old woman with COPD and hypertension presents with progressive dyspnea. BNP level is 85 pg/mL. Which of the following is the most appropriate interpretation?
opts: Heart failure is effectively ruled out
BNP is non-diagnostic; further testing with echocardiography is required
Pulmonary embolism is the likely cause of dyspnea
Renal impairment is falsely elevating BNP
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: BNP interpretation in heart failure diagnosis
discriminator: BNP < 100 pg/mL has a high negative predictive value and effectively rules out HF.

stem: A 65-year-old man presents with orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, and bibasilar crackles. He sleeps on three pillows. Which chamber of the heart is primarily affected?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Clinical features of left-sided heart failure
discriminator: Orthopnea, PND, and bibasilar crackles indicate pulmonary congestion from left ventricular failure.

stem: A 55-year-old man with HFrEF on ramipril 10 mg daily develops a persistent dry cough after 4 weeks of therapy. What is the most appropriate next step?
opts: Add dextromethorphan to suppress the cough
Stop ramipril and observe without replacement
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: ACE-I cough management — switch to ARB
discriminator: ACE-I cough is managed by switching to an ARB, which does not affect bradykinin metabolism.

stem: A 62-year-old man with HFrEF (EF 35%) on optimal doses of ACE-I, bisoprolol, and spironolactone is started on dapagliflozin. What is the primary outcome benefit of adding this drug in HFrEF?
opts: Reduction in heart failure hospitalisation and cardiovascular mortality
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: SGLT2i benefit in heart failure
discriminator: SGLT2 inhibitors reduce HF hospitalisation and CV mortality in HFrEF, independent of glycemic control.

stem: A 70-year-old man with known HFrEF presents with acute onset severe dyspnea, hypoxia (SpO2 85%), and bilateral crackles up to the apices. BP is 150/90, HR 105. What is the single best first pharmacological intervention?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: First-line treatment for acute decompensated heart failure
discriminator: IV loop diuretics (furosemide) are first-line for congestion in acute HF.

stem: A 68-year-old man on chronic carvedilol therapy for HFrEF presents with acute pulmonary edema. His heart rate is 110 bpm. Which of the following is the correct approach to his beta-blocker during this acute episode?
opts: Continue carvedilol at the same dose
Double the carvedilol dose to control heart rate
Hold carvedilol until he is euvolemic and stable
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Beta-blocker management in acute decompensated HF
discriminator: Beta-blockers reduce myocardial contractility and should be temporarily held during acute decompensation.

stem: A 72-year-old man with advanced HFrEF (NYHA III-IV) has a serum sodium of 128 mEq/L. He is on furosemide, lisinopril, and spironolactone. Which hormone is primarily responsible for this hyponatremia?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Mechanism of hyponatremia in advanced heart failure
discriminator: Reduced effective circulating volume in advanced HF stimulates non-osmotic ADH release, causing water retention and dilutional hyponatremia.

stem: An 18-year-old man with beta-thalassemia major who has received regular blood transfusions since childhood presents with dyspnea, leg edema, and elevated JVP. Echocardiography shows a dilated left ventricle with LVEF of 30%. What is the most likely underlying cause?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Iron overload cardiomyopathy in transfusion-dependent thalassemia
discriminator: Repeated transfusions in thalassemia major lead to iron deposition in the myocardium, causing dilated cardiomyopathy.

stem: A 60-year-old man with severe COPD presents with bilateral leg edema, tender hepatomegaly, and elevated JVP. There are no crackles on chest auscultation. What is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Cor pulmonale (right heart failure secondary to lung disease)
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Clinical features of right heart failure (cor pulmonale)
discriminator: Elevated JVP + hepatomegaly + edema with clear lungs and history of COPD = cor pulmonale.

stem: A 55-year-old man with known HFrEF presents with acute dyspnea and bilateral pulmonary infiltrates on chest X-ray. Pulmonary artery catheterization reveals a pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) of 12 mmHg. What does this finding suggest?
opts: Cardiogenic pulmonary edema is the cause
Non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema (e.g., ARDS) is more likely
Both cardiogenic and non-cardiogenic mechanisms are present
Volume overload from renal failure is the primary cause
The PCWP is normal; pulmonary edema is not present
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Differentiating cardiogenic from non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema using PCWP
discriminator: PCWP < 18 mmHg in the presence of pulmonary edema suggests a non-cardiogenic cause.

stem: A 50-year-old woman is newly diagnosed with HFrEF (LVEF 30%) after presenting with dyspnea. She is euvolemic on examination, BP 120/80, HR 72, sinus rhythm. She is not on any heart failure medications. What is the single best next step?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: First-line mortality-reducing therapy in HFrEF
discriminator: ACE-I (or ARNI) is the foundational first-line mortality-reducing drug in HFrEF, started before or alongside beta-blockers.

stem: A 60-year-old man with HFrEF (EF 30%) on optimal doses of ramipril, bisoprolol, spironolactone, and dapagliflozin remains in NYHA class III with recurrent HF hospitalisations. Which medication change has been proven to provide additional mortality benefit?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: ARNI superiority over ACE-I in HFrEF
discriminator: PARADIGM-HF trial demonstrated that ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan) is superior to ACE-I in reducing mortality and hospitalisation in HFrEF.

stem: A 65-year-old man with HFrEF on bisoprolol 10 mg daily has a resting heart rate of 48 bpm and complains of fatigue and dizziness. He is euvolemic with BP 110/70. What is the most appropriate management?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Beta-blocker dose adjustment in symptomatic bradycardia
discriminator: Symptomatic bradycardia on beta-blocker → reduce dose. Never stop abruptly.

stem: A 68-year-old woman with stable HFrEF (EF 35%) on optimal medical therapy presents with 3 days of worsening dyspnea and 4 kg weight gain. She reports having eaten salty foods at a family gathering. All her medications are up to date. What is the most likely trigger of decompensation?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Identifying triggers of acute decompensation in chronic HF
discriminator: Weight gain + history of salty meal in a patient on optimal meds = dietary sodium excess causing fluid retention.

stem: A 22-year-old man with beta-thalassemia major and history of regular transfusions since childhood presents with dyspnea on climbing stairs. Examination reveals elevated JVP and a displaced apex beat. What is the single best test to confirm the underlying cause of his heart failure?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Investigation of choice for cardiac iron overload
discriminator: Cardiac MRI T2* is the gold standard for non-invasive quantification of myocardial iron content.

stem: A 65-year-old man presents 6 hours after an acute anterior wall MI with BP 80/50 mm Hg, cold clammy extremities, oliguria (< 20 mL/hr), and confusion. His JVP is elevated at 14 cm H2O. Which finding best distinguishes cardiogenic shock from hypovolemic shock in this patient?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Differentiating cardiogenic shock from hypovolemic shock
discriminator: Elevated JVP in shock indicates cardiogenic cause (high filling pressures), while hypovolemic shock has low JVP.

stem: A 55-year-old woman presents with dyspnea on moderate exertion 3 months after an anterior wall ST-elevation MI. Echocardiography shows LVEF of 45%. How should her heart failure be managed?
opts: Treat with diuretics only as needed for symptoms
Treat with ACE inhibitor and beta-blocker, similar to HFrEF
No treatment is needed as EF is above 40%
Treat as HFpEF with symptom control only
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Management of HFmrEF (mid-range ejection fraction)
discriminator: HFmrEF (LVEF 40-49%) is managed with the same mortality-reducing drugs as HFrEF based on current guidelines.

stem: A 72-year-old woman with hypertension and type 2 diabetes presents with exertional dyspnea and ankle edema. Echocardiography shows LVEF of 60% with normal LV size and evidence of diastolic dysfunction. BP is 155/90. Which of the following is the most appropriate management strategy?
opts: Start ramipril, bisoprolol, and spironolactone for mortality benefit
Control blood pressure and use diuretics for symptom relief
Start dapagliflozin primarily for mortality benefit
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Management strategy for HFpEF — no proven mortality drugs
discriminator: HFpEF has no proven mortality-reducing pharmacotherapy; management focuses on blood pressure control, diuretics for congestion, and comorbidity management.

stem: A 70-year-old man with acute cardiogenic pulmonary edema has a respiratory rate of 32/min, SpO2 of 88% on 15 L/min oxygen via a non-rebreather mask, and is using accessory muscles. He is conscious and able to protect his airway. What is the most appropriate next step?
opts: Increase oxygen to 100% with a higher flow system
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Indication for non-invasive ventilation in acute cardiogenic pulmonary edema
discriminator: Moderate-severe respiratory distress with hypoxia despite high-flow oxygen in an awake patient with intact airway → NIV (CPAP/BiPAP) is indicated.

stem: A 70-year-old woman with HFpEF (LVEF 60%), hypertension, and type 2 diabetes has persistent dyspnea despite optimal diuretic therapy and blood pressure control. Which additional therapy has been shown to reduce the risk of heart failure hospitalisation in such patients?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: SGLT2i in HFpEF for hospitalisation reduction
discriminator: EMPEROR-Preserved trial showed empagliflozin reduces HF hospitalisation in HFpEF patients.

stem: A 63-year-old man with HFrEF (EF 30%) has been on carvedilol 25 mg twice daily for 6 months. His resting heart rate is 52 bpm. He is asymptomatic, with normal exercise tolerance, BP 115/75. What is the most appropriate management?
opts: Reduce carvedilol to 12.5 mg twice daily
Continue the current dose without change
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Asymptomatic bradycardia on beta-blocker in HFrEF does not require dose adjustment
discriminator: Asymptomatic bradycardia in a stable HFrEF patient on target-dose BB does not require intervention.

stem: A 68-year-old woman with LVEF of 55%, hypertension, and diabetes has dyspnea on exertion and ankle edema. BP is 155/90, JVP is not elevated, and there are mild bibasilar crackles. CXR shows a normal heart size. Which of the following interventions is NOT indicated in this patient?
opts: Diuretics for pulmonary and peripheral congestion
Lifestyle modification including dietary sodium restriction
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: HFpEF does not require HFrEF mortality regimen
discriminator: LVEF 55% = HFpEF. No mortality benefit from ARNI/BB/MRA in HFpEF without separate indications.

stem: A 60-year-old man with newly diagnosed HFrEF (EF 25%) presents with acute pulmonary edema. After 48 hours of IV furosemide and CPAP, he improves but still has bibasilar crackles and 1+ edema. When is the most appropriate time to initiate a beta-blocker?
opts: Immediately, as beta-blockers reduce mortality in HFrEF
After the patient is euvolemic and stable, before discharge
Only after 6 months of ACE-I therapy
Beta-blockers are contraindicated in HFrEF with EF < 30%
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Timing of beta-blocker initiation in HFrEF after acute decompensation
discriminator: Beta-blockers are initiated only after the patient is euvolemic and no longer requires IV diuretics or inotropes.

stem: A 75-year-old woman with HFrEF (EF 30%), chronic atrial fibrillation, and chronic kidney disease (serum creatinine 2.5 mg/dL) is on digoxin 0.25 mg daily, furosemide, and lisinopril. She presents with nausea, vomiting, and yellow-tinted vision. ECG shows atrial fibrillation with a ventricular rate of 45 bpm. What is the most likely cause?
opts: Uremic syndrome from worsening renal function
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Digoxin toxicity in heart failure with renal impairment
discriminator: Renal impairment reduces digoxin clearance; classic triad of GI symptoms (nausea/vomiting), visual disturbances (yellow-tinted vision), and bradyarrhythmia points to digoxin toxicity.

stem: A 44-year-old man presents with palpitations. ECG shows a short PR interval, delta wave, and wide QRS complex. He develops atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular rate. Which drug is contraindicated?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: WPW + AF — verapamil contraindication
discriminator: Delta wave + short PR = WPW. Verapamil accelerates accessory pathway conduction and can degenerate to VF in WPW + AF.

stem: A 20-year-old man presents with palpitations and lightheadedness. ECG shows a narrow complex tachycardia at 180/min, regular, with no visible P waves. BP is 110/70 mmHg. What is the single best next step?
opts: Vagal manoeuvres followed by adenosine if ineffective
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Stable narrow complex SVT management algorithm
discriminator: Narrow complex, regular, stable (BP normal) SVT = vagal manoeuvres first, then adenosine. Not DC cardioversion (for unstable).

stem: A 35-year-old man presents with palpitations and presyncope. ECG shows a narrow complex tachycardia at 190/min. BP is 70/50 mmHg. What is the single best next step?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Unstable SVT — DC cardioversion indication
discriminator: Hypotension (BP 70/50) with tachycardia = hemodynamically unstable. Unstable SVT requires immediate synchronized DC cardioversion, not drugs.

stem: A 65-year-old woman with hypertension presents with palpitations. ECG shows irregularly irregular rhythm with no discernible P waves. Ventricular rate is 145/min. What is the most likely diagnosis?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: ECG recognition of atrial fibrillation
discriminator: Irregularly irregular rhythm + absent P waves = atrial fibrillation. No sawtooth pattern to suggest flutter.

stem: A 72-year-old man with newly diagnosed AF has hypertension (well-controlled), diabetes, and no prior stroke or TIA. His CHA2DS2-VASc score is calculated. Which single additional factor would change his anticoagulation recommendation from 'consider' to 'recommend'?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: CHA2DS2-VASc scoring and anticoagulation thresholds
discriminator: Age ≥75 scores 2 points in CHA2DS2-VASc. A score of ≥2 in men or ≥3 in women triggers a recommendation for oral anticoagulation.

stem: A 60-year-old male with AF and heart failure (dyspnoea, raised JVP, crackles) presents with a rapid ventricular rate of 130/min. What is the most appropriate rate control strategy?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Rate control in AF with heart failure — digoxin + diuretic
discriminator: AF + HF with signs of congestion (JVP, crackles) = digoxin for rate control + diuretic for decongestion. Beta-blockers may worsen acute HF.

stem: A 30-year-old woman presents with palpitations, heat intolerance, weight loss, and a staring gaze. Pulse is irregularly irregular at 140/min. What is the most appropriate rate control agent?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Thyrotoxic AF — beta-blocker is first-line
discriminator: Warm hands, tremor, staring gaze + AF = thyrotoxic AF. Beta-blocker (propranolol) is first-line because it directly counteracts thyrotoxicosis effects.

stem: ECG shows saw-tooth flutter waves at 300/min with every third flutter wave conducted to the ventricle. What is the ventricular rate?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Atrial flutter — calculating ventricular response with AV block
discriminator: Atrial rate 300/min with 3:1 AV block → ventricular rate = 300 ÷ 3 = 100/min.

stem: A 55-year-old man collapses in the emergency department. ECG shows a wide complex rhythm at 200/min with no pulse. What is the single best first action?
opts: Start chest compressions and secure airway
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: VF/pulseless VT — immediate defibrillation
discriminator: Wide complex + no pulse = VF/pulseless VT. Defibrillation is the first and most important intervention. Adrenaline and amiodarone come after shocks.

stem: A 60-year-old man remains in VF after 3 defibrillation attempts and 2 minutes of CPR. IV access is established. What are the next drugs to administer?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Refractory VF — amiodarone + adrenaline after 3 shocks
discriminator: After 3 failed shocks in VF/pulseless VT: amiodarone 300 mg IV + adrenaline 1 mg IV, then resume CPR and shock again.

stem: A 70-year-old woman with long-standing hypertension presents with presyncope. ECG shows a regular wide complex tachycardia at 170/min with AV dissociation. BP is 90/60 mmHg. What is the most likely diagnosis and best next step?
opts: Atrial flutter with aberrancy — give verapamil
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: VT recognition and management — unstable VT
discriminator: Wide complex + AV dissociation + hypotension = VT that is hemodynamically unstable → synchronized DC cardioversion.

stem: A 45-year-old woman with no cardiac history presents with palpitations. ECG shows a regular wide QRS tachycardia at 180/min. BP is 120/70 mmHg. She is asymptomatic other than palpitations. What is the most appropriate management?
opts: Amiodarone 150 mg IV infusion over 10 min
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Stable VT management — amiodarone
discriminator: Wide complex tachycardia + stable (normotensive, no symptoms) = stable VT → amiodarone IV. DC cardioversion is for unstable VT.

stem: A 30-year-old woman with anxiety presents after a tricyclic antidepressant overdose. ECG shows prolonged QRS (160 ms) and QTc (520 ms). What is the single best treatment?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: TCA overdose — sodium bicarbonate for Na channel blockade
discriminator: TCA overdose causes Na channel blockade → prolonged QRS/QTc → ventricular arrhythmias. Sodium bicarbonate is the specific antidote.

stem: A 50-year-old woman presents with palpitations and presyncope. ECG shows a regular rhythm at 250/min with a QRS of 120 ms. There is 1:1 conduction. The rhythm terminates spontaneously. What is the most likely diagnosis?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Atrial flutter with 1:1 AV conduction — recognition
discriminator: Rate 250/min (within flutter range 250-350) with 1:1 conduction at a rate that is exactly the atrial rate. The QRS is narrow (120 ms) suggesting supraventricular origin.

stem: A 65-year-old man with inferior STEMI develops complete heart block with a ventricular escape rate of 35/min. BP is 80/50 mmHg and he is drowsy. What is the single best acute management?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Complete heart block — hemodynamically unstable requires immediate pacing
discriminator: CHB + hypotension + drowsiness = hemodynamically unstable. Transcutaneous pacing is the fastest bedside intervention. Atropine is often ineffective in CHB.

stem: A 55-year-old asymptomatic woman has an ECG showing PR interval of 240 ms with no dropped beats. All QRS complexes are conducted. What is the diagnosis?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: First-degree AV block — ECG definition
discriminator: PR > 200 ms with 1:1 conduction = first-degree AV block. All QRS complexes are conducted; there are no dropped beats.

stem: ECG shows progressive PR prolongation followed by a non-conducted P wave. The QRS is narrow. This pattern repeats. What is the diagnosis?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Mobitz type I (Wenckebach) — ECG pattern
discriminator: Progressive PR prolongation → dropped QRS → narrow QRS = Wenckebach (Mobitz I). Usually in the AV node and often benign.

stem: ECG shows constant PR interval of 180 ms with intermittent non-conducted P waves. The QRS is wide (140 ms). BP is normal. What is the most appropriate management?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Mobitz type II — pacemaker indication even if asymptomatic
discriminator: Mobitz II (constant PR + dropped QRS) + wide QRS = infranodal block. High risk of progression to complete heart block → permanent pacemaker indicated.

stem: ECG shows P waves at 80/min and QRS complexes at 38/min with no relationship between them. The QRS is wide. What is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Atrial fibrillation with slow ventricular response
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Complete heart block — AV dissociation with independent rhythms
discriminator: Complete AV dissociation (no relationship between P and QRS) with atria faster than ventricles and wide QRS escape = complete heart block.

stem: A 75-year-old woman with complete heart block and a wide QRS escape rhythm is asymptomatic and has normal BP. What is the most appropriate long-term management?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Complete heart block — permanent pacemaker indication regardless of symptoms
discriminator: Complete heart block with wide QRS escape rhythm is an indication for permanent pacemaker even if asymptomatic, due to risk of asystole.

stem: A 40-year-old man collapses while playing football. Bystander CPR is started. The ECG on the defibrillator shows a chaotic rhythm with no discernible QRS complexes. What is the rhythm?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: VF — ECG recognition of coarse VF
discriminator: Chaotic rhythm with no discernible QRS complexes in a collapsed patient = VF. Asystole is a flat line; PEA has some electrical activity but no pulse.

stem: A 55-year-old woman on multiple QT-prolonging drugs presents with recurrent episodes of a polymorphic ventricular tachycardia where the QRS complexes twist around the baseline. She has a prolonged QTc of 560 ms. What is the single best acute treatment?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Torsades de pointes — IV magnesium is first-line
discriminator: Polymorphic VT with QRS twisting around baseline + long QTc = torsades de pointes. Magnesium sulphate (2 g IV over 1-2 min) is first-line, regardless of serum magnesium level.

stem: A 22-year-old woman with known WPW syndrome presents with palpitations. ECG shows a narrow complex tachycardia at 170/min, regular, without delta waves. She is hemodynamically stable. What is the most appropriate acute treatment?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Orthodromic AVRT (WPW) — adenosine is safe in narrow complex SVT
discriminator: Known WPW but narrow complex SVT without delta waves = orthodromic AVRT (impulse goes down AV node, up accessory pathway). Adenosine is safe and effective because it blocks AV node conduction.

stem: A 52-year-old man with stable angina on no medications presents for an elective ECG. The ECG shows a delta wave, short PR interval, and wide QRS. He is entirely asymptomatic. What is the most appropriate management?
opts: No treatment needed; reassure and follow up if symptoms develop
Stress test to evaluate for ischemia
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Asymptomatic WPW — no treatment needed
discriminator: Asymptomatic WPW (no history of palpitations, syncope, or AF) does not require treatment. Ablation is reserved for symptomatic patients or high-risk occupations.

stem: A 68-year-old man with ischaemic cardiomyopathy (LVEF 30%) and NYHA class II heart failure has an episode of sustained monomorphic VT. He is successfully cardioverted. What is the most appropriate long-term management to prevent sudden cardiac death?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: ICD indications — secondary prevention in structural heart disease
discriminator: LVEF ≤35% (30% here) + spontaneous sustained VT = class I indication for ICD for secondary prevention of sudden cardiac death.

stem: A 65-year-old man presents with exertional syncope, angina, and dyspnoea. On examination, he has a harsh ejection systolic murmur at the right upper sternal border radiating to the carotids, with a slow-rising pulse. What is the single best diagnostic test to confirm severity?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Aortic stenosis — diagnostic gold standard
discriminator: Exertional syncope + angina + dyspnoea + ejection systolic murmur RUSB radiating to carotids = AS. Doppler echo is the gold standard for grading severity (valve area, mean gradient).

stem: A 70-year-old woman with severe aortic stenosis develops exertional syncope and angina. She has NYHA class III symptoms. What is the definitive management?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Severe symptomatic AS — valve replacement indicated
discriminator: Symptomatic severe AS (syncope, angina, dyspnoea) has poor prognosis without intervention — 50% mortality at 2 years. Aortic valve replacement is indicated.

stem: A 60-year-old man with rheumatic heart disease has a mid-diastolic rumbling murmur at the apex with an opening snap. What is the most likely diagnosis?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Mitral stenosis — murmur recognition
discriminator: Mid-diastolic rumbling murmur at apex + opening snap = mitral stenosis. Opening snap is specific to MS and occurs when the stenotic mitral valve opens in early diastole.

stem: As the orifice of the mitral valve progressively narrows in mitral stenosis, which chamber pressure rises FIRST?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Mitral stenosis — haemodynamic sequence
discriminator: MS obstructs LV inflow → LA pressure rises first (not LV). This is the defining haemodynamic feature of MS.

stem: A 58-year-old diabetic patient had an inferior STEMI 2 days ago. He now has sudden hypotension and a new pansystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border with a palpable thrill. What is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Papillary muscle rupture with acute mitral regurgitation
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Post-MI VSD — physical exam discriminator (thrill at LLSB)
discriminator: Post-STEMI day 2 + new pansystolic murmur at LLSB + thrill = VSD. Papillary muscle rupture has apical murmur without thrill.

stem: A 70-year-old man with hypertension has a decrescendo diastolic murmur at the left sternal edge, a collapsing (water-hammer) pulse, and a wide pulse pressure of 80 mmHg. What is the most likely diagnosis?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Aortic regurgitation — murmur, pulse, and haemodynamics
discriminator: Decrescendo diastolic murmur at left sternal edge + collapsing pulse + wide pulse pressure = aortic regurgitation.

stem: A 55-year-old woman presents with dyspnoea on exertion and haemoptysis. ECG shows left atrial enlargement and atrial fibrillation. On auscultation, there is a loud S1, opening snap, and mid-diastolic rumble at the apex. What is the most likely cause of her valvular disease?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Rheumatic heart disease — most common cause of MS worldwide
discriminator: MS in a woman from a developing country with history suggestive of rheumatic fever = rheumatic heart disease. Rheumatic fever is the most common cause of MS globally.

stem: A 45-year-old man presents with a murmur found on routine exam. On auscultation, there is a mid-systolic click followed by a late systolic murmur at the apex. What is the most likely diagnosis?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Mitral valve prolapse — mid-systolic click + late systolic murmur
discriminator: Mid-systolic click + late systolic murmur at apex = mitral valve prolapse. The click is caused by sudden tensing of chordae tendineae as the prolapsing leaflet reaches its maximum excursion.

stem: A 35-year-old intravenous drug user presents with fever, tricuspid regurgitation murmur, and septic pulmonary emboli. Blood cultures grow Gram-positive cocci in clusters. What is the most likely organism?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Infective endocarditis — organism by risk group (IVDU)
discriminator: IVDU + tricuspid valve IE + Gram-positive cocci in clusters = Staphylococcus aureus. IVDU IE most commonly affects the tricuspid valve and is caused by S. aureus.

stem: A 50-year-old man with a history of mitral valve prolapse presents with fever for 2 weeks. On examination, there are painful red nodules on his fingertips, splinter haemorrhages under his nails, and conjunctival petechiae. Blood cultures are positive. What is the most likely diagnosis?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Infective endocarditis — Duke criteria and peripheral stigmata
discriminator: Fever + predisposing heart condition (MVP) + peripheral stigmata (Osler nodes, splinter haemorrhages, petechiae) + positive blood cultures = definite IE by Duke criteria.

stem: A 28-year-old woman with known mitral valve prolapse undergoes a dental extraction. Which of the following conditions would require antibiotic prophylaxis for infective endocarditis?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: IE prophylaxis — only highest-risk patients
discriminator: Only high-risk patients need IE prophylaxis: prosthetic valves, prior IE, unrepaired cyanotic CHD, cardiac transplant valvulopathy. MVP with regurgitation does NOT qualify for prophylaxis per current guidelines.

stem: A 19-year-old man presents with acute rheumatic fever following Group A streptococcal pharyngitis. He has carditis with mitral regurgitation. What is the most appropriate secondary prophylaxis regimen?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 1.2 MU IM every 3-4 weeks
Oral penicillin V 250 mg twice daily
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Rheumatic fever — secondary prophylaxis with benzathine penicillin G
discriminator: Benzathine penicillin G IM is the standard for secondary RF prophylaxis. Benzyl penicillin is short-acting IV and not used for prophylaxis.

stem: A 48-year-old woman with heart failure has an LVEF of 30% on echocardiography. She has functional mitral regurgitation. Which medication has the strongest mortality benefit in her condition?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: HFrEF with functional MR — ARNI mortality benefit
discriminator: ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan) has the strongest mortality benefit in HFrEF from the PARADIGM-HF trial, superior to ACE inhibitors.

stem: A 22-year-old man presents with acute onset fever, chills, and a new regurgitant murmur 2 weeks after a dental cleaning. He has pre-existing bicuspid aortic valve. Blood cultures grow Gram-positive cocci in chains that are optochin-resistant. What is the most likely organism?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: IE — Strep viridans after dental procedure in pre-existing valve disease
discriminator: Dental procedure + pre-existing valvular disease + Gram-positive cocci in chains = Streptococcus viridans (alpha-haemolytic, optochin-resistant). Strep viridans is the most common cause of native valve IE.

stem: A 60-year-old woman with a mechanical mitral valve replacement presents with fever and chills. She is started on empiric antibiotics for suspected prosthetic valve endocarditis. Blood cultures grow Gram-positive cocci in pairs and chains. What empiric antibiotic regimen is most appropriate?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Prosthetic valve IE — empiric antibiotic regimen
discriminator: Prosthetic valve IE requires vancomycin + gentamicin for empiric coverage (covers Staph epidermidis/methicillin-resistant Staph and Gram-negative bacilli).

stem: A 32-year-old woman presents with acute onset pleuritic chest pain, fever, and a pericardial rub. ECG shows diffuse ST elevation with PR depression. She had a sore throat 2 weeks ago. What complication of rheumatic fever is she most likely experiencing?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Acute rheumatic fever — carditis presentation
discriminator: Recent sore throat + fever + pericardial rub + diffuse ST elevation = acute rheumatic carditis (part of Jones criteria). Pericarditis is a common manifestation of rheumatic carditis.

stem: A 75-year-old man presents with dyspnoea, orthopnoea, and PND. On auscultation, he has a pansystolic murmur at the apex radiating to the axilla. What is the most likely diagnosis?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Mitral regurgitation — murmur character and symptoms
discriminator: Pansystolic murmur at apex radiating to axilla = mitral regurgitation. Orthpnoea and PND indicate left heart failure from volume overload.

stem: A 55-year-old man with suspected infective endocarditis has negative transthoracic echocardiography. What is the next best step?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: IE diagnosis — TOE when TTE is negative but suspicion remains
discriminator: Negative TTE + high suspicion for IE → transoesophageal echo (TOE) has higher sensitivity for vegetations, especially on prosthetic valves.

stem: A 68-year-old man with a mechanical aortic valve on warfarin presents with acute dyspnoea and一个新的 regurgitant murmur. His INR is 1.5. What prosthetic valve complication is most likely?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Prosthetic valve thrombosis — inadequate anticoagulation
discriminator: Mechanical valve + subtherapeutic INR + acute onset dyspnoea and regurgitant murmur = prosthetic valve thrombosis. Subtherapeutic anticoagulation is the major risk factor.

stem: A 30-year-old woman with known mitral stenosis (valve area 1.0 cm²) becomes pregnant. She develops worsening dyspnoea at 28 weeks gestation. What is the most appropriate next step?
opts: Medical management with diuretics and beta-blockers
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: MS in pregnancy — medical management first
discriminator: Pregnancy increases cardiac output and heart rate, worsening MS symptoms. Medical management (beta-blockers for rate control, diuretics for congestion) is first-line. Intervention is reserved for refractory symptoms.

stem: A 40-year-old man has a blood pressure of 150/60 mmHg with a bounding pulse. On auscultation, there is a decrescendo diastolic murmur at the left sternal border and a separate mid-systolic flow murmur at the apex. What do the two murmurs represent?
opts: Aortic regurgitation and Austin Flint murmur
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Austin Flint murmur — functional mid-diastolic murmur in severe AR
discriminator: Severe AR (wide pulse pressure, bounding pulse, decrescendo diastolic murmur) + mid-diastolic murmur at apex without opening snap = Austin Flint murmur. This is a functional murmur from the AR jet hitting the anterior mitral leaflet.

stem: A 72-year-old woman with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis is deemed high-risk for surgical valve replacement due to frailty and multiple comorbidities. What is the best therapeutic option?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: TAVI for high-risk severe AS
discriminator: High-risk surgical candidate + severe symptomatic AS = TAVI. TAVI is preferred over surgery in elderly/frail patients at high surgical risk.
