stem: A 65-year-old man with IE is being treated with antibiotics. On day 5, he develops acute dyspnoea and a new murmur. Echocardiogram shows severe acute aortic regurgitation with a large vegetation. What is the most appropriate next step?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: IE — surgical indications: heart failure from acute valvular regurgitation
discriminator: IE + acute severe AR + heart failure (dyspnoea) = surgical indication. Surgery is indicated for heart failure, uncontrolled infection, abscess, or embolic events despite appropriate antibiotics.

stem: A 50-year-old man with severe chronic aortic regurgitation presents with progressive dyspnoea and reduced exercise tolerance. Echocardiogram shows LV end-systolic diameter of 55 mm and LVEF of 45%. What is the most appropriate management?
opts: Medical management with vasodilators and monitor
Increase physical activity to strengthen heart
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Chronic severe AR — surgical indications (symptoms + LV dilation/dysfunction)
discriminator: Symptomatic severe AR + LVEF <50% (45%) + LVESD >50 mm (55 mm) = surgery indicated even if symptoms are mild.

stem: A 25-year-old woman with mild mitral stenosis (valve area 2.0 cm²) presents with acute dyspnoea and palpitations. ECG shows atrial fibrillation with a ventricular rate of 150/min. What is the most appropriate acute management?
opts: Rate control with beta-blocker or digoxin
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: MS with new AF — rate control first
discriminator: Mild MS + new AF + rapid ventricular rate → rate control first. AF with rapid rate in MS reduces diastolic filling time, worsening dyspnoea. Beta-blockers slow the rate and increase filling time.

stem: A 60-year-old diabetic man with hypertension has persistent proteinuria despite good glucose control. BP is 165/100 mmHg. Which antihypertensive class provides renoprotection beyond blood pressure reduction?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: HTN + DM + proteinuria — ACEi renoprotection
discriminator: ACE inhibitors reduce intraglomerular pressure, slow progression of diabetic nephropathy independent of BP lowering. They are first-line in HTN with proteinuria.

stem: A 28-year-old pregnant woman at 8 months gestation has BP 150/90 mmHg. Which antihypertensive agent is safest (Category A in pregnancy)?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: HTN in pregnancy — labetalol is Category A
discriminator: Labetalol (alpha + beta blocker) is Category A in pregnancy. ACEi and ARBs are teratogenic (Category D/X).

stem: A 52-year-old man is found comatose after a severe headache. BP is 180/110 mmHg. CT head shows subarachnoid haemorrhage. Which medication should be given to prevent a specific complication of SAH?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: SAH — nimodipine for cerebral vasospasm prevention
discriminator: Coma + severe headache + SAH on CT = subarachnoid haemorrhage. Nimodipine (calcium channel blocker) prevents delayed cerebral ischaemia from vasospasm.

stem: A 52-year-old man presents with BP 210/120 mmHg, confusion, and papilloedema on fundoscopy. What is the most appropriate classification and management?
opts: Stage 2 hypertension — start two oral agents
White coat hypertension — repeat BP measurement
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Hypertensive emergency vs urgency — end-organ damage defines emergency
discriminator: BP ≥180/120 + end-organ damage (encephalopathy with confusion, papilloedema) = hypertensive emergency. Requires IV antihypertensives and ICU monitoring.

stem: A 55-year-old man with a hypertensive emergency (BP 220/130 mmHg with encephalopathy) is started on IV therapy. What is the target BP reduction in the first hour?
opts: Reduce by 25% of the presenting BP
Reduce by 50% in the first hour
No reduction in the first hour — gradual over 24 hours
Reduce diastolic to <90 mmHg in 30 minutes
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Hypertensive emergency — target BP reduction 25% in first hour
discriminator: In hypertensive emergency, aim for 25% reduction in mean arterial pressure over the first hour. Rapid reduction to normal can cause cerebral and coronary hypoperfusion.

stem: A 62-year-old man presents with tearing chest pain radiating to the back, BP 200/110 in the right arm and 150/85 in the left arm. Chest X-ray shows widened mediastinum. What is the single best next diagnostic step?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Aortic dissection — diagnostic imaging
discriminator: Tearing chest pain radiating to back + pulse differential + widened mediastinum = aortic dissection until proven otherwise. CT aortogram is the gold standard diagnostic test.

stem: A 62-year-old man with confirmed Type A aortic dissection (involving ascending aorta) is being prepared for management. What is the most appropriate definitive treatment?
opts: Medical management with IV beta-blocker and vasodilator
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Aortic dissection — Type A requires emergency surgery
discriminator: Type A (ascending aorta involvement) = surgical emergency. Type B (descending aorta only) = medical management.

stem: A 62-year-old man with Type B aortic dissection has BP 200/110 mmHg. Which drug should be given FIRST to reduce the risk of extension?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Aortic dissection — beta-blocker FIRST before vasodilator
discriminator: In aortic dissection, beta-blocker must be given FIRST to reduce heart rate and dP/dt. Vasodilators are added AFTER beta-blockade to prevent reflex tachycardia which increases aortic wall stress.

stem: A 40-year-old man with hypertension and depressive illness needs an antihypertensive. His BP is 152/94 mmHg. Which drug is most suitable?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: HTN + depression — avoid beta-blockers, use CCB
discriminator: Beta-blockers can worsen or cause depression. CCBs (amlodipine) are CNS-neutral and preferred in patients with depression.

stem: A 65-year-old man with hypertension and intermittent claudication (PVD) has BP 160/95 mmHg. Which antihypertensive is most suitable?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: HTN + PVD/claudication — CCB preferred over beta-blocker
discriminator: Beta-blockers theoretically worsen claudication by reducing cardiac output and peripheral circulation. CCBs are vasculoprotective and preferred in PVD.

stem: A 45-year-old man presents with HTN and hypokalaemia (K+ 3.0 mmol/L), metabolic alkalosis, and suppressed plasma renin activity. CT abdomen shows a 2 cm adrenal adenoma. What is the most appropriate treatment?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Primary hyperaldosteronism — unilateral adenoma treated with adrenalectomy
discriminator: HTN + hypokalaemia + metabolic alkalosis + suppressed renin + adrenal adenoma = primary hyperaldosteronism from aldosterone-producing adenoma (Conn syndrome). Adrenalectomy offers surgical cure.

stem: A 45-year-old man with hypertension develops syncope upon standing. He takes an alpha-blocker for benign prostatic hyperplasia. What is the most likely cause of his syncope?
opts: ACE inhibitor cough leading to vasovagal syncope
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Alpha-blocker side effect — orthostatic hypotension
discriminator: Syncope on standing + taking alpha-blocker (prazosin, doxazosin, terazosin) = orthostatic hypotension, especially after first dose.

stem: A 55-year-old woman has BP readings of 135/85, 132/86, and 130/84 mmHg on three separate visits. She has no comorbidities. What is her BP classification?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: BP staging — stage 1 hypertension (SBP 130-139 or DBP 80-89)
discriminator: Sustained SBP 130-139 or DBP 80-89 = Stage 1 hypertension per ACC/AHA guidelines.

stem: A 60-year-old man with long-standing hypertension has a heaving apex beat in the 5th intercostal space. What is the most likely mechanism of his cardiac change?
opts: Volume overload of the left ventricle
Pressure overload of the left ventricle
Right ventricular hypertrophy from pulmonary hypertension
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Chronic HTN — LV pressure overload → concentric hypertrophy
discriminator: Heaving apex beat = LV pressure overload (concentric hypertrophy). Chronic hypertension increases afterload → LV concentric hypertrophy → heaving apex.

stem: A 60-year-old woman presents with acute-onset dyspnoea, BP 200/120 mmHg, and bilateral crackles on chest auscultation. Chest X-ray shows pulmonary oedema. What is the most appropriate initial management?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Hypertensive emergency with pulmonary oedema — acute HF management
discriminator: HTN emergency + flash pulmonary oedema = acute hypertensive heart failure. IV furosemide (decongestion) + IV nitroglycerin (vasodilation, preload reduction) are first-line.

stem: A 70-year-old man with hypertension and gout has BP 155/92 mmHg despite lifestyle modification. Which antihypertensive should be avoided?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: HTN + gout — avoid thiazide diuretics
discriminator: Thiazide diuretics increase serum uric acid by reducing urate excretion, precipitating gout flares. They should be avoided in patients with gout.

stem: A 35-year-old woman presents with episodic hypertension (BP 200/120 mmHg during spells), headache, palpitations, and diaphoresis. What is the most likely diagnosis?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Secondary hypertension — phaeochromocytoma presentation
discriminator: Episodic severe hypertension + headache + palpitations + diaphoresis = catecholamine excess from phaeochromocytoma. The paroxysmal nature is characteristic.

stem: A 20-year-old man is found to have upper extremity BP of 160/95 mmHg but lower extremity BP of 110/70 mmHg. What cardiac finding is most commonly associated with this condition?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Coarctation of aorta — association with bicuspid aortic valve
discriminator: Upper extremity HTN + lower extremity hypotension = coarctation of aorta. Bicuspid aortic valve is the most common associated cardiac anomaly (present in ~50-85% of coarctation patients).

stem: A 50-year-old woman presents with BP 195/115 mmHg, serum creatinine 2.8 mg/dL (baseline 1.0), and urinalysis shows 2+ protein and red cell casts. She is anuric for 6 hours. What is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Hypertensive emergency with acute kidney injury
Chronic kidney disease with essential hypertension
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Hypertensive emergency — AKI as end-organ damage
discriminator: BP >180/120 + acute rise in creatinine (AKI) + proteinuria + red cell casts = hypertensive emergency with renal end-organ damage (malignant nephrosclerosis).

stem: A 50-year-old woman presents with hypertensive encephalopathy (confusion, BP 220/130 mmHg, papilloedema). Which IV antihypertensive is most appropriate and what is its mechanism?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Hypertensive encephalopathy — IV sodium nitroprusside
discriminator: Sodium nitroprusside is a potent direct arterial and venous vasodilator. It is the classic first-line IV agent for hypertensive encephalopathy. Labetalol and nicardipine are also used.

stem: A 62-year-old man with hypertensive emergency requiring IV therapy develops confusion and agitation after 24 hours of nitroprusside infusion. What complication should be suspected?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Sodium nitroprusside — cyanide toxicity with prolonged use
discriminator: Nitroprusside infusion >24-48 h + confusion/agitation = cyanide toxicity. Nitroprusside is metabolised to cyanide, which can accumulate with prolonged infusion or renal impairment.

stem: A 40-year-old man with hypertension, central obesity, moon face, and wide purplish striae has BP 165/100 mmHg. What is the most likely cause of his hypertension?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Secondary HTN — Cushing syndrome features
discriminator: Central obesity + moon face + wide purple striae + HTN = Cushing syndrome (glucocorticoid excess).

stem: A 22-year-old woman presents with hypertension and radiofemoral delay on examination. What radiographic finding is characteristic of this condition?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Coarctation of aorta — rib notching on CXR
discriminator: Radiofemoral delay + HTN in young = coarctation of aorta. Rib notching on CXR is caused by collateral circulation eroding the inferior borders of ribs.

stem: A 55-year-old woman with hypertension develops bilateral lower extremity oedema while taking amlodipine. What is the mechanism of this side effect?
opts: Sodium and water retention from renal effects
Arteriolar vasodilation with preserved capillary hydrostatic pressure
Left ventricular failure causing pedal oedema
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: CCB side effect — peripheral oedema from arteriolar vasodilation
discriminator: CCBs (especially dihydropyridines like amlodipine) cause preferential arteriolar vasodilation without venodilation. This increases capillary hydrostatic pressure → fluid extravasation → dependent oedema.

stem: A 70-year-old man with hypertension (BP 165/95 mmHg) and type 2 diabetes without proteinuria is started on antihypertensive therapy. What is his recommended BP target?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: BP targets in hypertension with diabetes
discriminator: Most guidelines recommend a BP target of <130/80 mmHg for patients with diabetes (with or without proteinuria) to reduce cardiovascular and renal events.

stem: A 60-year-old man presents with chest pain at rest for 6 hours. ECG shows ST depression of 2 mm in leads V3–V5. Troponin I is elevated at 5 ng/mL. What is the most appropriate initial management?
opts: Oral beta-blocker alone and stress test in 24 hours
IV nitrates and discharge if pain-free
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: NSTEMI → antiplatelet + anticoagulant + early invasive strategy (not fibrinolysis)
discriminator: NSTEMI (ST depression, troponin+) is managed with antiplatelet/anticoagulant therapy and early invasive angiography, NOT fibrinolysis. Fibrinolysis is for STEMI only.

stem: A 55-year-old man with stable angina (exertional chest pain relieved by rest) has a positive stress test showing inferior wall ischemia. He has no high-risk features. What is the most appropriate first-line management?
opts: PCI with stent to the culprit artery
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Stable angina — optimal medical therapy first, not PCI
discriminator: Stable angina with no high-risk features → medical therapy first (BB + CCB + nitrate). PCI does not reduce mortality in stable angina — it relieves symptoms only when medical therapy fails.

stem: A 58-year-old man presents with inferior STEMI. ECG shows ST elevation in II, III, aVF, and ST depression in V2 with a tall R wave in V1. His BP is 90/60 and JVP is elevated. Which of the following is the most important initial management step?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Inferior STEMI + RV involvement (hypotension + elevated JVP) → IV fluids, avoid nitrates
discriminator: Inferior STEMI with RV involvement (ST depression in V2 + tall R in V1, hypotension, elevated JVP) → preload dependent. Nitrates/opiates cause severe hypotension. Give IV fluids first.

stem: A 50-year-old man presents with typical cardiac chest pain at rest for 20 minutes. ECG shows no ST-T changes. Serial troponins are negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Unstable angina = troponin-negative ACS — still requires management
discriminator: Typical cardiac pain at rest + no troponin elevation = unstable angina (UA), not 'no ACS'. UA is ACS without myonecrosis and carries significant risk.

stem: A 70-year-old woman with hypertension, diabetes, and obesity presents with exertional dyspnea. Echocardiogram shows EF 60% with diastolic dysfunction and left ventricular hypertrophy. Which of the following is the most appropriate management for her heart failure?
opts: Diuretics for symptom control + manage comorbidities
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: HFpEF — diuretics + comorbidity management, not ARNI/BB as first-line
discriminator: HFpEF (EF ≥ 50%) management focuses on symptom control (diuretics) and treating comorbidities (HTN, DM, AF). Drugs proven in HFrEF (ARNI, BB, MRA) do not have the same mortality benefit in HFpEF.

stem: A 65-year-old man with known HFrEF presents with acute severe dyspnea, orthopnea, and frothy pink sputum. BP is 160/100, RR 32, SpO2 88% on room air. What is the most appropriate initial management?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Acute pulmonary edema — GTN + NIV first, morphine is not first-line
discriminator: Acute cardiogenic pulmonary edema → GTN (vasodilation, preload reduction) + NIV (positive pressure) first. Morphine is no longer first-line due to risk of respiratory depression.

stem: Which of the following statements about digoxin in heart failure is TRUE?
opts: Digoxin reduces hospitalizations but not mortality
Digoxin is the drug of choice for HFrEF with reduced EF
Digoxin is contraindicated in atrial fibrillation with HF
Digoxin has the strongest mortality benefit of all HF drugs
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Digoxin — symptom and hospitalization benefit only, no mortality benefit
discriminator: Digoxin improves symptoms and reduces HF hospitalizations but does NOT reduce mortality. This distinguishes it from ARNI, BB, and MRA which all have mortality benefit.

stem: A 55-year-old man with HFrEF (EF 30%) on lisinopril, metoprolol, and furosemide remains symptomatic (NYHA II). Which medication has been shown to provide a mortality benefit SUPERIOR to ACE inhibitors in this population?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan) — mortality benefit superior to ACEi in HFrEF
discriminator: PARADIGM-HF: ARNI was superior to enalapril in reducing death and HF hospitalization in HFrEF. ARNI = sacubitril (neprilysin inhibitor) + valsartan (ARB).

stem: A 35-year-old man with known Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) syndrome presents with palpitations. ECG shows atrial fibrillation with a ventricular rate of 220/min and a broad, irregular QRS complex. Which of the following drugs is CONTRAINDICATED?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: WPW + AF — verapamil is contraindicated (risk of VF)
discriminator: Verapamil and other CCBs accelerate accessory pathway conduction in WPW + AF, potentially precipitating ventricular fibrillation. They are contraindicated.

stem: A 45-year-old woman presents with palpitations, dizziness, and BP 85/50. ECG shows a narrow-complex tachycardia at 200/min without visible P waves. What is the most appropriate management?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Unstable SVT — DC cardioversion, not adenosine or drugs
discriminator: Any tachyarrhythmia with hemodynamic instability (hypotension, dizziness) → synchronized DC cardioversion. Adenosine is for stable SVT only.

stem: A 60-year-old man collapses in the hospital ward. The cardiac monitor shows ventricular fibrillation. What is the most appropriate immediate step?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: VF arrest — defibrillate first, amiodarone after 3 shocks
discriminator: VF/pulseless VT → defibrillate immediately. Amiodarone is given after the third shock if VF persists. Defibrillation is the only treatment that terminates VF.

stem: A 25-year-old woman is brought to the ER after ingesting an overdose of tricyclic antidepressants. ECG shows sinus tachycardia with a QRS duration of 140 ms. What is the most appropriate treatment?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: TCA overdose + wide QRS → IV sodium bicarbonate
discriminator: TCA overdose causes Na-channel blockade (wide QRS). Sodium bicarbonate is the specific antidote — it alkalinizes serum and provides Na+ to overcome the blockade.

stem: A 40-year-old woman with hyperthyroidism presents with palpitations and dyspnea. ECG shows atrial fibrillation with a ventricular rate of 140/min. What is the most appropriate rate-control medication?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Thyrotoxic AF — beta-blocker (propranolol) is first-line for rate control
discriminator: Thyrotoxicosis increases beta-adrenergic tone. Beta-blockers (propranolol) address both the tachycardia and the hyperadrenergic symptoms. Digoxin is less effective in high-output states.

stem: A 55-year-old man with known severe aortic stenosis (valve area 0.7 cm², mean gradient 55 mmHg) presents with exertional chest pain. Which of the following diagnostic tests is CONTRAINDICATED?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Severe AS — stress test is contraindicated (risk of syncope, arrest)
discriminator: Severe AS is an absolute contraindication to exercise stress testing. The fixed obstruction prevents cardiac output from increasing, risking syncope and cardiac arrest.

stem: In mitral stenosis, which hemodynamic change occurs FIRST as the valve area narrows?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: MS — LA pressure rises first (LV is protected)
discriminator: Mitral stenosis → LA pressure rises first, not LV pressure. LV is 'protected' from the pressure load (LV pressure may even be low). AS = LV pressure overload; MS = LA pressure overload.

stem: A 58-year-old man develops sudden hypotension and a new harsh holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border with a palpable thrill, 3 days after an inferior STEMI treated with fibrinolysis. What is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Acute mitral regurgitation from papillary muscle rupture
Free wall rupture with cardiac tamponade
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Post-MI VSR — thrill at LLSB differentiates from acute MR
discriminator: Post-infarction VSR: harsh murmur + THRILL at LLSB + shock. Papillary muscle rupture: apical murmur radiating to axilla, no thrill. The thrill is the key discriminator.

stem: A 35-year-old woman with known mitral valve prolapse presents with fever and a new regurgitant murmur. Blood cultures grow gram-positive cocci in chains. What is the most likely causative organism?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: IE in pre-existing valvular disease — most commonly Strep viridans
discriminator: Native valve IE in patients with pre-existing valvular disease is most commonly caused by Streptococcus viridans (oral viridans group streptococci). Staph aureus is more common in prosthetic valves, IVDU, and acute aggressive IE.

stem: Which of the following is the recommended prophylaxis for recurrence of acute rheumatic fever?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G IM every 4 weeks
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: RF prophylaxis — benzathine penicillin G IM every 4 weeks
discriminator: Benzathine penicillin G IM (1.2 million units) every 3–4 weeks is the standard secondary prophylaxis for RF. Oral penicillin is less reliable due to compliance issues.

stem: A 28-year-old pregnant woman at 32 weeks gestation has BP 155/95 on two readings. Urine protein is negative. Which antihypertensive is safest in pregnancy?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: HTN in pregnancy — labetalol is safe (Category A); ACEi/ARB are teratogenic
discriminator: Labetalol (beta-blocker with alpha-blocking activity) is the preferred antihypertensive in pregnancy. ACEi and ARB are absolutely contraindicated (teratogenic, especially in 2nd/3rd trimester).

stem: A 45-year-old man with hypertension and depression is on sertraline. Which antihypertensive is most appropriate considering his depression?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: HTN + depression — avoid beta-blockers (worsen depression), choose CCB
discriminator: Beta-blockers (especially lipophilic ones like propranolol) can worsen depression. CCBs (amlodipine) are neutral and preferred in patients with depression.

stem: A 50-year-old woman presents with the worst headache of her life. CT head shows subarachnoid hemorrhage. She has a history of hypertension. Which calcium channel blocker is indicated to prevent a specific complication?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: SAH — nimodipine prevents cerebral vasospasm
discriminator: Nimodipine is a CCB that crosses the BBB and reduces cerebral vasospasm after SAH. Other CCBs like amlodipine/nifedipine do not have this effect.

stem: A 55-year-old man with hypertension presents with sudden severe tearing chest pain radiating to the back. BP is 210/120 in the right arm and 160/90 in the left arm. Which imaging study is MOST appropriate for definitive diagnosis?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Aortic dissection — CT aortogram is the gold standard; echo may miss
discriminator: CT aortogram is the definitive imaging for aortic dissection. Pulse deficit + BP differential + tearing chest pain = dissection until proven otherwise. Echo may miss if the intimal flap is not well visualized.

stem: For a patient with confirmed acute aortic dissection (Stanford type A), which medication should be given FIRST before vasodilators?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Aortic dissection — beta-blocker first to reduce HR and dP/dt, THEN vasodilator
discriminator: Give IV beta-blocker (esmolol) FIRST to reduce heart rate and dP/dt before vasodilators. Vasodilators alone can cause reflex tachycardia which increases aortic wall stress and propagates the dissection.

stem: A 60-year-old man with HFrEF (EF 30%) and moderate functional mitral regurgitation remains symptomatic on optimal medical therapy. Which of the following has been shown to provide the greatest mortality benefit?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: HFrEF + MR — GDMT (ARNI, not MR intervention) has mortality benefit
discriminator: In HFrEF with functional MR, guideline-directed medical therapy (especially ARNI) reduces mortality. MR is often a consequence of LV dysfunction, and treating the underlying HF reduces MR severity. Mitral valve intervention has not shown mortality benefit in functional MR.

stem: A 35-year-old woman with known mitral stenosis presents with progressive dyspnea. Which of the following hemodynamic changes is the DIRECT consequence of mitral valve obstruction?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: MS — LA pressure increases as a direct consequence of valve obstruction
discriminator: Mitral stenosis directly obstructs LV filling → LA pressure rises. This transmits backward to pulmonary circulation causing symptoms.

stem: Which drug is the first-line rate-control agent for atrial fibrillation in a patient with heart failure?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Which drug is the first-line rate-control agent for atrial fibrillation in a patient with heart failure?
discriminator: AF + HF = digoxin + diuretic. Digoxin provides rate control and positive inotropy. Beta-blockers can worsen acute HF.

stem: A patient with a prosthetic mitral valve develops fever and a new murmur. What is the most likely organism if he had dental work 2 weeks ago?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: A patient with a prosthetic mitral valve develops fever and a new murmur. What is the most likely organism if he had den
discriminator: Dental procedures -> Strep viridans. Prosthetic valve IE <1 year = Staph epidermidis. IVDU = Staph aureus.

stem: Which haemodynamic change distinguishes acute MR from VSR after a STEMI?
opts: Thrill is present in MR, absent in VSR
Thrill is present in VSR, absent in MR
VSR has lower oxygen saturation in the right atrium
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Which haemodynamic change distinguishes acute MR from VSR after a STEMI?
discriminator: VSR produces a thrill at LLSB. Acute MR does not have a thrill. This is the single most important physical exam discriminator.

stem: A 65-year-old with HTN, DM, and proteinuria has BP 160/95 on amlodipine. Which drug should be added?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: A 65-year-old with HTN, DM, and proteinuria has BP 160/95 on amlodipine. Which drug should be added?
discriminator: ACEi provides renoprotection in diabetic nephropathy. It should be first-line in HTN + DM + proteinuria.

stem: Which type of hypersensitivity reaction is responsible for the PPD skin test in TB?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Which type of hypersensitivity reaction is responsible for the PPD skin test in TB?
discriminator: PPD = delayed-type hypersensitivity = Type IV. TB granuloma formation is also Type IV.

stem: In the Cardiology Chapter Map — Core Topics bridge review, which concept is best identified by this discriminator: STEMI -> PCI if <120 min else thrombolysis. NSTEMI -> no thrombolysis. Unstable angina = troponin negative.?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Day 22
discriminator: STEMI -> PCI if <120 min else thrombolysis. NSTEMI -> no thrombolysis. Unstable angina = troponin negative.

stem: A review question gives this trigger: Heart Failure. Which linked concept should you revise first?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Day 23
discriminator: HFrEF = ARNI + BB + MRA. HFpEF = diuretics + comorbidities. Acute pulmonary oedema = GTN + NIV.

stem: Which topic best matches the exam discriminator: Stable narrow = adenosine. Unstable = DC cardio. WPW + AF = no verapamil. VF = shock first.?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Day 24
discriminator: Stable narrow = adenosine. Unstable = DC cardio. WPW + AF = no verapamil. VF = shock first.

stem: A mixed review stem is built around Valvular Disease. Which answer is the intended discriminator pair?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Day 25
discriminator: AS = RUSB, reactive stair to carotids. MS = opening snap, LA pressure rises first. Post-MI + thrill = VSR.

stem: In the Cardiology Chapter Map — Core Topics bridge review, which concept is best identified by this discriminator: DM + proteinuria = ACEi. Pregnant = labetalol. Dissection = CT + BB first. SAH = nimodipine.?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Day 26
discriminator: DM + proteinuria = ACEi. Pregnant = labetalol. Dissection = CT + BB first. SAH = nimodipine.

stem: A review question gives this trigger: Yes — superior to ACEi. Which linked concept should you revise first?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Sacubitril/valsartan (ARNI)
discriminator: Neprilysin inhibition + ARB

stem: Which topic best matches the exam discriminator: Reduces remodelling, HR, O2 demand?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Beta-blocker (bisoprolol, carvedilol)
discriminator: Reduces remodelling, HR, O2 demand

stem: A mixed review stem is built around Yes. Which answer is the intended discriminator pair?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: MRA (spironolactone, eplerenone)
discriminator: Aldosterone blockade

stem: In the Cross-Reference: Heart Failure Drug Mortality Benefit bridge review, which concept is best identified by this discriminator: Afterload reduction, remodelling?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: ACEi / ARB
discriminator: Afterload reduction, remodelling

stem: A review question gives this trigger: No — symptom only. Which linked concept should you revise first?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Digoxin
discriminator: Inotrope + rate control

stem: Which topic best matches the exam discriminator: Diuresis (decongestion)?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Furosemide
discriminator: Diuresis (decongestion)

stem: A mixed review stem is built around LV pressure overload. Which answer is the intended discriminator pair?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Aortic stenosis
discriminator: Ejection systolic RUSB, slow-rising pulse

stem: In the Cross-Reference: Valvular Lesion Haemodynamics bridge review, which concept is best identified by this discriminator: Early diastolic murmur, water-hammer pulse?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Aortic regurgitation
discriminator: Early diastolic murmur, water-hammer pulse

stem: A review question gives this trigger: LA pressure rises first. Which linked concept should you revise first?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Mitral stenosis
discriminator: Mid-diastolic rumble, opening snap

stem: Which topic best matches the exam discriminator: Pansystolic apex radiating to axilla?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Mitral regurgitation
discriminator: Pansystolic apex radiating to axilla

stem: A mixed review stem is built around Left-to-right shunt. Which answer is the intended discriminator pair?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: VSR (post-MI)
discriminator: Pansystolic LLSB WITH thrill

stem: In the Cross-Reference: Antiarrhythmics by Vaughan Williams bridge review, which concept is best identified by this discriminator: Prolong QRS + QTc?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Ia (Na channel blockers)
discriminator: Prolong QRS + QTc

stem: A review question gives this trigger: Lidocaine, mexiletine. Which linked concept should you revise first?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Ib
discriminator: VT post-MI (less used now)

stem: Which topic best matches the exam discriminator: AF conversion in WPW?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: Ic
discriminator: AF conversion in WPW

stem: A mixed review stem is built around Propranolol, metoprolol, bisoprolol. Which answer is the intended discriminator pair?
subject: Medicine-Cardiology
concept: II (BB)
discriminator: Rate control, thyrotoxic AF

stem: A 55-year-old chronic smoker presents with abrupt onset of fever, chills, and rusty-coloured sputum for 3 days. Chest radiograph shows dense lobar consolidation of the right upper lobe. Gram stain of sputum shows Gram-positive lancet-shaped diplococci. Which of the following is the most likely causative organism?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Most common causative organism of community-acquired pneumonia
discriminator: Rusty sputum + lancet-shaped GPC diplococci + lobar consolidation → Strep pneumoniae

stem: A 62-year-old with COPD presents with acute exacerbation and suspected pneumonia. Sputum culture on blood agar shows no growth, but growth is observed on chocolate agar. Which of the following best explains this culture pattern?
opts: The organism requires factor X (hemin) and factor V (NAD), which are only present in chocolate agar
The organism is an obligate intracellular pathogen that cannot grow on routine media
Blood agar inhibits the growth of this Gram-negative coccobacillus
The organism requires BCYE agar for culture
The organism is a fastidious anaerobe killed by oxygen in blood agar
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Haemophilus influenzae growth requirements (factor X and V)
discriminator: No growth on blood agar + growth on chocolate agar → H. influenzae requires X+V factors present in chocolate agar

stem: A 50-year-old chronic alcoholic is brought to the ER with high-grade fever, rigors, and production of thick, gelatinous, bloody sputum. CXR shows dense consolidation in the right upper lobe with a bulging fissure sign. Which organism is most likely responsible?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Klebsiella pneumonia — currant-jelly sputum and bulging fissure sign
discriminator: Alcoholic patient + currant-jelly sputum + bulging fissure sign → Klebsiella pneumoniae

stem: A 22-year-old medical student presents with dry cough, fever, and headache for one week. CXR shows bilateral patchy infiltrates. Cold agglutinins are positive. Which of the following extrapulmonary manifestations is most specifically associated with this infection?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Mycoplasma pneumoniae — extrapulmonary manifestations
discriminator: Young adult + dry cough + bilateral patchy infiltrates + cold agglutinins → Mycoplasma; haemolytic anaemia and erythema multiforme are classic extrapulmonary features

stem: A 30-year-old man is diagnosed with sputum smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis. Which of the following is the correct intensive-phase regimen?
opts: Rifampicin + Isoniazid + Pyrazinamide + Ethambutol for 2 months
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Standard TB intensive-phase regimen (RHZE)
discriminator: Active pulmonary TB requires 4-drug intensive phase (RHZE) × 2 months, then 2-drug continuation (RH) × 4 months

stem: A 60-year-old man with severe pneumonia is intubated and mechanically ventilated. Despite ventilation with 100% FiO₂, his arterial PaO₂ remains at 55 mmHg. Which of the following best explains this finding?
opts: Intrapulmonary shunt due to consolidated lung tissue
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Refractory hypoxaemia with 100% O₂ = intrapulmonary shunt
discriminator: PaO₂ does not improve with 100% FiO₂ → shunt physiology (blood bypasses ventilated alveoli entirely), NOT V/Q mismatch

stem: A 35-year-old woman on anti-tuberculosis therapy for 2 months develops a tingling sensation and numbness in both feet, with difficulty walking. Which drug is most likely responsible?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Isoniazid-induced peripheral neuropathy — pyridoxine (B6) deficiency
discriminator: Bilateral symmetrical peripheral neuropathy after 2 months of ATT → INH-induced B6 deficiency

stem: A patient on rifampicin develops reddish-orange discolouration of urine and sweat. He is also noted to have elevated liver enzymes. Which of the following statements about rifampicin is correct?
opts: It causes orange-red discolouration of body fluids and is hepatotoxic
It causes orange-red discolouration only of urine; sweat is unaffected
It causes hyperuricaemia leading to gout
The discolouration indicates haemolysis and requires immediate drug cessation
It is safe in patients with pre-existing liver disease
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Rifampicin side effects — orange secretions and hepatotoxicity
discriminator: Rifampicin causes orange-red discolouration of all body fluids (urine, sweat, tears, saliva) and is hepatotoxic (can cause hepatitis)

stem: A 40-year-old immunocompromised patient presents with fever, night sweats, and weight loss over 4 weeks. CXR shows bilateral diffuse tiny nodular opacities (1-2 mm) scattered throughout both lung fields in a millet-seed pattern. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Miliary TB — millet-seed nodules on CXR, haematogenous spread
discriminator: Immunocompromised + constitutional symptoms + millet-seed (1-2 mm) diffuse nodules on CXR → miliary TB

stem: A mother asks whether the BCG vaccine will protect her 10-year-old son from getting pulmonary tuberculosis later in life. Which of the following is the most accurate statement about BCG vaccine efficacy?
opts: It effectively prevents miliary TB and TB meningitis in children, but has variable efficacy against adult pulmonary TB
It provides complete protection against all forms of TB in all age groups
It is effective only against drug-resistant strains of TB
It prevents reactivation of latent TB in adults
It is ineffective and no longer recommended by WHO
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: BCG vaccine — limitations and efficacy spectrum
discriminator: BCG prevents severe childhood TB (miliary, meningitis) but not adult pulmonary reactivation

stem: A lung biopsy from a patient with suspected TB shows granulomatous inflammation with central caseating necrosis. Numerous acid-fast bacilli are seen on Ziehl-Neelsen stain. Which type of hypersensitivity reaction is primarily responsible for this tissue response?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: TB granuloma formation — Type IV hypersensitivity
discriminator: Caseating granulomas with AFB+ → cell-mediated immunity → Type IV hypersensitivity

stem: A 3-year-old child accidentally ingests kerosene oil stored in a soft drink bottle. The mother calls the emergency helpline. Which of the following is the most dangerous complication of kerosene ingestion?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Kerosene/hydrocarbon aspiration — most dangerous complication
discriminator: Hydrocarbon ingestion → aspiration bronchopneumonia (NOT hepatic/renal failure); do NOT induce vomiting

stem: A patient on anti-tuberculosis therapy for 3 weeks develops acute-onset pain and swelling in both ankles and knees. Serum uric acid is elevated. Which drug is most likely responsible?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Pyrazinamide — hyperuricaemia and gout-like arthralgia
discriminator: ATT at 3 weeks + joint pains + high uric acid → pyrazinamide

stem: A 70-year-old man who was admitted for stroke develops fever and productive cough 72 hours after admission. CXR shows a new left lower lobe infiltrate. Which of the following best classifies this pneumonia?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Hospital-acquired pneumonia — definition (≥48 hours after admission)
discriminator: Pneumonia developing ≥48 hours after hospital admission = HAP

stem: A 10-year-old asymptomatic child is found to have a calcified nodule in the right upper lobe with ipsilateral hilar lymph node calcification on a routine CXR. She has no history of TB treatment. Which of the following best describes this finding?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Primary TB — Ghon complex (parenchymal focus + hilar lymphadenopathy → calcification)
discriminator: Asymptomatic child + calcified parenchymal nodule + calcified hilar LN = healed Ghon complex

stem: A 55-year-old man presents with pneumonia, profuse watery diarrhoea, and confusion. He mentions he recently serviced an air conditioning cooling tower. Serum sodium is 125 mEq/L. Which organism is most likely responsible?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Legionella pneumophila — water exposure, diarrhoea, hyponatraemia
discriminator: Water/aerosol exposure + diarrhoea + hyponatraemia + confusion → Legionella

stem: Which of the following best defines multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB)?
opts: Resistance to at least isoniazid and rifampicin
Resistance to any one first-line anti-TB drug
Resistance to all first-line anti-TB drugs
Resistance to isoniazid, rifampicin, and any fluoroquinolone
Resistance to second-line injectable drugs only
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: MDR-TB definition — resistance to INH + rifampicin
discriminator: MDR-TB = resistance to the two most potent first-line drugs: isoniazid AND rifampicin

stem: A 45-year-old man who underwent splenectomy after a road traffic accident 2 years ago presents with fever, chills, and rusty sputum. CXR shows left lower lobe consolidation. Which of the following organisms is most likely responsible?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Post-splenectomy OPSI — most common cause is Strep pneumoniae (encapsulated organism)
discriminator: Post-splenectomy + rusty sputum + consolidation → encapsulated organism → Strep pneumoniae (OPSI)

stem: A 60-year-old woman develops high fever, cough with purulent sputum, and respiratory distress 5 days after recovering from influenza. CXR shows multilobar infiltrates with multiple cavities. Which organism is most likely responsible?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Post-influenza necrotizing pneumonia — Staphylococcus aureus
discriminator: Post-influenza + cavitating multilobar pneumonia → Staph aureus necrotizing pneumonia

stem: A 30-year-old HIV-positive man presents with subacute headache, fever, and neck stiffness for 2 weeks. CSF analysis shows lymphocytic pleocytosis (200 cells/µL), low glucose (20 mg/dL), and elevated protein (200 mg/dL). Which of the following should be added to his treatment regimen?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: TB meningitis — CSF profile and adjunctive dexamethasone
discriminator: Lymphocytic meningitis + low glucose + high protein in HIV patient → TB meningitis; add dexamethasone

stem: A 75-year-old man with advanced Parkinson's disease and dysphagia presents with fever and cough. He is found to have right lower lobe consolidation. Which of the following best describes the likely microbiology of this pneumonia?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Aspiration pneumonia — dependent lobe involvement, anaerobic/oropharyngeal flora
discriminator: Dysphagia (Parkinson's) + dependent lobe (RLL) → aspiration pneumonia → anaerobic/oropharyngeal flora

stem: A 78-year-old woman with pneumonia presents with confusion, BP 85/55 mmHg, respiratory rate 32/min, and BUN 30 mg/dL (equivalent to urea 10.7 mmol/L). Her CURB-65 score is calculated. Based on the score, which of the following is the most appropriate management?
opts: Admit to ICU as she has a CURB-65 score of 4
Treat as outpatient with oral antibiotics (CURB-65 = 1)
No antibiotics needed as this is viral pneumonia
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: CURB-65 scoring — all components equal weight, score ≥3 = severe pneumonia, consider ICU
discriminator: Confusion (1) + BP <90/60 (1) + RR ≥30 (1) + Urea >7 (1) + Age ≥65 (1) = 5/5 → severe → ICU

stem: A 32-year-old woman on standard 4-drug ATT for pulmonary TB develops jaundice and elevated liver enzymes (ALT 450 U/L) after 3 weeks of therapy. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
opts: Stop all anti-TB drugs immediately and re-challenge with INH first once liver enzymes normalise
Continue all drugs and add hepatoprotective agents
Reduce the dose of rifampicin only
Continue isoniazid and rifampicin but stop pyrazinamide and ethambutol
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: ATT-induced hepatitis — stop all drugs, re-challenge sequentially starting with INH
discriminator: Jaundice + high ALT on ATT → drug-induced hepatitis → STOP all drugs, then re-challenge one by one

stem: A 28-year-old man presents with cough, purulent sputum, hemoptysis, fever, and significant weight loss over 2 months. CXR shows a cavitating lesion in the right upper lobe. Sputum AFB smear is positive. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
opts: Rifampicin + Isoniazid + Pyrazinamide + Ethambutol (RHZE) for 2 months, then Rifampicin + Isoniazid for 4 months
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Active cavitary pulmonary TB — standard RHZE regimen
discriminator: Cavitating RUL + hemoptysis + weight loss + AFB+ → active pulmonary TB → standard RHZE × 2 then RH × 4

stem: Which anti-tuberculosis drug is most commonly associated with hyperuricaemia and gout-like joint pain?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Pyrazinamide — hyperuricaemia and gout-like arthralgia (recall)
discriminator: Hyperuricaemia + arthralgia is the classic PZA side effect signature

stem: A 30-year-old woman with known asthma on PRN salbutamol has daytime symptoms 4 times per week and nocturnal symptoms twice per month. FEV1 is 78% predicted. According to GINA, what is the next step in management?
opts: Add low-dose ICS + LABA to PRN SABA
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: GINA step-up — symptoms >2x/week = step 3 (add LABA to ICS)
discriminator: Day symptoms >2x/week + preserved FEV1 (>70%) = GINA step 3: add LABA to low-dose ICS. Step 1 is PRN SABA; step 2 is low-dose ICS; step 3 adds LABA.

stem: A 22-year-old woman presents with acute severe asthma. She cannot complete sentences, respiratory rate is 32/min, heart rate 120/min, SpO2 88% on room air, and PEF is 40% of predicted. What is the single most important first-line treatment?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Acute severe asthma — nebulised SABA with oxygen is first-line
discriminator: Acute severe asthma (PEF 33-50%, cannot complete sentences) → first-line: inhaled SABA (salbutamol) via nebuliser with supplemental oxygen.

stem: A 40-year-old woman with acute severe asthma has not improved after nebulised salbutamol, ipratropium, and IV hydrocortisone. PEF remains 35% predicted. What is the next best step?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Acute asthma refractory to initial therapy — IV MgSO4
discriminator: Refractory bronchospasm after maximal SABA + ipratropium + steroid → IV MgSO4 is the next step before considering intubation.

stem: A 55-year-old man with a 40 pack-year smoking history presents with progressive dyspnoea and chronic cough productive of sputum for 3 years. Spirometry: FEV1/FVC 0.65, FEV1 55% predicted, with no significant reversibility after bronchodilator. What is the most likely diagnosis?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: COPD diagnosis — smoking + chronic cough + irreversible FEV1/FVC <0.7
discriminator: Smoking history + chronic productive cough ≥3 months × 2 years + FEV1/FVC <0.70 with no reversibility = COPD.

stem: A 65-year-old man with known COPD has FEV1 38% predicted, FEV1/FVC 0.52, CAT score 22, and 3 exacerbations in the past year. What are his GOLD spirometry grade and group?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: GOLD classification — grade by FEV1%, group by exacerbations + symptoms
discriminator: FEV1 30-49% = GOLD 3. ≥2 exacerbations/year + CAT ≥10 = Group D. These two axes are independent.

stem: A 55-year-old man with COPD exacerbation presents with drowsiness. ABG: pH 7.28, PaO2 52 mmHg, PaCO2 72 mmHg. He is rousable and has no contraindications. What is the single best next step?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: COPD exacerbation with respiratory acidosis — NIV is first-line
discriminator: pH 7.25-7.35 + hypercapnia (PaCO2 >45) + drowsy but rousable = indication for NIV (BiPAP). Intubation is for NIV failure or contraindications.

stem: A 60-year-old man with COPD exacerbation is started on controlled oxygen therapy. Which SpO2 target is most appropriate?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: COPD exacerbation — controlled oxygen target SpO2 88-92%
discriminator: In COPD exacerbations, the target SpO2 is 88-92%. Higher targets risk hypercapnic respiratory failure by blunting hypoxic drive.

stem: A 65-year-old man with COPD presents with pleuritic chest pain, acute dyspnoea, and hypoxia. D-dimer is elevated. What is the most important differential diagnosis to rule out?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Dyspnoea differential in COPD — PE is a critical mimic
discriminator: COPD exacerbation-like presentation + pleuritic chest pain + hypoxia + elevated D-dimer = rule out PE. COPD patients are at increased risk of PE, which can mimic an exacerbation.

stem: A nursing home resident using an inhaled corticosteroid inhaler develops white curd-like plaques in the oral cavity. What is the most likely diagnosis?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: ICS complication — oropharyngeal candidiasis
discriminator: White curd-like plaques (pseudomembranous candidiasis) that can be scraped off, in a patient using inhaled corticosteroids = oropharyngeal candidiasis.

stem: A 50-year-old man with COPD develops right heart failure with elevated JVP, pedal oedema, and hepatomegaly. He has no orthopnoea or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea. What is the most likely diagnosis?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Cor pulmonale — right heart failure from lung disease, no orthopnoea
discriminator: COPD + right HF signs (JVP, oedema, hepatomegaly) + absence of orthopnoea/PND = cor pulmonale. The absence of orthopnoea distinguishes right from left heart failure.

stem: ABG: pH 7.48, PaCO2 30 mmHg, PaO2 85 mmHg, HCO3 24 mmol/L. What is the acid-base interpretation?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: ABG interpretation — respiratory alkalosis from hyperventilation
discriminator: pH >7.45 (alkalemia) + PaCO2 <35 (low CO2) = respiratory alkalosis. HCO3 normal = no metabolic compensation yet.

stem: ABG: pH 7.25, PaCO2 70 mmHg, PaO2 55 mmHg, HCO3 30 mmol/L. What is the acid-base interpretation?
opts: Chronic respiratory acidosis with acute exacerbation
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: ABG — acute-on-chronic respiratory acidosis in COPD
discriminator: Low pH (acidemia) + high PaCO2 (hypercapnia) = respiratory acidosis. HCO3 is elevated (30) indicating chronic compensation, but pH is still low suggesting acute-on-chronic exacerbation.

stem: A 35-year-old nonsmoker presents with dyspnoea and cough. Spirometry: FEV1/FVC 0.82, FVC 60% predicted, FEV1 58% predicted. What pattern of lung disease is this?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Spirometry — restrictive pattern (normal/increased FEV1/FVC with reduced FVC)
discriminator: FEV1/FVC ≥0.70 (normal or increased) + reduced FVC (<80%) = restrictive pattern. This suggests reduced lung volumes without airway obstruction.

stem: A 45-year-old man with asthma is well-controlled on low-dose ICS-formoterol as maintenance and reliever therapy (MART). He now has daytime symptoms twice daily and nocturnal awakenings 3 times per week. FEV1 is 65% predicted. What is the next GINA step?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: GINA step 4 — increase to medium-dose ICS-LABA
discriminator: Symptoms uncontrolled on low-dose ICS-LABA (MART) → medium-dose ICS-LABA is the next step (GINA step 4).

stem: A 55-year-old man with COPD exacerbation has purulent sputum, increased dyspnoea, and fever. What antibiotic should be added to his bronchodilator and steroid therapy?
opts: Antibiotics are not indicated for COPD exacerbations
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: COPD exacerbation — antibiotics for purulent sputum
discriminator: COPD exacerbation + purulent sputum = bacterial infection likely → antibiotics indicated. First-line: amoxicillin/clavulanate or doxycycline.

stem: A 50-year-old man with COPD on LABA + LAMA + ICS continues to have >2 exacerbations per year. His blood eosinophil count is 400 cells/µL. What adjustment to therapy is most likely to reduce exacerbations?
opts: Stop ICS to reduce pneumonia risk
Continue ICS as blood eosinophils ≥300 predict ICS response
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: COPD — ICS indication based on blood eosinophil count
discriminator: Blood eosinophils ≥300 cells/µL predict good response to ICS for exacerbation reduction in COPD. This patient has eosinophils 400 → continue/add ICS.

stem: A 35-year-old woman with asthma has FEV1 55% predicted, FEV1/FVC 0.65 during an acute attack. After treatment with bronchodilators, FEV1 improves to 80% predicted and FEV1/FVC to 0.78. What does this indicate?
opts: Reversible airway obstruction characteristic of asthma
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Asthma — reversible airway obstruction on spirometry
discriminator: Significant improvement (>12% and >200 mL increase in FEV1) after bronchodilator = reversible obstruction, hallmark of asthma.

stem: A 60-year-old man with a 30 pack-year smoking history presents with progressive dyspnoea. His DLCO (diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide) is significantly reduced. What pattern of COPD does this most likely reflect?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: DLCO — reduced in emphysema (alveolar destruction), normal in chronic bronchitis
discriminator: Low DLCO indicates alveolar destruction (emphysema). Chronic bronchitis has normal DLCO as the alveoli are intact.

stem: A 45-year-old man with no smoking history presents with progressive dyspnoea and is found to have emphysema on high-resolution CT. What laboratory test should be ordered?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency — early-onset emphysema in nonsmoker
discriminator: Emphysema in a young nonsmoker → suspect alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency. This genetic disorder causes early-onset panacinar emphysema.

stem: A 60-year-old man with COPD (GOLD 3, Group D) on LABA + LAMA + ICS continues to have frequent exacerbations. Smoking cessation is his top priority. Which pharmacotherapy for smoking cessation has the highest efficacy?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Smoking cessation — varenicline has highest efficacy
discriminator: Varenicline (nicotinic receptor partial agonist) has the highest abstinence rates among smoking cessation pharmacotherapies.

stem: A 22-year-old woman with asthma presents with acute dyspnoea, PEF 30% of predicted, SpO2 85% on room air. She is silent on auscultation (no wheeze) and appears exhausted. What is the classification of this exacerbation?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Life-threatening asthma — silent chest, exhaustion, PEF <33%
discriminator: Silent chest (no wheeze = severely reduced airflow) + exhaustion + PEF <33% + SpO2 <90% = life-threatening asthma. Immediate intubation may be needed.

stem: A 65-year-old man with COPD has chronic hypoxaemia (PaO2 52 mmHg on room air). He is a former smoker. What intervention improves survival in hypoxaemic COPD?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: COPD — long-term oxygen therapy improves survival in chronic hypoxaemia
discriminator: Chronic severe hypoxaemia (PaO2 ≤55 mmHg or SpO2 ≤88%) in COPD is an indication for LTOT (>15 h/day), which is the only therapy proven to improve survival in these patients.

stem: A 25-year-old woman with asthma on high-dose ICS-LABA presents with persistent symptoms and frequent exacerbations. She has a history of nasal polyps and aspirin sensitivity. What add-on biologic therapy is most appropriate?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Asthma biologics — omalizumab for allergic asthma with raised IgE
discriminator: Asthma + nasal polyps + aspirin sensitivity + persistent symptoms despite high-dose ICS-LABA → consider omalizumab if elevated IgE and allergic phenotype.

stem: A 55-year-old man with COPD exacerbation was treated with controlled oxygen, bronchodilators, steroids, and antibiotics. Despite initial improvement, he develops progressive drowsiness. ABG now: pH 7.20, PaCO2 85 mmHg, PaO2 60 mmHg on 2 L O2. What is the most appropriate next step?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: COPD exacerbation — NIV failure/intubation criteria
discriminator: pH <7.25 (7.20) + worsening hypercapnia (PaCO2 85) + drowsy despite initial treatment = NIV failure or contraindication. pH <7.25 with altered consciousness is an indication for invasive mechanical ventilation.

stem: A 50-year-old man with chronic cough and dyspnoea has FVC 80% predicted, FEV1 50% predicted, and FEV1/FVC 0.63, with no significant reversibility. He has had 2 exacerbations in the past year and CAT score is 8. What are his GOLD grade and group?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: GOLD classification — grade by FEV1%, group by exacerbations + symptom score
discriminator: FEV1 50% = GOLD 2. CAT 8 (<10) = low symptoms. 2 exacerbations/year ≥2 = Group C (low symptoms + high exacerbation risk).

stem: A 60-year-old man presents with progressive dyspnoea. On examination, there is stony dullness to percussion over the right hemithorax and the trachea is deviated to the left. What is the most likely diagnosis?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Pleural effusion — clinical signs: dullness + tracheal deviation away
discriminator: Stony dullness + trachea deviated to the opposite side is the classic sign of a pleural effusion. Tension pneumothorax is hyperresonant, not dull.

stem: A 45-year-old man with cirrhosis presents with bilateral pleural effusions. Thoracentesis is performed. Pleural fluid protein is 2.2 g/dL, serum protein is 6.5 g/dL. Pleural LDH is 120 U/L (serum ULN 200 U/L). Which of the following best classifies this effusion?
opts: Transudate — does not meet Light criteria
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Light criteria — exudate vs transudate classification
discriminator: Pleural/serum protein ratio = 2.2/6.5 = 0.34 (< 0.5). Pleural/serum LDH ratio = 120/200 = 0.6 (not > 0.6). Pleural LDH 120 vs 2/3 ULN = 133 — so < 133. None of the three Light criteria are met → transudate.

stem: A 28-year-old tall, thin male presents with sudden-onset severe dyspnoea and right-sided pleuritic chest pain while resting. He has no significant medical history. On examination, breath sounds are absent on the right with hyperresonance. Trachea is central. Blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg. What is the most likely diagnosis?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Primary spontaneous pneumothorax — risk factors and presentation
discriminator: Tall thin young male + sudden pleuritic pain + absent breath sounds + hyperresonance + normal trachea (no shift) = primary spontaneous pneumothorax (non-tension).

stem: A 30-year-old man sustains a stab wound to the left chest. On examination, there is a sucking sound from the wound with respiration. He is in respiratory distress. What is the single best next step in management?
opts: Perform needle decompression at 2nd ICS MCL
Apply a pressure dressing over the wound
Obtain a CXR before any intervention
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Open pneumothorax (sucking chest wound) — immediate management
discriminator: Sucking chest wound = open pneumothorax. The first step is to convert it to a simple pneumothorax using a three-sided occlusive dressing (seals on three sides, flaps on the fourth to let air escape).

stem: A 55-year-old man with known COPD presents with acute dyspnoea. CXR shows a 3 cm rim of air in the right pleural space with the lung edge visible. He is comfortable at rest but becomes short of breath on walking. What is the most appropriate management?
opts: Observation with interval CXR in 4 hours
Needle aspiration or chest tube drainage
Immediate needle decompression at 2nd ICS MCL
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Secondary spontaneous pneumothorax — management based on size and reserve
discriminator: COPD patient with a > 2 cm pneumothorax and symptoms = secondary pneumothorax with poor reserve. Even small pneumothoraces in COPD need drainage because of limited pulmonary reserve.

stem: A 65-year-old woman with a history of colon cancer presents with progressive dyspnoea. CXR shows a large right pleural effusion. Thoracentesis is performed. What is the single best first test on the pleural fluid to determine if this is malignant?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Malignant effusion — first diagnostic test is cytology
discriminator: In a patient with known cancer and a new pleural effusion, cytology on pleural fluid is the first and most specific test for malignant effusion.

stem: A 24-year-old woman presents with productive cough, high-grade fever, and right pleuritic chest pain for 10 days. She has been on oral amoxicillin and then co-amoxiclav with no improvement. CXR shows a loculated right pleural effusion. What is the most likely diagnosis?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Empyema — failure of pneumonia to respond to antibiotics
discriminator: Pneumonia not responding to multiple antibiotics + persistent fever + loculated effusion = empyema until proven otherwise.

stem: A 40-year-old man is brought to the ED after a road traffic accident. He is hypotensive with distended neck veins. Breath sounds are absent on the left with hyperresonance and the trachea is deviated to the right. What is the single best next step?
opts: Immediate needle decompression at 2nd ICS MCL on the left
Insert a chest tube at 4th-5th ICS triangle of safety
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Tension pneumothorax — clinical diagnosis, do not wait for CXR
discriminator: Hypotension + distended neck veins + absent breath sounds + hyperresonance + tracheal deviation away = TENSION pneumothorax. This is a clinical diagnosis — needle decompression immediately, no CXR.

stem: A 50-year-old man with empyema is being managed with IV antibiotics. Which of the following is the most important additional intervention?
opts: Switch to a different antibiotic class
Chest tube drainage of the pleural space
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Empyema — drainage is mandatory in addition to antibiotics
discriminator: Empyema = pus in the pleural space. Antibiotics alone are insufficient because they cannot penetrate the loculated pus. Chest tube drainage is essential.

stem: A 62-year-old woman with breast cancer presents with recurrent right pleural effusion that is symptomatic despite two therapeutic thoracenteses. What is the most appropriate definitive management?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Recurrent malignant effusion — pleurodesis
discriminator: Recurrent symptomatic malignant effusion after drainage → pleurodesis to obliterate the pleural space and prevent re-accumulation.

stem: A 35-year-old man with a primary spontaneous pneumothorax has a 1.5 cm apical rim on CXR and is asymptomatic. What is the most appropriate management?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Primary spontaneous pneumothorax — small asymptomatic: observe
discriminator: Small (< 2 cm rim), asymptomatic primary spontaneous pneumothorax → observation with interval CXR. No intervention required.

stem: A 70-year-old man presents with sudden dyspnoea, hypotension, and distended neck veins. CXR shows a widened mediastinum but no pneumothorax. What is the most likely diagnosis?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Mediastinal widening = tamponade, not tension pneumothorax
discriminator: Mediastinal WIDENING + hypotension + distended neck veins + no pneumothorax = cardiac tamponade. Tension pneumothorax causes mediastinal SHIFT (tracheal deviation), not widening.

stem: A 65-year-old man with COPD and a 40-pack-year smoking history presents with dyspnoea and right pleuritic chest pain. CXR shows a 1 cm rim of air in the right pleural space. He is comfortable at rest with oxygen saturation of 94% on room air. What is the most appropriate management?
opts: Observation with interval CXR in 6 hours
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Secondary spontaneous pneumothorax — chest tube even if small
discriminator: This is a secondary pneumothorax (COPD background). Even though the rim is < 2 cm and the patient is currently comfortable, secondary pneumothorax requires chest tube drainage because patients have minimal pulmonary reserve.

stem: Which of the following is the correct anatomical site for chest tube insertion?
opts: 4th-5th intercostal space, mid to anterior axillary line
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Chest drain insertion — triangle of safety landmarks
discriminator: Chest drain (chest tube) insertion is at the 4th-5th ICS, mid to anterior axillary line — the triangle of safety. The 2nd ICS MCL is for needle DECOMPRESSION, not chest tube.

stem: A 30-year-old man undergoes diagnostic thoracentesis for a pleural effusion. To avoid injury to the intercostal neurovascular bundle, the needle should be inserted:
opts: At the midpoint between the ribs
Directly through the intercostal space laterally
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Thoracentesis — above the rib to avoid neurovascular bundle
discriminator: The intercostal neurovascular bundle runs in the costal groove at the inferior edge of each rib. Needle insertion above the rib avoids injury.

stem: A 68-year-old man with congestive heart failure presents with bilateral pleural effusions. He is in mild respiratory distress. Which of the following pleural fluid findings would be most consistent with a transudative effusion?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Transudate vs exudate — pleural fluid characteristics
discriminator: Transudates have low protein (< 3 g/dL) and low LDH. CHF is a classic cause of transudative effusion. Option B has protein 2.0 (< 3) and low LDH — consistent with transudate.

stem: A 22-year-old tall, thin male presents with sudden-onset left pleuritic chest pain and mild dyspnoea. CXR shows a 3.5 cm rim of air in the left pleural space. He is in mild distress but hemodynamically stable. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
opts: Needle aspiration or chest tube drainage
Immediate needle decompression at 2nd ICS MCL
CT chest to assess for blebs
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Primary spontaneous pneumothorax — large/symptomatic → aspiration or drain
discriminator: Primary spontaneous pneumothorax with > 2 cm rim AND symptoms → needs intervention. Needle aspiration or small-bore chest tube drainage is appropriate.

stem: A child presents with acute dyspnoea following a choking episode. On examination, chest movements are reduced on the left, breath sounds are absent, the left hemithorax is hyperresonant and appears black on CXR with mediastinal deviation to the right. What is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Foreign body aspiration with right main bronchus obstruction
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Tension pneumothorax in children — same clinical features
discriminator: Reduced chest movements + absent breath sounds + hyperresonance + black hemithorax + mediastinal deviation = tension pneumothorax. The hyperresonance differentiates it from effusion (dullness).

stem: A 55-year-old woman presents with dyspnoea and dullness over the right lower chest. CXR shows a right pleural effusion. She completed treatment for pulmonary tuberculosis 2 years ago. Thoracentesis yields fluid with protein 4.5 g/dL, LDH 300 U/L (serum ULN 200). Pleural/serum protein ratio is 0.6. Which of the following best describes this effusion?
opts: Transudate — does not meet Light criteria
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Light criteria application — exudate determination
discriminator: Pleural/serum protein ratio = 0.6 (> 0.5) → Light criterion (1) is met. This alone makes it an exudate regardless of LDH values.

stem: A 45-year-old man with pneumonia develops a pleural effusion. Thoracentesis reveals frank pus. Gram stain shows Gram-positive cocci in chains. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
opts: Insert a chest tube and start IV antibiotics
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Empyema — frank pus = immediate chest tube + antibiotics
discriminator: Frank pus on thoracentesis = empyema. Immediate chest tube drainage + IV antibiotics are mandatory. Antibiotics alone are insufficient.

stem: A 38-year-old man presents with sudden dyspnoea, hypotension, and distended neck veins 12 hours after a central line insertion. Breath sounds are absent on the right with hyperresonance. What is the single best next step?
opts: Needle decompression at 2nd ICS MCL on the right
Insert chest tube at 4th-5th ICS triangle of safety
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Iatrogenic tension pneumothorax — clinical diagnosis, immediate decompression
discriminator: Central line insertion is a known cause of iatrogenic pneumothorax. Hypotension + distended neck veins + absent breath sounds + hyperresonance = tension pneumothorax. CLINICAL diagnosis — do not wait for imaging.

stem: A 60-year-old man with right pleural effusion undergoes diagnostic thoracentesis at the 7th-8th ICS posteriorly. The needle is inserted at the upper border of the 8th rib. Which anatomical structure is the needle most likely to avoid?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Thoracentesis — above the rib avoids intercostal bundle
discriminator: The needle inserted above the rib (upper border of 8th rib) avoids the intercostal neurovascular bundle, which runs in the costal groove at the INFERIOR border of the rib above (8th rib's inferior border).

stem: A 50-year-old man with left pleural effusion has pleural fluid analysis showing: protein 3.8 g/dL, LDH 260 U/L, glucose 25 mg/dL, pH 7.1. Which combination of diagnoses is most likely?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Exudative effusion — low pH and low glucose: malignancy or empyema
discriminator: Low pleural glucose (< 60 mg/dL) and low pH (< 7.2) in an exudative effusion are classic for complicated parapneumonic effusion/empyema or malignant effusion. High protein and LDH make it an exudate.

stem: A 32-year-old woman presents with dyspnoea and right-sided dullness. She has a history of breast cancer treated 3 years ago. CXR shows a large right pleural effusion. Thoracentesis yields bloody fluid. Cytology is negative. What is the next best step to establish the diagnosis?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Malignant effusion — pleural biopsy when cytology is negative
discriminator: Suspected malignant effusion with negative initial cytology → proceed to pleural biopsy (CT-guided or thoracoscopic) for histological confirmation.

stem: A 40-year-old man is brought to the ED after a penetrating chest injury. He has absent breath sounds on the left with hyperresonance and the trachea is deviated to the right. Blood pressure is 80/50 mmHg. A three-sided occlusive dressing has been applied to the wound. After needle decompression at 2nd ICS MCL, his BP improves to 110/70 mmHg. What is the definitive next step?
opts: Insert a chest tube at 4th-5th ICS triangle of safety
CT chest to assess for associated injuries
Observe in the ED for 6 hours
Surgical repair of the chest wall defect
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Post-decompression management — chest tube insertion
discriminator: After initial needle decompression for tension pneumothorax, definitive management is chest tube insertion at 4th-5th ICS. The three-sided dressing managed the open component; needle decompression relieved the tension; now a chest tube is needed for continuous pleural drainage.

stem: A 28-year-old man presents with haemoptysis, progressive dyspnoea, and cola-coloured urine. CXR shows bilateral ground-glass opacities. Urinalysis shows haematuria with RBC casts. Anti-GBM antibody is positive. What is the most likely diagnosis?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Goodpasture syndrome — young adult with haemoptysis + haematuria + anti-GBM + ground-glass CXR
discriminator: Young adult + haemoptysis + haematuria + anti-GBM positive + ground-glass CXR = Goodpasture. Anti-GBM is pathognomonic.

stem: Goodpasture syndrome involves which type of hypersensitivity reaction?
opts: Type II — antibody-mediated against basement membrane
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Goodpasture hypersensitivity type — Type II
discriminator: Goodpasture is the classic Type II hypersensitivity example (antibody against basement membrane). Type III = immune complex (SLE, PSGN, HSP).

stem: A 45-year-old man presents with haemoptysis, haematuria, sinusitis, and nasal ulcers. Laboratory testing shows a positive c-ANCA (PR3). CXR reveals multiple cavitating nodules. What is the most likely diagnosis?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Wegener granulomatosis (GPA) — classic triad lung + kidney + ENT with c-ANCA+
discriminator: ENT involvement (sinusitis, nasal ulcers) + c-ANCA positive + cavitating nodules = Wegener. Microscopic polyangiitis has NO ENT symptoms.

stem: Which antibody is characteristically positive in granulomatosis with polyangiitis (Wegener)?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Wegener (GPA) antibody — c-ANCA against PR3
discriminator: c-ANCA (cytoplasmic ANCA) targeting proteinase-3 (PR3) is the classic antibody for Wegener. p-ANCA targets MPO and is associated with microscopic polyangiitis.

stem: A 50-year-old woman presents with haemoptysis and rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis. She has no sinusitis, nasal ulcers, or any ENT symptoms. p-ANCA (anti-MPO) is positive. CXR shows pulmonary infiltrates without cavitation. What is the most likely diagnosis?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Microscopic polyangiitis — p-ANCA positive, NO ENT involvement
discriminator: p-ANCA + pulmonary-renal + NO ENT = microscopic polyangiitis. The absence of ENT is the key discriminator from Wegener.

stem: Which antibody is characteristically positive in microscopic polyangiitis?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Microscopic polyangiitis antibody — p-ANCA (MPO)
discriminator: p-ANCA targeting myeloperoxidase (MPO) is the antibody associated with microscopic polyangiitis. p stands for perinuclear staining pattern.

stem: A renal biopsy from a patient with rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis shows crescents on light microscopy and linear IgG deposition along the glomerular basement membrane on immunofluorescence. What is the most likely diagnosis?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Renal biopsy immunofluorescence — linear IgG = anti-GBM disease (Goodpasture)
discriminator: Linear IgG along GBM on immunofluorescence is diagnostic of anti-GBM disease (Goodpasture). Pauci-immune (no Ig deposits) is seen in ANCA vasculitis. Granular deposits suggest immune complex disease.

stem: What is the defining histopathological feature of rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis (RPGN) that is common to all pulmonary-renal syndromes?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: RPGN pathology — crescents on renal biopsy
discriminator: Crescents (proliferation of parietal epithelial cells in Bowman space) are the hallmark of RPGN, regardless of the underlying aetiology (anti-GBM, ANCA, or immune complex).

stem: A 22-year-old woman presents with haemoptysis and haematuria. CXR shows diffuse ground-glass opacities. Anti-GBM antibody is positive. Which of the following is a cornerstone of her treatment?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Goodpasture treatment — plasmapheresis is cornerstone
discriminator: Plasmapheresis removes circulating anti-GBM antibodies and is the cornerstone of therapy for Goodpasture syndrome, combined with steroids and cyclophosphamide.

stem: An 8-year-old girl presents with periorbital oedema and cola-coloured urine. She had a sore throat 10 days ago. Urinalysis shows haematuria with RBC casts. C3 complement is low. There is no haemoptysis. What is the most likely diagnosis?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: PSGN vs Goodpasture — child + antecedent infection + low C3 + no haemoptysis
discriminator: Child + sore throat 10 days ago + low C3 + nephritic syndrome + NO haemoptysis = PSGN. Goodpasture has haemoptysis and normal complement.

stem: What is the typical CXR finding in Goodpasture syndrome?
opts: Kerley B lines and pleural effusion
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Goodpasture CXR — bilateral ground-glass opacities from alveolar haemorrhage
discriminator: Ground-glass opacities due to diffuse alveolar haemorrhage are characteristic of Goodpasture. Cavitating nodules = Wegener. Kerley B lines = pulmonary oedema.

stem: A 38-year-old man with granulomatosis with polyangiitis (Wegener) is started on induction therapy. Which of the following is the most appropriate induction regimen?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: ANCA vasculitis induction therapy — steroids + cyclophosphamide/rituximab
discriminator: Induction for ANCA-associated vasculitis (GPA/MPA) is high-dose steroids plus either cyclophosphamide or rituximab. Plasmapheresis is reserved for severe renal involvement.

stem: What is the classic clinical triad of Wegener granulomatosis (GPA)?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Wegener triad — lung + kidney + ENT
discriminator: The triad of lung involvement, renal involvement, and ENT (sinusitis, nasal ulcers, saddle nose) is pathognomonic for Wegener granulomatosis.

stem: A 32-year-old man presents with episodic haemoptysis and progressively declining renal function over 3 weeks. He is a smoker. CXR shows bilateral ground-glass opacities. Anti-GBM antibody is positive. In addition to corticosteroids and cyclophosphamide, what other therapy is indicated?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Goodpasture — anti-GBM positive requires plasmapheresis
discriminator: Anti-GBM positive disease specifically requires plasmapheresis to remove pathogenic antibodies. The stem describes classic Goodpasture with confirmed anti-GBM.

stem: A 55-year-old man with known granulomatosis with polyangiitis (c-ANCA positive) on maintenance therapy presents with worsening renal function. Renal biopsy shows pauci-immune crescentic GN. What does pauci-immune mean?
opts: Linear IgG deposition along the GBM
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Pauci-immune GN — ANCA vasculitis immunofluorescence pattern
discriminator: Pauci-immune refers to the absence or minimal presence of immunoglobulin deposits on immunofluorescence, characteristic of ANCA-associated GN (Wegener and microscopic polyangiitis).

stem: A 30-year-old man presents with haemoptysis and haematuria. He is a heavy smoker. CXR shows bilateral opacities. Anti-GBM is positive. His serum creatinine is 800 µmol/L and he is oliguric. What is the most important intervention to improve renal survival?
subject: Medicine-Respiratory
concept: Goodpasture with severe renal failure — urgent plasmapheresis
discriminator: Anti-GBM disease with severe renal involvement (creatinine > 500, oliguria) requires urgent plasmapheresis to remove antibodies and potentially recover renal function if started before dialysis dependence.
